Breaking: Inkling-2-Mini in 5.4 GB Memory

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 14 min read (2785 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Github

⏱️ ~14 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, lookAtMyQuant is a quantization compiler.
  • On Gemma 4 E2B, its GGUF has 12× lower KL than Q4_K_M at the same file size.
  • Recent findings suggest that lookAtMyQuant 2 takes Qwen3.5-4B to 1.23 GB, 2.3 bits per weight.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, lookAtMyQuant is a quantization compiler. It measures how much each stored piece of a model hurts the output when compressed. It then picks a code for each piece so the whole model fits a size budget with the least damage.

On Gemma 4 E2B, its GGUF has 12× lower KL than Q4_K_M at the same file size. The method and every result are on the site.

The code is under the MIT license.

Recent findings suggest that lookAtMyQuant 2 takes Qwen3.5-4B to 1.23 GB, 2.3 bits per weight. The file solves 330 of 540 exact-answer math problems. Prism ML's Bonsai 2 Ternary 4B solves 328 at 1.20 GB, and the original solves 359. Its KL from the original on held-out text is 0.45 nats, against 0.59 for Bonsai.

The recipe is post-training quantization with trellis codes, calibrated on the model's own worked math solutions with digit tokens weighted 10×, and with bits allocated per row by Fisher information. 4,000 steps of distillation follow, in which every layer is re-quantized once from the original weights. The page has the findings, the full recipe and its cost, about $34 of GPU time.

Sources indicate that the recipe's code is here, and the next section runs it. The 1.23 GB file itself is the lm2-qwen35-4b-1.2gb release, packed for the Apple Silicon runtime.

According to recent reports, the same recipe takes Qwen3.8-27B from 53.7 GB to 7.2 GB, 2.1 bits per weight, calibrated and distilled on English prose and chat, code and math. The file solves 401 of the 540 math problems, as many as the original, and Unsloth's UD-IQ2_XXS GGUF of the same size solves 348. It also scores above that GGUF on HumanEval (73.8% against 67.1%), MMLU (78.8% against 75.0%) and GSM8K (94.5% against 92.7%).

Beside it sits a 4-bit DSpine drafter (1.02 GB, converted from tencent/Qwen3.8-27B-DSpine-b16 with runtime_mlx/convert_dspine.py and packed with pack_drafter.py), which roughly doubles decode speed on math and code on Apple silicon.

Extended to a 26.4B physical / 5.4B active 3×-looped MoE (L6–17 looped 3× = 48 logical visits, 128 experts top-8), the compiler and full-MoE proximal fine-tuning (SQYFR / SQYFR v2 / SQYFR v3) compress thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Mini from 18.89 GB of text weights into six Apple Silicon MLX builds spanning 8 GB iPhones up to lossless teacher parity: 3.85 GB (1.18 bpp), 4.72 GB (1.45 bpp), 5.38 GB (1.65 bpp), 8.87 GB (2.72 bpp), 11.18 GB (3.43 bpp), and 12.76 GB (3.92 bpp) — combining 4 KB SRAM hashed block-vector trellis codes (ht2/ht3), row trellis codes (rtr1/rtr4), surgical 128-row-group Fisher outlier allocation (gu_rg_map/dn_rg_map), dedicated attention projection floors, a tr2 floor on the tail lm_head bucket (head.7), and exact native NVFP4 passthrough (69/192 and 109/192 highest-sensitivity expert buckets kept at 0.0 error in the 11.2 GB and 12.8 GB builds).

Evaluated untruncated (max_new_tokens = 1,536, greedy, reasoning_effort="none") on the same BF16 teacher, openai/gsm8k (test[:200]), all 164 executable openai/openai_humaneval problems (strict <|content_text|> execution across every build), 4 Vision VQA tests (with the untouched 637 MB BF16 vision tower), and 16+13-language TextMix windows:.

Sources indicate that at 12.76 GB, Inkling-2-Mini-LookAtMyQuant-12.8GB matches 100.0% of the untouched BF16 teacher on every benchmark (349 / 349 pooled) in 32.5% less text weight memory. Both 11.18 GB and 8.87 GB retain 99.2–99.3% 3-task mean (345 / 349 = 98.9% pooled), with 8.87 GB cutting KL 2.34× on English/chat/code (0.0208 vs 0.0486) and 29.6% across all 13 languages (0.0571 vs 0.0811) below Unsloth's 9.14 GB UD-Q2_K_XL GGUF. Below 2 bpp, SQYFR v2 lifts 5.38 GB (1.65 bpp) to 90.0% top-1 agreement (free_KL = 0.0864), 87.0% GSM8K, and 71.3% strict HumanEval (117 / 164), while SQYFR v3 (combining two-pass on-policy student-prefix DAgger distillation, surgical within-stage 128-row-group Fisher outlier splitting, and 950 exact-P polish steps over 14.15M row scales + 440K–452K float16 pre-RHT input-column scales + 38.8M native steering) lifts 4.72 GB (1.45 bpp, sized to fit under the 12 GB iPhone 5.99 GiB Jetsam ceiling alongside the 179 MB drafter at 4.35 GiB active / 5.35 GiB decode peak) to 94.0% GSM8K (188 / 200, 97.4% of the BF16 teacher) and 68.9% strict HumanEval (113 / 164, 90.6% 3-task mean), and lifts 3.85 GB (1.18 bpp, 3.54 GiB active / 4.57 GiB decode peak for 8 GB devices) from static PTQ collapse (1.0% GSM8K, 1.8% HumanEval) to 89.5% GSM8K (179 / 200), 59.1% strict HumanEval (97 / 164), and 4 / 4 Vision (85.5% 3-task mean).

All six run through lamq and runtime_mlx via unified single-launch Metal kernels (UnifiedMoESide mixing unrotated NVFP4 and Hadamard-rotated per-expert or 128-row-group trellis experts across decode, speculative verify, and M5 MetalPerformancePrimitives prefill + FlashAttention-2 SDPA + exact unbiased temp > 0 speculative sampling), optionally paired with the 178.9 MB 4-bit DSpark drafters: on Apple M5 Max, 12.8 GB reaches 2,016 tok/s T=512 prefill, 60.5 tok/s serial, and 112.7 tok/s median lossless drafted decode (119.2 tok/s math, 106.2 tok/s code; 12.72 GB active RAM); 11.2 GB reaches 2,032 tok/s prefill, 62.4 tok/s serial, and 103.7 tok/s median (111.7 tok/s math; 11.13 GB active RAM); 8.9 GB decodes at 63.5 tok/s serial and 106.0 tok/s median (125.8 tok/s reasoning, 123.8 tok/s math; 9.41 GB active RAM); 5.4 GB reaches 1,807 tok/s prefill, 75.3 tok/s serial, and 124.4 tok/s median (142.9 tok/s math, 126.5 tok/s reasoning; 5.33 GB active RAM); 4.7 GB decodes at 69.2 tok/s serial and up to 129.0 tok/s on math (3.25 tok/check, 94.7 tok/s code; 4.67 GB active RAM); and 3.9 GB decodes at 75.8 tok/s serial and 113.0 tok/s median (117.3 tok/s math, 108.5 tok/s code; 3.81 GB active RAM).

On Apple silicon, install the runtime package directly (this installs mlx, mlx-lm, numpy, and huggingface-hub without the PyTorch compiler dependencies):.

It has been revealed that from a local clone, pip install -e . installs the lamq command, or run python -m runtime_mlx without installing.

Command line. Pass either a local model folder or a Hugging Face repo ID:.

lamq generate reads stdin when -p is omitted, supports --raw, --system, --thinking, --temp, --mode linear|chat-fork|copy-wide, --no-adaptive, and --json. lamq info inspects a packed model's format and dimensions without loading weights.

It has been revealed that python integration. runtime_mlx.load returns an (model, tokenizer) pair compatible with mlx_lm.generate and mlx_lm.stream_generate (auto-detecting opgraph-packed-1 models such as Qwen3.5-4B / Qwen3.8-27B, inkling2-packed models such as Inkling-2-Mini, and lamq.json exports such as Gemma 4 E2B):.

For streaming, multi-turn chat, or speculative decoding through one interface, use Runtime:.

According to recent reports, openAI-compatible server. lamq serve puts a packed Inkling-2-Mini model behind /v1/chat/completions, streaming or not, so chat clients and coding agents can use it. Requests go through the model's own chat template, including tools and reasoning_effort; thinking comes back as reasoning_content and tool invocations as tool_calls.

When a request lists tools, "tool_choice": "auto" lets the model choose whether to call one. This is the default. Set "tool_choice": "none" to disable calls for that turn. Requests that require a call or force a particular function receive HTTP 400.

It has been revealed that --context (default 32768) caps prompt plus completion. A longer prompt gets llama.cpp's "exceeds the available context size" error, which agent clients take as a cue to compact. Requests have a 1 MiB JSON limit and receive HTTP 503 if the model is busy. The server binds to 127.0.0.1 by default and rejects requests with a browser Origin header. Set LAMQ_API_KEY to require Authorization: Bearer on every endpoint. Other bind addresses require a key. Use a TLS-terminating proxy for connections over an untrusted network.

For a trusted single-user MLX loopback server, --prompt-cache N keeps up to N prefilled KV snapshots (0 by default). An extension to an earlier prompt reuses its matching snapshot, and an identical retry prefills one token. The server disables reuse when requiring a bearer key or binding to a network address. In Python, pass prompt_cache=PromptCache() from runtime_mlx.inkling to stream_dspark or stream_serial.

Use POST /apply-template to render a chat prompt or POST /tokenize with a content string to return token IDs.

It has been revealed that inkling prefill uses one pass when the prompt fits the estimated MLX memory budget and chunks long prompts under memory pressure. Set --prefill-chunk N in lamq generate, lamq chat, or lamq serve to choose a chunk size, or set it to 0 for one pass.

The optimized MLX runtime stores the attention cache in FP16 by default. Set LAMQ_GLOBAL_KV=fp8 or LAMQ_GLOBAL_KV=q4 to reduce global attention cache memory on long prompts. Both options can change generated tokens. Sliding-window attention keeps its FP16 cache.

Install the CUDA extra on a machine with a supported NVIDIA GPU. The public model ID and chat template are shared with the Apple Silicon runtime.

According to recent reports, triton handles ordinary generation and NVFP4 experts. The native CUDA engine supports DSpark on trellis packs. See the CUDA runtime for model support, revision selection, and benchmark commands.

It has been revealed that install the dependencies and download the model and WikiText-2. The code reads SmolLM2-360M's config when it starts, so do this first.

Measure. This compresses one piece at a time, leaves the rest exact, and records the KL to the original model. The full set for this model, 2,312 measurements, took about 50 minutes on an L40S.

Recent findings suggest that allocate. This picks one code per piece, with the least summed KL inside the budget. It needs no GPU. This command uses the SmolLM2-360M measurements in this repository, with a budget of 3.044 bits per weight.

The plan it writes has the same widths as results/compiler/plans/sm_lin_3044.json.

In a recent development, build and score. This quantizes the model to the blueprint, one matrix at a time. It then reports perplexity and KL to the original on WikiText-2 test.

Our run of that plan is in results/batch/cc_sm_lin_3044.json. It reached perplexity 16.64 and KL 0.0926, against an original perplexity of 15.31. Add --layers 1 --calib 8 --eval 2 for a quick check that everything works.

Industry observers note that each step is a named job; python run_batch.py --list prints its command. The jobs need Qwen3.5-4B in models/Qwen3.5-4B on the volume and the text mix (modal run --detach modal_fetch.py --text). Every file they make goes to lm2/ on the volume.

lm2BuildSmoke, lm2FinetuneSmoke and lm2MathSmoke run the same code on two layers, 60 steps and 36 problems, in a few minutes each.

The row blueprint. lm2Build reads results/compiler/rows/q35_rowplan_1p2GB.json, which gives 1 to 4 bits to each of 1,520 row groups. row_allocation.py made it. Its build-control command builds and packs a control with a fixed split of rows, prepare-rows allocates rows inside the control's packed bytes with rowgroup_alloc.py, and build-rows builds under the plan and checks the packed size against it.

Sources indicate that the codebooks. The four e-means codebooks the build decodes with are in cache/codes/. --trellis-fit lloyd gives the earlier ones, and a proposal made before the change keeps them unless the flag claims otherwise.

Recent equal-byte recipe improvements. Two zero-byte additions are available in the compiler and fine-tuning scripts:.

According to recent reports, where these jobs differ from our run. Our GSM8K solutions were written earlier, with thinking always off. Our text KL on 13 sources used 52 windows picked from the text mix by a separate tool; --sources mix takes the mix's own evaluation windows, on which our file scores 0.44 where the page reports 0.45.

Industry observers note that run_batch.py names every job, and modal_app.py runs them. modal_fetch.py downloads models and the text mix used for calibration and evaluation.

The runs behind the site used these machines, each with 8 CPU cores:.

Industry observers note that gguf_compiler.py makes plans out of llama.cpp's own tensor types, so the result runs in llama.cpp as it is. public_eval.py scores public quantizations the same way as our plans. Both run inside the image in modal_gguf.py, which builds llama.cpp with CUDA.

It has been revealed that quantize.py --export writes a plan in the format runtime_mlx/ reads. A plan with trellis codes also needs --trellis-rows 16,8, which runs each trellis path along a row of its matrix, so that decoding an entry reads only that row. On Apple silicon, pip install . installs mlx and mlx-lm; requirements.txt holds the PyTorch compiler dependencies.

Industry observers note that on Gemma 4 E2B at 2.5 GB, the trellis plan has 26% lower KL than the Lloyd–Max plan and decodes about 22% slower. runtime_mlx/test_trellis_gen.py and runtime_mlx/test_trellis.py check the trellis kernels against the matrices the quantizer built.

runtime_mlx/fast_q35.py decodes the packed 1.2 GB Qwen3.5-4B file one token at a time, straight from its trellis codes. runtime_mlx/drafter_q35.py adds speculative decoding. A small drafter proposes the seven tokens after the model's latest one in a single pass. The model then checks all eight positions in one pass over its coded weights (runtime_mlx/block_q35.py) and keeps the proposals that match its own choice, so the text is exactly its own greedy text.

On an M5 Max, over 30 held-out prompts of up to 256 tokens, generation with the drafter was 2.0 times as fast: 176 tokens a second against 88, timed in alternation in one process on 2026-11-11. A check kept 4.3 tokens on average. Over eight everyday prompts it was 1.5 times as fast. The gain follows how predictable the text is: 2.5 times on algebra, 2.0 on code, 1.2 on chat and 1.05 on a story, and one of the 30 held-out prompts ran slower with the drafter. The text matched plain greedy decoding on every prompt. These are speeds after the first token; reading the prompt takes about 0.1 s either way.

Two later changes are in this code. Each was measured against the version before it on 40 paired generations: proposing from the 96,033 most common tokens was 6.0% faster, and picking the winning token inside the packed product was 5.3% faster. Linear mode also enables self-calibrating adaptive fallback by default (adaptive=True; pass --no-adaptive to disable): when rolling acceptance drops below the measured break-even ratio of drafted-check latency to serial-step latency (accounting for cache flush and drafter context replay), it pauses drafting for short exact serial bursts and resumes once acceptance recovers, preserving bit-exact greedy parity while avoiding slowdowns on low-acceptance prose.

Industry observers note that the drafter is a DSpine model, trained with SpecForge from the published DFlash drafter for Qwen3.5-4B on the 1.2 GB file's own greedy answers. modal_drafter.py runs the training as one Modal job, and it cost $42. On 300 held-out prompts the trained drafter gets 4.65 tokens per check, against 4.30 for the stock DFlash drafter.

Sources indicate that pack_drafter.py stores the drafter at 4 bits a weight in the build's own code, with no calibration data: 464 MB against 1.83 GB at 16 bits. On 60 held-out prompts the 4-bit drafter kept 4.35 tokens per check against 4.38, and the text was the same. drafter_q35.py loads either form and writes the packed one out dense as it loads. The 4-bit drafter is the lm2-drafter-4bit release. It runs beside the packed 1.2 GB file, the lm2-qwen35-4b-1.2gb release.

The benchmark defaults to linear verification. Use --mode chat-fork to try a second candidate at an ambiguous early position, or --mode copy-wide for known contiguous copies. Copy mode uses the source cursor and tunes the gate/up and down projections for 16-slot checks. Both modes verify all emitted tokens with the packed target. To benchmark the chat fork, run:.

Sources indicate that for a copy benchmark, pass --mode copy-wide --heldout path/to/copy-prompts.json. The JSON entries carry source, prompt_len, and input_ids from the packed model's tokenizer.

The checks, and the packer for a drafter of your own:.

runtime_mlx/pack_dense.py writes the packed file from the fine-tuned build's dense weights, and runtime_mlx/modal_pack.py runs it on Modal. check_drafter.py compares the drafter in MLX with SpecForge's own model on reference blocks that drafter/reference.py writes.

Each test file runs on its own from the repository root, and all seven finish in under a minute.

Sources indicate that runtime_mlx/test_core.py checks the runtime against the quantizer's math. Run python runtime_mlx/make_ref.py first, which writes 1.6 GB of reference files.

Sources indicate that runtime_mlx/test_fast_q35.py and runtime_mlx/test_block_q35.py check the Qwen3.5 kernels against NumPy products of independently unpacked codes, with no model. When LAMQ_Q35_PACKED names a packed file, the second also checks a block of tokens against decoding them one at a time. When LAMQ_Q38_PACKED names the packed Qwen3.8-27B file, it runs the same checks on a model whose output head is stored apart from its embedding.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, “I write behind the wheel of the van,” Jason Scott, leader of the namesake band Jason Scott and the High Heat, says.
  • Bassist Ryan Magnani, however, calls bullshit: The van is just one of the places that Scott, a prolific Oklahoma writer, is able to come up with material.
  • In a recent development, jason Scott and the High Heat released their latest album Play Boy back in September, marking their second record on the Leo33 label and their second in just over a year, following the March 2025 drop of American Grin.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, “I write behind the wheel of the van,” Jason Scott, leader of the namesake band Jason Scott and the High Heat, says. “There’s no other time.”.

Bassist Ryan Magnani, however, calls bullshit: The van is just one of the places that Scott, a prolific Oklahoma writer, is able to come up with material. “Just the other day, you came off of a drive and you stated, ‘I think I just wrote a cool song.’ And I am looking around like, ‘Where did you write a song? You don’t have a guitar,’” Magnani states. ‘You said, ‘Nah, I was just thinking about it.’”.

In a recent development, jason Scott and the High Heat released their latest album Play Boy back in September, marking their second record on the Leo33 label and their second in just over a year, following the March 2025 drop of American Grin. Scott has spent the better part of a decade writing songs shaped by his Pentecostal upbringing and the personal and artistic awakenings he had after pursuing music full-time, but Play Boy goes hard in a different direction. It’s best described as “Jason Scott, unfiltered,” a collection of songs written on whims.

“It has no inherent meaning, and it did not come from anywhere,” Scott claims, “other than, ‘That’s all we be doin’ out here.’”.

With Scott on guitar and vocals and Magnani on bass, the High Heat features Gabriel Mor on guitar, Garrison Brown on guitar and keys, and Tremaine “Bobby” Wade on drums. Taylor Johnson, a one-time member, is the band’s producer. On this particular afternoon, they are gathered around a table at an Irish pub on Manhattan’s Upper West Side, coming in hot from a European run and gearing up for a CBS Saturday Morning taping the next day. Together, the High Heat are a group of misfits from Oklahoma capable of being sincere in one moment, and irreverent in the next.

Sources indicate that the group skewed toward the latter when they introduced Play Boy to the world in early summer by releasing the twangy “Shit Show” and its accompanying video. Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century.

If the song plays out as something of a parody of A-list entertainers (“Come and get it, either pass that shit or hit it/They is until they isn’t, honey that’s the biz,” is the song’s hook), the video is a fever dream. Brett Loudermilk and Zain Curtis of Paperboy Studios, best-known for Ke$ha’s NSFW “Boy Crazy” video, oversaw the production, which opens with the band in a living room, nursing severe hangovers, before a parade of increasingly-absurd characters wanders in. Midway through, the room becomes the site of a burlesque show. Wade is walked on a leash by a dominatrix.

The band says the shoot itself followed the theme in the video, of starting out tame and building to chaos, as the day went on. “They didn’t tell us what they were gonna do. They just kept surprising us,” Mor says. “They’d say, ‘We’ve got a woman, and she’s gonna walk Bob like a dog.’ Every scene was like, ‘We have no idea what’s gonna happen.’”.

The album cover features a pregnant woman modeling lingerie and holding a cigarette in front of a dressing room mirror, with a table littered with half-drank cups of liquor nearby.

Sources indicate that “That was Grace, and it was the first time we had met her,” Scott states. “She did such an incredible job on the shoot, and we ended up with all these cool photos of her. One just worked out to be our artwork. She has had baby June since then.”.

Industry observers note that since “Shit Show,” the High Heat have gotten even more conceptual with their music videos.” The latest, “How to Get Away With Murder,” pokes deadly fun at dating in the digital age. It’s cinematic, haunting, and very bloody. Industry observers note that making such adventurous, boundary-pushing videos is only adding to the respect they have already earned from their peers, and Scott and his bandmates wield influence across Americana music. Mor has served as the stylist for Flatland Cavalry. Magnani has directed videos for Wyatt Flores. Scott himself played the lead character in Jason Isbell’s “King of Oklahoma” video.

In a recent development, so, when it came time to record Play Boy, the High Heat found plenty of willing collaborators. “Shit Show” alone featured background vocals by Ken Pomeroy — recently named Emerging Artist of the Year at the Americana Honors & Awards — and keys by fellow Oklahoman John Fullbright. Rod Elkins, drummer for Tyler Childers and the Food Stamps, played on the track.

“We just ask the cool people that we know,” Brown notes of the guest appearances.

In a recent development, even before Play Boy, the High Heat were edging closer to being the cool people that other artists know. Their schedule includes high-profile festival stops at January’s Mile 0 Fest and their Stagecoach debut next spring in Indio, California. They’re also working on aims for their annual Loser’s Ball concert, slated for the holiday season in Oklahoma City. Their live show, much like their album interview in a New York pub, is loose and aimed at giving fans the chance to leave the show with a memory. “Jason is always talking about ‘making moments’ in a setlist. Whenever those moments happen, we need to go fully into it,” Brown notes, “because it forces everybody to pay attention.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As many SAG-AFTRA members struggle to qualify for health insurance, the union is taking the concern to the U.S. government.

On Friday, Screen Actors Guild President Sean Astin announced the President’s Healthcare Task Force to address the “broken healthcare system” while several actors have faced losing their insurance under the union’s minimum eligibility requirements.

According to recent reports, “This is a critical moment, where both our members and the public at large can no longer wait for relief from a broken healthcare system,” he mentioned in a statement. “Our SAG-AFTRA Health Strategy is healthy and strong, but a substantial majority of our members do not qualify. For our members who don’t qualify, there is very little that can be done to provide coverage.”.

Astin added, “SAG-AFTRA has supported efforts to expand healthcare for all through the AFL-CIO. This task force seeks a new level of participation in the national movement to expand care for everyone. We will actively engage with policymakers, gather allies and provide a structured way for our members to participate formally in the process. The President’s Healthcare Task Force will be an instrument of support in the movement for universal healthcare.” Watch on Deadline.

The SAG-AFTRA National Board voted unanimously on Friday to form the Task Force, which seeks to mobilize SAG-AFTRA’s collective strength and public influence to fight for universal access to affordable, comprehensive and reliable health care.

SAG’s new initiative comes amid financial scrutiny for the union following National Executive Director Duncan Crabtree-Ireland’s recent contract renewal, after his salary surpassed $1M in 2023.

‘Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album’ Is All Over the Place (in a Good Way)

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The 13-years-in-the-making Grand Theft Auto VI has been hailed for its of-the-moment touches, but it does have one quaintly anachronistic aspect: Nobody reaches for the aux. The game’s in-universe radio stations provide the soundtrack to its criminal and romantic endeavors, with drivers eschewing streaming and flipping the dial until they find their favorites. Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album, appropriately, feels like a frantic flip through a dial so wide, it can even fit a still-trucking smooth jazz station.

Sources indicate that opening track “Starting From Zero,” a collaboration between the aggro-electro duo Justice (who composed the game’s score) and soul crooner Michael McDonald, transports the listener to the sublime, the combination of thudding synths and McDonald’s immediately identifiable voice throwing back to the days of hits being launched from buddy-cop movies and Miami Vice. It’s pastiche, sure, but it’s pastiche done well, and it bookends nicely with the album’s closing cut. “Overtown Lights,” a collaboration between Return to Forever bassist Stanley Clarke, pianist and bandleader Robert Glasper, and drummer Yussef Dayes, evokes a carefree late-night drive over streets slicked with rain and illuminated by reflected headlights.

If Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album were just a collection of homages to the good-ish old days of neon t-shirts paired with blazers, it would probably be a solid listen, as evidenced by the genre-splicing Justice-SZA-King Gizzard-Tame Impala team-up “Flower In A Hurricane” and the training-montage-ready Dua Lipa cut “Go Easy.” But this collection is more than that — similar to the game, whose intricate details firmly place it in a heightened version of the present, it’s a wide-ranging representation of popular music’s current moment. “That’s It,” the collaboration between Swedish MC Yung Lean, Atlanta kingpin Future, and superproducer Metro Boomin, follows the Justice/McDonald collab, and even though it opens with icy synths that feel connected to the previous track, the fluttering trap snares and bone-rattling bass, as well as Lean’s anxiety-ridden lyrics, jolt the milieu back to 2026. Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century.

Sources indicate that hip-hop’s 21st-century vanguard is well-represented on GTAVI:TA, with rap enigma Travis Scott’s spaced-out “RHYNO” — produced by Daft Punk’s Guy-Manuel de Homem-Christo — and the frantic Kodak Black/Don Toliver collaboration “Let’s Rock” heading a pack that also includes Playboi Carti, Cardi B, and Young Thug. Music from pop’s Spanish-speaking diaspora is also in ample supply; regional Mexican stars Fuerza Regida’s thumping “Suzuki” is a throwdown, and “Largate,” the collaboration between singer-songwriter Helado Negro and dreampop romantic Kali Uchis, is one of the album’s true highlights, the singers ruminating on a breakup in the midst of a haze conjured by strummed guitars. Trending Stories Patrick Stewart Cause of Death Revealed Miley Cyrus and Maxx Morando Marry at Palm Springs Wedding Princess of Wales Reflects on Cancer Battle in 'Heal' Documentary Special Boy George on His Israel Trip: 'I Wasn't Able to Not Say Something'.

GTAVI:TA’s pop universe operates on hyperspeed, with BLACKPINK’s JENNIE’s voice welding itself to the robot-rocking synths of “Power Trip,”  Zara Larsson paying homage to her fellow Swedes Ace Of Base on the sinuous “Fast Emotion,” and Camila Cabello finding a middle ground between her full-speed-ahead c, xoxo era and her more mellow cuts like “Havana.” (Not having a Latin freestyle-nodding selection accompany a game that’s so Floridian seems wrong, but there’s always GTAVII.).

In a recent development, A couple of tracks hold their own, genre-wise: Irascible Nashville star Morgan Wallen’s “Last Thing You Need” rides in on a candy-coated guitar riff and splits the difference between the Urban Cowboy era and the present moment; Keith Richards lays down a faithful version of Jimmy Reed’s Chicago blues classic “Bright Lights, Big City”; and The Time’s Jesse Johnson teams up with torch-carrying producer Dam-Funk for “Stone Kold Krazy Luuv,” a slow jam that brings together sparkling synths, flinty riffing, and a thick bassline. These songs not only feel like the results of serendipitous dial spins; along with the rest of GTAVI:TA, they nod to the parent album’s status as one of monoculture’s last blockbusters.

Latest Update: How to clear slippery moss and green algae from patio pavers — without blasting out the sand

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (660 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tomsguide

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that damp, shady weather turns even the best-kept patio into a slippery green mess, and reaching for a pressure washer is not always the smartest fix.
  • Fortunately, you do not need heavy machinery to get your patio looking clean and safe underfoot again.
  • Recent findings suggest that while a power washer strips surface grime in minutes, it only removes the visible top layer of moss and algae, leaving microscopic spores behind in the pores of the stone.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that damp, shady weather turns even the best-kept patio into a slippery green mess, and reaching for a pressure washer is not always the smartest fix. High-pressure jets can blast jointing sand straight out from between your pavers, pit soft natural stone, and leave behind micro-scratches where moss and algae grow back even faster.

Fortunately, you do not need heavy machinery to get your patio looking clean and safe underfoot again. A stiff broom, a watering can, and a few simple household staples or outdoor treatments are all it takes to lift stubborn green growth without damaging your stonework.

Recent findings suggest that while a power washer strips surface grime in minutes, it only removes the visible top layer of moss and algae, leaving microscopic spores behind in the pores of the stone. Worse still, blasting delicate limestone, sandstone, or older mortar joints with high-pressure water erodes the surface and loosens the pavers themselves.

Gentle cleaning methods work differently. Instead of relying on brute force, they break down the organic growth at the root so you can brush or rinse it away cleanly, keeping both your stone surface and the sand between your pavers intact.

Before applying any cleaner, move patio furniture out of the way, sweep away loose leaves with a stiff broom (avoid metal rakes, which can scratch pavers), and lightly water any nearby lawn or flowerbeds so plants do not absorb soapy or acidic runoff.

Once prepped, choose the method that best suits your patio material:.

If you have delicate natural stone like limestone or sandstone, or simply want the gentlest fix, start with a bucket of warm water and a few generous squeezes of dish soap.

Pour the sudsy mixture over the pavers, let it sit for 15 minutes to loosen the grime, and scrub diagonally across the joints with a stiff outdoor brush so you do not dislodge the sand. Rinse thoroughly with a garden hose.

For heavier green buildup on concrete or brick pavers, wet the patio down first, scatter washing soda crystals (sodium carbonate) across the affected areas, and add a small drizzle of dish soap.

Work the paste into the pavers with a stiff brush, then leave it to sit for 24 to 48 hours before hosing it away. Always wear gloves when handling soda crystals, and keep pets off the patio until it is rinsed clean.

Skip this method on natural stone: because vinegar is acidic, it can etch and discolor limestone, sandstone, or travertine.

Mix equal parts white vinegar and water in a watering can or garden sprayer, saturate the mossy patches, and leave the solution to soak for 20 to 30 minutes before scrubbing with a stiff brush and rinsing well.

In a recent development, if you are tackling a large patio or stubborn black-spot lichen, an oxygen- or enzyme-based outdoor paver cleaner saves hours of scrubbing. Apply the solution with a watering can on a dry day, leave it to break down the spores over a few days, and let the next rainfall wash the dead growth away naturally.

Breaking: Apple fires back at Epic over claims it withheld 122,000 documents

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (821 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Apple has responded to Epic Games’ filing from last Friday, pushing back against accusations that it improperly withheld more than 122,000 documents related to its proposed App Store commissions.
  • While the Supreme Court is set to review whether the civil contempt designation against Apple should be upheld in its lawsuit against Epic Games, the two companies have also been battling in the district court over what commission, if any, Apple should be allowed to charge on purchases made through external payment systems.
  • Apple submitted its proposal to the district court on August 13, calling for commissions ranging from 5% to 15%, but Epic is disputing not just the basis for those proposed rates, but also Apple’s handling of document production in the proceedings.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple has responded to Epic Games’ filing from last Friday, pushing back against accusations that it improperly withheld more than 122,000 documents related to its proposed App Store commissions. Here are the details.

While the Supreme Court is set to review whether the civil contempt designation against Apple should be upheld in its lawsuit against Epic Games, the two companies have also been battling in the district court over what commission, if any, Apple should be allowed to charge on purchases made through external payment systems.

Apple submitted its proposal to the district court on August 13, calling for commissions ranging from 5% to 15%, but Epic is disputing not just the basis for those proposed rates, but also Apple’s handling of document production in the proceedings.

As part of the proceedings, Epic had submitted 16 categories of documents it wanted Apple to produce (including “internal analyses of the financial or business impact” of its proposed commissions and “communications relating to any strategies to dissuade developers from offering link-outs”), along with a list of current and former Apple employees whose records should be searched.

Apple agreed to use Epic’s proposed search terms and include all employees, and began producing documents it determined were responsive to Epic’s requests.

Epic, however, said last Friday that Apple was improperly withholding more than 122,000 documents matching those search terms from the records of the seven initial employees, and asked the court to order Apple to produce all matching non-privileged documents, regardless of its relevance assessments.

Which brings us to Apple’s newest filing.

In its filing, Apple argues that contrary to Epic’s claim that its proposed search terms were “tailored” to the proceedings over link-out fees, they were actually “overbroad,” capturing large numbers of unrelated documents.

For instance, Apple notes that while intended to identify documents related to its proposed commission rates, Epic’s “commission*” search term also “captures documents that refer to government and private commissions, as well as documents hitting on the totally irrelevant term ‘commissioner,’ such as documents discussing the NFL Commissioner.”.

“[…] the use of a wildcard in a search string is designated by the asterisk symbol, which means that the search string will hit on any term that includes the prefix before the asterisk.

In the same vein, Apple notes that “Epic’s use of ‘fee*’ in its search strings related to litigation and Apple’s link-out-related projects pulled in documents containing words like ‘feel,’ ‘feed,’ ‘feedback,’ ‘feet,’ and ‘feeble’ without the word ‘fee’ or ‘fees’ appearing at all.”.

Apple’s overall argument is that these unrelated matches account for the vast majority of documents identified by Epic’s searches, and it cites legal precedent to argue that it should only be required to produce documents responsive to Epic’s requests, rather than every document matching the agreed-upon search terms:.

In fact, at least 95% of the Initial Custodian Document Population hit on generic terms like these and did not include any reference to the term “link-out” or its variations, despite that concept being central to the Proffer and related discovery. These sweeping terms do not just increase the total volume of the Initial Custodian Document Population, they also captured highly sensitive and irrelevant documents, such as Apple employees’ personal tax or financial records, medical records, documents discussing unannounced products, documents containing passwords, investor-relations materials, and privileged or protected legal communications.

Recent findings suggest that the law is clear: parties are only required to produce responsive documents, not every document returned by a search string. […] (“The Court will not compel defendants to produce any document simply because it contains a search term whether or not it is responsive to the discovery request.”). Epic has not shown, and cannot show, why the regular discovery process should be disrupted here. Speculation based on hit counts, particularly where the producing party can explain low responsiveness rates, does not justify the extraordinary and unprecedented remedy Epic seeks.

Apple goes on to argue that complying with Epic’s demands would require extensive additional work, including reviewing documents for privileged or sensitive information and redacting protected material, making it impossible to meet Epic’s proposed December 2 deadline.

Finally, Apple asks the court to reject Epic’s motion but proposes that, should the court decide that some intervention is warranted, a randomized, statistically significant sample of the documents it deems nonresponsive be submitted to a Special Master for independent review, rather than producing all of them to Epic directly.

  • The Jennifer Tiexiera-directed film, produced by Brad Pitt’s Plan B Entertainment, features footage from Dudamel and the LA Phil’s pair of performances at 2025’s Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival, where they made history as the first major orchestra to perform a full set at the massive event.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, I n December, Gustavo Dudamel will make his much-anticipated return to conduct the Los Angeles Philharmonic for a string of dates. It’s the first time he will head back to his former home of nearly 20 years since beginning his tenure as the Newly introduced York Philharmonic’s Music and Artistic Director. Given the multiple standing ovations and chants of “Gustavo” that resonated through the Hollywood Bowl during his final LA Phil bow in late August, his arrival will be a much welcome one.

Recent findings suggest that alongside his trip back to the West Coast, Rolling Stone can exclusively announce a documentary about Dudamel and the LA Phil will premiere on Dec. 7 coinciding with his concerts at Walt Disney Hall on Dec. 4, 5, and 6. The documentary, titled Symphony of a Thousand, is described as “Set during challenging times in L.A., the film encapsulates Dudamel’s philosophy on how music can create connection and community in an increasingly fractured world.”.

The Jennifer Tiexiera-directed film, produced by Brad Pitt’s Plan B Entertainment, features footage from Dudamel and the LA Phil’s pair of performances at 2025’s Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival, where they made history as the first major orchestra to perform a full set at the massive event. It features Dave Grohl,  LL Cool J, Cynthia Erivo, Natasha Bedingfield, Becky G, CA7RIEL & Paco Amoroso, and Zedd. Kevin Macdonald serves as the executive producer, with producers Jeremy Kleiner, Dede Gardner, and Chloe Mamelok.

It has been revealed that landmark pop culture moments like this have peppered the course of Dudamel’s trailblazing career. And he wasn’t about to go (east) quietly. His final nights helming the LA Phil culminated in a weekend at the Bowl that featured the Foo Fighters and other pop luminaries, concerts that doubled as a benefit for his home country of Venezuela. A conversation at the Grammy Museum followed.

Recent findings suggest that “I met Gustavo at a party about 12 years ago, and I fell in love with him. As a heterosexual man, it confused me,” Coldplay’s Chris Martin affectionately jokes when joining Dudamel and LA Phil onstage during the benefit concert for Venezuela finale. “And I realized it wasn’t so much sexual as musical in the way I just wanted to cuddle him forever. And we’ve been musically cuddling ever since.” Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century.

Sources indicate that trailing Dudamel during his final full-time week in L.A., that sentiment carries through to every interaction. At the closed final rehearsal on a Sunday morning in August, camera crews swirl around as two women busily work to notate the score, and a handful of onlookers from the team at the Bowl gather to take in the moment in the blazing heat. There’s a hushed reverence knowing an era is coming to an end, but also smiles abound, particularly from Dudamel who warmly hugs old friends as they join him onstage.

It has been revealed that as he conducts, he throws the full weight of his body in a stance both graceful and animated — like a kid at his first dance. His baton alights in the air and comes down, and the orchestra responds, while he swoops and sways to the music. “5/4 pum pum,” Dudamel instructs as they run through one composition. Later, Meme del Real from Café Tacvba takes the stage to rehearse the poignant “Eras.” Lasso follows with an a cappella of “En Otra Vida.”.

In a recent development, it’s the morning after their phenomenal performance with Foo Fighters, which marked the band’s first-ever set at the Hollywood Bowl. That pairing is not an unusual one for Dudamel, though. He’s made a name for himself breaking down perceived traditional genre boundaries in his 17 years at the Bowl, where he’s collaborated with an array of artists, including LL Cool J, Christina Aguilera, and Beck, who later at the finale concert performs “Ride Lonesome.” Beck’s dad, celebrated arranger-composer David Campbell, also attends the final rehearsal. It has been revealed that “If I reflect about how I feel, yes, I feel exhausted,” Dudamel tells Rolling Stone with a smile when we meet at the Grammy Museum a couple of days later. “Every day a rehearsal, every day a concert. Next day a different program, another concert.” It’s been a nonstop whirlwind, but it’s also been a time “full of beauty,” he claims.

It has been revealed that “I have the chance to dive inside of all of that amount of talent — because it’s not only the soloists that play with me; it’s all that orchestra, that 100 musicians that are there, that I have shared 17 years of my life with them, and of course it doesn’t finish,” he continues. “This goes to eternity because when you develop something that is so deep and so powerful as developing an identity through music, it’s the biggest privilege … Every single note, every single second that I have the chance to share, or people share with me, that is a privilege to have the chance to work with all of these people and to create all of this environment.”.

In a recent development, if there are a couple of overarching words to describe Dudamel, they would be magnetic charm. When we arrive at the Grammy Museum a few hours before his event, several people rush him to ask for selfies, to which he happily obliges before he’s promptly ushered into the building. People from the music world and beyond appear drawn to him, not only for the music he helms and the open environment he’s created around it, but also for his altruism.

At intermission during Dudamel’s Hollywood Bowl finale, Coldplay’s Martin heads backstage to rehearse with YOLA, the youth orchestra inspired by Dudamel’s own experience coming up in El Sistema, the publicly-funded National Network of Youth and Children Orchestras of Venezuela. (It was there while discovering music technique that “I saw the immense and infinite possibilities of all kinds of music,” Dudamel states.) Martin asks each child their name before leading them through a warm-up and taking to the piano. He vamps his lyrics to “Viva La Vida” before the choir comes in with the buoyant Oh-oh-oh bridge. “Absolutely fantastic,” Martin tells the students. He reminds them: “Remember when we’re out there onstage, this is our band … We’re doing this together.” Later onstage, they deliver their spine-tingly performance, which prompts a crowd-wide sing-along.

Recent findings suggest that YOLA, which provides free instruments and education to create social change through music, is a vital part of Dudamel’s legacy and his north star. “I grew up not in an environment of conservatory, rigid. No,” he indicates. “It was music as a tool of social transformation — that is El Sistema. And of course, for me, opening spaces for young people to have access to music as a tool for them to have beauty, to have creativity, to have empathy, creating together — that is for me the most important thing. And [as] artistic institutions, we have to do that … for people to see the transforming power of music.

“When you have this chance to transform your life, creating harmony, creating beauty together — when you go out as a citizen, you behave differently because you see the real dimension of connection that goes beyond any material thing, any ideological point of view, and then you are connected through the empathy of human being and doing things beautiful for others.”.

As for his hopes to bring a similar program to Upcoming York and beyond, he believes it’s imperative. “We don’t have the chance in this world to contemplate, to really see each other, to create something that requires discipline, but at the same time joy together. When you are doing music, in an orchestra, in a choir, and you feel that first moment that you create harmony and that you are part of something beautiful and powerful, that enhances your spirit. I think that is the way for our kids to be inspired, especially in the chaotic but beautiful, in the only world that we have. So we have to create more spaces like this.”.

As a longtime champion of crossover collaborations, Dudamel attracts artists across genres and disciplines, but a recent team-up came by way of an unusual source, via actor Bradley Cooper, who is a mutual friend of Dudamel’s and Stella Hopkins. Hopkins began sharing scores with Dudamel, which were composed by her husband, actor Anthony Hopkins. It led to them working on an album.

Industry observers note that “The thing about musicians is that they, unlike actors, they don’t have that ego,” Anthony Hopkins tells Rolling Stone of working with Dudamel. The pair met up at the Grammy Museum to talk about their collaboration on Hopkins’ debut classical album, Life Is a Dream. Dudamel conducted London’s Philharmonia Orchestra for the project, which comprises work Hopkins has composed over the course of more than six decades.

During his Venezuelan benefit show, Dudamel and LA Phil performed Hopkins’ “Stella Aria,” a moving ode to the actor’s wife, which featured a beautiful solo from Venezuelan cellist Gregorio Nieto at the concert.

“It is a great honor and a privilege because he actually endorsed my music,” states Hopkins. “I mean, I’m always filled with self-doubts as we all are … I have no theoretical, technical, musical training as such — everything is instinctive from childhood. So, naturally in me is the — ‘do I, is this good enough?,’ But when I sat there and Gustavo got up onto the podium to conduct the massive orchestra there, and I was astounded as the sound came out. He’s playing my music. Did I write that?’”.

Dudamel has a knack for making artists feel comfortable in new situations as his next act in New York illustrates — it has begun, unsurprisingly, with rave reviews. In September, his premiere debut with the New York Philharmonic at Radio City Music Hall drew the kind of rock star lineup one would expect from Dudamel. Hosted by Liev Schreiber, it featured Lizzo, St. Vincent, and Joaquina. “The Philharmonic plays for Dudamel with visible investment and enthusiasm,” a New York Times review of his first week’s New York concerts reads. “Its members haven’t looked this happy onstage in years. Either he inspires them, or his starry arrival has lifted their morale. Or both. Whatever is going on, it works.” Trending Stories Patrick Stewart Cause of Death Revealed Watch Buffalo Springfield Come Together for the First Time in Many Years Jennifer Lopez Teases New Music on ‘Fallon’: ‘This Does Feel Like a Happy Era’ Selena Gomez Shares Her Reaction to Martin Short Ruining Her Wedding Cake.

Sources indicate that it’s apparent his inclusive approach to music uplifts both musicians and fans alike. And it is contagious. His Radio City Music Hall opener began with a standing ovation.

“That is one thing that I love the most. You know, to really make people see that there are no borders between us — we enjoy, we can be there, we can be listening,” he indicates of his approach. “When you really listen not only with your ears, but with your soul, the music becomes a dimension that is infinite.”.

As a huge fan of the design of the Air, and the functionality of the 18 Pro, Apple’s 20th anniversary iPhone model could prove the perfect model for me. And for anyone else not opting for iPhone Duo 2.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Home > Journals > Michigan Law Review > MLR > Volume 118 > Issue 7 (2020).

Sources indicate that the recent revival of political interest in antitrust has resurfaced a longstanding debate about the role of industrial concentration and monopoly in enabling Hitler’s rise to power and the Third Reich’s wars of aggression. Proponents of stronger antitrust enforcement argue that monopolies and cartels brought the Nazis to power and warn that rising concentration in the American economy could similarly threaten democracy. Skeptics demur, observing that German substantial business largely opposed Hitler during the crucial years of his ascent. Drawing on business histories and archival material from the U.S. Office of Military Government’s Decartelization Branch, this Article assesses the historical record on the role of industrial concentration in facilitating Nazism. It finds compelling evidence that, while German big business principally did not support Hitler before he won the chancellorship in 1933, the extreme concentration of market power during the Weimar period enabled Hitler to seize and consolidate totalitarian power through a variety of mechanisms. Hence, the German experience with Nazism lends support to the idea that extreme concentration of economic power enables extreme concentration of political power. However, most of the conduct that created the radical economic concentration of the Weimar period would be unlawful under contemporary antitrust principles, which casts doubt on claims that a significant shift in antitrust enforcement is necessary to forestall antidemocratic forces.

According to recent reports, daniel A. Crane, Fascism and Monopoly, 118 Mich. L. Rev. 1315 (2020). Available at: https://repository.law.umich.edu/mlr/vol118/iss7/2.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, in this era where every tech product is trying to also be every other tech product, I appreciate the Index’s simplicity.
  • To buy the Index 01 ring, you get yourself a sizing kit (either buy one for $10 or 3D print it yourself), order the ring, and pair it with the Pebble app on your phone.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that pebble’s $75 ring, the Index 01, has one job: It lets you record voice memos. That seems like it would be underwhelming, and the idea was ridiculed by some of Pebble’s fans when the product was first announced. But I’ve been wearing it for a few weeks, and folks: I love it.

In a recent development, in this era where every tech product is trying to also be every other tech product, I appreciate the Index’s simplicity. This is a ring with no heart rate sensors or even charging pins, just a microphone, a button to activate it, and a light to let you know that it’s working. The audio is processed on your device; no need to send anything to the cloud.

To buy the Index 01 ring, you get yourself a sizing kit (either buy one for $10 or 3D print it yourself), order the ring, and pair it with the Pebble app on your phone. I use an iPhone rather than an Android, which means I can’t use certain features like setting timed reminders or connecting to Beeper, but it’s still an incredibly useful little device. The Index has no charger, since it uses a disposable battery that Pebble estimates will last about two years.

It has been revealed that the simplest way to use the Index is to wear it on your index finger (hence the name, get it?) and press the button with your thumb. Speak a quick note while holding the button in, and the ring will flash to let you know it got the message. A moment later, you’ll get a notification saying that it added (whatever you mentioned) to your “Notes to self” note.

Sources indicate that to take this further, you can create different notes and ask the ring to add what you say to a specific note. You can also double-click the button to ask a question. The answer will appear in the notification you get on your phone or watch a moment later. (The ring does not speak to you.).

In a recent development, all the notes you leave yourself appear as plain text in the Pebble app, fully editable. If you tap on each one, you can see a timestamp from when you left the note, and you can replay the voice recording if the transcription doesn’t make sense. (Why is there a “pencil sharp pepper” on my packing list? Ohh, that’s a pencil sharpener.) You can also add notes by typing them, which I find useful when starting a to-do list or a packing list.

It has been revealed that it’s incredible how useful a simple timestamped note can be. I used to do something similar with my “notes to self” chat in Signal, but the Index makes it even easier since I won’t get distracted by opening my phone. For example, I make a note on the Index whenever I take a medication, so that tomorrow morning I will be able to check whether I already took, say, a long-acting allergy pill. (You do not want to accidentally double up on those.).

There’s one thing that, for years, I wished for a simple tool to help me do. It’s trivial, which makes it extra frustrating that I have not been able to find a good solution. I would simply like to note when I leave for a road trip, and when I start and end each stop. This way I can tell how long the driving took as a portion of the whole trip, and how long my stops tend to be so I can strategy them better next time.

You’d think this would be easy, but every existing tool drove me nuts in a different way. Stopwatches only store a single number, so I can’t break down how long each stop was—and if I miss a button press, I’m screwed. Sending myself a Signal text is probably my best option, but if I’ve just parked my car after three hours of driving, the second I pick up my phone I’m going to see all the notifications that arrived while I was on the road, and I’ll forget to actually send that text.

According to recent reports, but this is exactly what the Index does well. I don’t even need to open my phone or look at my watch. Pressing the button with my thumb means I can do this one-handed without having a microphone always listening. (It’s also a great way to jot down the random things I think of while driving.).

The Index worked perfectly for my travel log, and I even used it for a workout after I got to my hotel room that night. I’d do 10 pushups, then tell the ring “add 10 pushups to my workout.” I’d do 20 crunches, and add that as well. I left the workout note open on my phone and could glance over and see what I had already done, since my messages got added to the note as I went.

In a recent development, I didn’t need a workout app for any of this, or a special-purpose travel app. I can just leave myself a dang note, and the note-taking app can remember when I left the note and, if I choose, play back exactly how I noted it. It’s gloriously simple. Good job, Pebble.

In a recent development, this is perhaps the best deal going on a Garmin right now. In a recent development, while this is a good price for a great adventure watch, the fact that the Fenix 7 Pro has been superseded by three rounds of Fenixes at this point makes me hope there might still be better deals to come on it and the Epix Pro. #62581. What China Gets From Its AI Honeypots and Smuggled Chips

What China Gets From Its AI Honeypots and Smuggled Chips

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1288 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollingstone

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that you could start casting the movie right now: Jensen Huang, the Taiwanese-American CEO of Nvidia, the most crucial tech company in the world, is sucked into an illicit affair with a Chinese spy.
  • Industry observers note that at least, that’s the simple version of the story.
  • Broadly speaking, there are two ways to think about AI, says Kyle Chan, an expert on Chinese technology development at the Brookings Institution.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that you could start casting the movie right now: Jensen Huang, the Taiwanese-American CEO of Nvidia, the most crucial tech company in the world, is sucked into an illicit affair with a Chinese spy. The most valuable tech in the world — Huang’s super-powered computer chips — are smuggled into China or installed into data centers connected to America’s greatest rival. Above it all, the possibility of a super-intelligent AI, a true artificial mind, looms — and its creator will be positioned to rule the world.

Industry observers note that at least, that’s the simple version of the story. But the real picture of the great geopolitical AI race is both more complex and more unbelievable than the tale of spies and smuggling that’s playing out in the press right now. China wants the U.S.’s chips — that much is clear. But why? And what can our only real rival power actually do with them? To answer this, Rolling Stone spoke with two experts in the Chinese tech sector, who pulled back the curtain on what the superpower actually wants when it comes to AI — and why it’s willing to use sex, smuggling and lies to get there.

Broadly speaking, there are two ways to think about AI, says Kyle Chan, an expert on Chinese technology development at the Brookings Institution.

Sources indicate that the first is as a straight race to one goal: creating a truly intelligent AI that surpasses human intelligence in all general tasks and can improve itself autonomously. In the industry, this is known as AGI, or Artificial General Intelligence. This point of view holds that the first country or company to achieve true AGI will have an earth-shattering advantage over any competition in economics, war, medicine, and technology. Basically, it sets the world of AI up as a winner-take-all race. Many U.S. officials — including, at times, Trump himself — have made this argument, alongside many of the private sector CEOs actually working on the technology.

“If you start with that assumption, then the effort to slow down China is nearly existential,” Chan states. Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century.

The biggest advantage the U.S. has is Nvidia’s chips. The most powerful computer chips in the world are made by one facility in Taiwan, using incredibly complex and rare machines manufactured by one tech giant in the Netherlands. It is a process so detailed and scientifically complex that it might as well be magic. Other companies can make chips, of course, but none of them can make chips as well as the single manufacturing company in Taiwan that Nvidia and most of the U.S. tech giants use. AI companies need these chips, and these chips alone, to run the most advanced AI models — which is why the U.S. has done a lot to limit China’s access to them, setting export controls on who Nvidia can sell their chips to and which countries they can be shipped into.

Because of this constraint, the Chinese don’t really see AI the same way as most of the U.S. industry does.

Sources indicate that instead of an existential threat, Chan claims, the second way to look at AI is a very powerful technology that will not necessarily lead to some massive strategic advantage for the first team past the AGI post. That makes the AI race a longer-term game, decided more by which power can holistically incorporate the advances of super-computing into its society and economy, which China has largely focused on doing.

Recent findings suggest that “What we’re kind of seeing unfold in the future is two different markets,” said Kenton Thibaut, a China expert at the Atlantic Council’s Digital Forensic Research Lab. The U.S. is focused on “frontier” systems — the absolute cutting-edge AI, powered by their chip advantage — while China is supplying “near frontier” technology that hits different parts of the market for AI technology. In China, Thibaut said, AI is viewed as a “general purpose” technology that should be harnessed for practical use as promptly as possible, rather than a more conceptual race to the furthest frontier. Related Content Man Found Guilty of Igniting Blaze That Became the Devastating Palisades Fire Trump Indicates He ‘Can’t Speak To’ Whether Russia is a Friend to America Trump Got Played by Putin and Xi Your Favorite THC Drinks Are About to Be Illegal.

Industry observers note that “All of the [Chinese] policies and major policy pronouncements and planning around AI have to do with ‘How do we make this useful in society?’” Thibaut mentioned. “I haven’t seen anything like that in the US.”.

It has been revealed that “[China’s] version of winning is being able to benefit the most from AI,” Chan indicates. “Integrate it in their economy, automate their factories, speed up drug discovery, et cetera. [They want it to] help them win across all these other domains, rather than this singular focus on achieving AGI.”.

It has been revealed that it’s a philosophical difference that is fueled by the physical constraints that the Chinese tech sector faces. The U.S. has access to more computing power than any other nation, allowing them to push the envelope. Companies like Anthropic have asked the U.S. government to regulate them more, fearful that their AI models will run out of control. In China, these discussions are scarce, Thibaut says, because the hardware they’re working with basically makes them moot — and the Chinese government is predisposed to prevent any societal disruptions. Instead, Chinese AI firms are usually focused on doing more with less — creating working, practical products and applications of AI that get the most out of whatever computing power they can harness.

And in some cases, that’s where the spies come in. The Nvidia honeypot scandal was largely controversial because it included a woman who ran a Singaporean front manufacturer that set up data centers in Southeast Asia stocked with Taiwan-made super-chips, and then leased the use of those chips to Chinese companies. Chan refers to this loophole, and the broader Chinese project of getting their hands on American tech, as a “bridge” to the country’s real goal: separating themselves from the Western “tech stack,” while still retaining competitive computing power. Eventually, Chan indicates, China wants to have its own version of the super-manufacturers in Taiwan, its own version of the very best chips — but until then, it has to use more subtle methods to get what it wants.

“If they want to keep pace today, they do still need access to Nvidia chips now,” Chan indicates. Trending Stories Patrick Stewart Cause of Death Revealed Miley Cyrus and Maxx Morando Marry at Palm Springs Wedding Princess of Wales Reflects on Cancer Battle in 'Heal' Documentary Special Boy George on His Israel Trip: 'I Wasn't Able to Not Say Something'.

Some parts of the U.S. government may be helping them achieve that. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnik had been very lax with Nvidia and Huang personally, allowing the company to continue selling to companies that the U.S. knew were linked with China. While Trump has mentioned he views AI as a winner-take-all race, Reuters reported that his administration also signed off on the sale of 900,000 AI chips to Chinese companies in one six-month period, and his own AI Czar David Sacks has explicitly advocated for selling more chips directly to China.

China, then, has allies to go along with its spies — and it seems that one way or another, it’s getting all the chips it needs.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The BBC has apologized to viewers after lewd noises could be heard during the Strictly Come Dancing live show at Blackpool’s Tower Ballroom.

A recording of sex noises appeared to be played from the audience as Strictly judge Motsi Mabuse delivered her remarks about the performance of Delta Goodrem and partner Kai Widdrington.

Recent findings suggest that microphones picked up the noise. Mabuse turned to the audience to establish what was going on, before facing the camera again and exclaiming: “It’s not me.”.

Emma Willis had to apologise at the end of tonight’s Strictly Come Dancing for ‘anything offensive’ that was heard during the show. Turns out, it was sex noises played by someone in the background. The episode of #Strictly is currently still not available on iPlayer. pic.twitter.com/fPxDW45h1V.

Industry observers note that at the end of the show (the format on which ABC’s Dancing with the Stars is based), presenter Emma Willis apologized to viewers “if you heard any audio disruptions”. Sources indicate that in a statement, a BBC spokesperson added: “We apologise to any viewers offended during the live broadcast of Strictly this evening. We are investigating how this happened.” The noise was edited out of the version of the show available on iPlayer. Watch on Deadline.

Industry observers note that the police were called to the incident. A Lancashire Police spokesperson told The Guardian: “We are aware of an incident that took place during the filming of Strictly Come Dancing in Blackpool.

“We have been in contact with the event organisers, and a formal complaint has been made to us. A mobile phone has been seized and we are now looking into the matter to see if any criminal offences have taken place.”.

Industry observers note that it is the second time a BBC live show has been interrupted by sex noises. Coverage of an FA Cup tie between Wolves and Liverpool was plagued by an apparent pornography prank in 2023.

Gary Lineker was anchoring live build-up to the replay match at the Molineux Stadium when he was interrupted by what sounded like sex noises coming from the studio.

The former England player looked perplexed by the noise in the studio, joking to fellow presenter Alan Shearer: “I don’t know who’s making that noise … It’s toasty in this studio, it’s a bit noisy as well. I don’t know if somebody is sending something on someone’s phone, if it’s a joke. I don’t know whether you heard it at home.”.

Lineker later tweeted a picture of a phone, which he mentioned had been taped to the back of the set in an apparent act of sabotage.

#62579. How Do You Land on a Moon With Almost No Gravity?

📅 06 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 15m • 📚 Deep Dive (2974 w)
