General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Ieee ↗ Open Full Page

How Do You Land on a Moon With Almost No Gravity?

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 15 min read (2974 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ieee

⏱️ ~15 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Japan’s MMX mission aims to sample the Martian moon Phobos.
  • Japan's MMX spacecraft will fire its engines to slow down and enter orbit around Mars.
  • According to recent reports, last August, looking up from the edge of an ancient river delta on Mars, the Perseverance rover’s electronic eye spied an oblong shadow crossing the distant, glowing Sun.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Japan’s MMX mission aims to sample the Martian moon Phobos.

Japan's MMX spacecraft will fire its engines to slow down and enter orbit around Mars.

According to recent reports, last August, looking up from the edge of an ancient river delta on Mars, the Perseverance rover’s electronic eye spied an oblong shadow crossing the distant, glowing Sun. Phobos, the Martian moon named for the Greek god of fear and panic, was transiting the solar disk. Too small to darken the pale, dust-tinged sky, but orbiting close enough to eclipse a significant fraction of the Sun, Phobos passed in less than a minute.

NASA’s Perseverance rover captured Phobos passing in front of the Sun from the surface of Mars.ASU/MSSS/SSI/JPL-Caltech/NASA.

According to recent reports, the tiny moon, with its murky origins, is an enigma, and one whose makeup and history could tell us much about Mars and the wider solar system. And now the international Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission, which successfully launched on 20 October, seeks to explore that mystery with an unprecedented series of landings on the unknown surface of Phobos.

Recent findings suggest that this mission brings unusual challenges—for example, designing an orbit to study a microgravity moon orbiting a much larger planet. Engineers also had to figure out how to assess and land on this low-gravity pile of loosely assembled dirt and rock, how a rover might rove across it, and how the spacecraft might take samples and return them to Earth.

Industry observers note that “I often say that landing on Phobos is like trying to land a balloon,” says Yasuhiro Kawakatsu, project manager of MMX at the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA). “It’s very difficult to drop a balloon to the ground and prevent it from tilting or bouncing.”.

Recent findings suggest that phobos is one of two small Martian moons; the other is Deimos, named after the Greek god of dread and terror. Their cosmic origins are unknown, though there are two prevailing theories. One holds that the moons were once asteroids from the belt between Mars and Jupiter, captured by the smaller planet’s gravity. In the other theory, Phobos and Deimos formed when a large celestial body slammed into Mars, sending debris into orbit. Some models suggest the pair are the last survivors from a cluster of satellites.

The enormous Stickney crater, roughly 9 kilometers across, dominates this view of Phobos taken by NASA’s Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter.University of Arizona/JPL-Caltech/NASA.

Scientifically speaking, Phobos is considered a rubble pile, a loosely consolidated aggregate of rock and dust. Far too small to become spherical under its own mass, it’s shaped like a lumpy potato, roughly 27 kilometers in length, with only 1/1,800th of Earth’s gravity. On Phobos, a typical adult would weigh about as much as a tennis ball does on Earth.

More than 10 years in the making, MMX rolled out on Japan’s flagship H3 rocket from Tanegashima spaceport on 20 October local time. It will arrive at Mars in 2027 carrying scientific payloads from several space agencies, including NASA, and a newly introduced rover called Idefix developed by the French and German space agencies (CNES and DLR) in collaboration with JAXA.

Engineers assembled MMX’s modules at Japan’s Tanegashima Space Center before the spacecraft’s October 2026 launch.JAXA.

MMX consists of three modules: a propulsion module to power its journey to Mars and apply the brakes to enter orbit around the red planet; an exploration module carrying the rover, sampling gear, and other scientific instruments; and a return module, attached to the exploration module, that harbors the capsule destined for a high-speed reentry into Earth’s atmosphere. After collecting samples on Phobos, the exploration and return modules will lift off together. The exploration module will then be jettisoned while the return module sets a course back home.

If all goes according to blueprint, MMX will deliver a 10-gram sample to Earth in the second half of 2031. But the mission will face a series of daunting challenges to reach that end point, including navigating complex orbits around Phobos and landing on its surface while Mars periodically blocks communications with Earth.

The MMX’s modular design includes the propulsion module [left] and the exploration and return modules [right].Kyodo News/Getty Images.

“It’s the most complex mission I have ever seen,” indicates Patrick Michel, director of research at CNRS (the French National Center for Scientific Research) and co-principal investigator on Idefix.

An H3 rocket carried MMX into space on 20 October 2026, beginning the mission’s five-year journey to Phobos and back.The Asahi Shimbun/Getty Images.

Sources indicate that once MMX reached low Earth orbit, its propulsion module’s engine fired, kicking off a nearly year-long deep-space cruise to Mars. On arrival, the spacecraft will need to fire its engines in an extended, carefully timed burn to slow down enough to be captured by Mars gravity. The propulsion module will then be jettisoned, leaving the exploration and return modules to orbit Mars.

“If something doesn’t go according to proposal, MMX will fly by Mars and get catapulted into the solar system,” says Nicola Baresi, an astrodynamicist who coauthored a paper on specially designed orbits for MMX.

From that initial orbit, MMX will transition into a specially designed quasi-satellite orbit that allows it to keep pace with the small moon but also move around it. Since Phobos is too small to orbit in the conventional sense, the spacecraft will orbit Mars alongside the moon, following a clever egg-shaped path that slings MMX alternately ahead of and behind the moon. “When you’re closer to Mars, you’re accelerating with respect to Phobos, and when you’re farther from Mars, you’re decelerating. So you essentially go back and forth,” explains Baresi.

Martian Maneuvers To reach Phobos, MMX will execute three major maneuvers: MOI-1 will put the spacecraft into orbit around Mars, MOI-2 will transfer it toward Phobos, and MOI-3 will place it into its final orbit alongside the moon.Chris Philpot.

To reach Phobos, MMX will execute three major maneuvers: MOI-1 will put the spacecraft into orbit around Mars, MOI-2 will transfer it toward Phobos, and MOI-3 will place it into its final orbit alongside the moon.

In a recent development, the best existing images of Phobos, from spacecraft such as NASA’s Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter and ESA’s Mars Express, have resolutions of only a few meters per pixel. That’s larger than Idefix, the mission’s rover, itself about the size of a microwave oven. To map the surface in greater detail, MMX will loop in front of and behind Phobos at distances ranging from 200 kilometers to less than 20 km from the surface.

According to recent reports, during its two-year remote sensing campaign, the exploration module will use several cameras and a laser altimeter to map the surface in high resolution and look for candidate landing sites. When Mars passes behind the Sun as seen from the Earth, causing a roughly two-week communications blackout, MMX will retreat into a larger, stable orbit. After communications resume, MMX will prepare to send its first visitor down to the surface.

According to recent reports, before the exploration and connected return modules attempt to land, Kawakatsu indicates, MMX will send a scout that in Japanese is called “the first penguin,” leaping into unknown waters. For this mission, the first to leap will be the Idefix rover, named for the canine companion to Obelix in the French comics series Asterix. The exploration module will release the rover during a low-altitude pass of between 40 and 100 meters above Phobos’s surface in 2028 or early 2029.

MMX will use its TENGOO camera [left] and LIDAR laser altimeter [right] to map Phobos’s terrain.JAXA.

Recent findings suggest that it will be a tense moment that calls back to 2005, during Japan’s Hayabusa mission to explore the asteroid Itokawa. In a similarly designed drop, the MINERVA rover was released from an orbiter, but erroneously at 200 meters instead of the intended 70 meters. The rover missed the asteroid and, without propulsion, drifted off into deep space.

In a recent development, idefix will get a slight nudge out of the exploration module toward its negligible-gravity target, freefalling and likely tumbling as it goes. It’s expected to touch down with a velocity of less than 1 meter per second. Unlike rovers that have landed on other surfaces with airbags or dedicated landing legs, Idefix will land without protection, apart from some extra padding on the solar panels due to their critical nature. The barely-there gravity of Phobos should allow the 23-kilogram rover to land softly, though exactly how this landing will play out is hard to predict.

The Idefix rover will travel to Phobos with its wheels tucked in and solar panels folded.DLR.

Sources indicate that “It will bounce probably several times,” says Stephan Ulamec, Idefix’s co-principal investigator and project manager at DLR. “It will come to rest somehow in some position.” Once it’s still, four retracted legs will deploy to right the rover autonomously, regardless of its orientation. It will then unfold its solar panels to charge its batteries for exploration tasks ahead.

A simulation reveals how Idefix is expected to tumble onto Phobos, right itself using its articulated legs, and begin exploring the moon’s surface. DLR.

Recent findings suggest that once operational, Idefix will roll at a snail’s pace, topping out at one millimeter per second. Its metal wheels have protruding blades like a paddle wheel, designed to gain traction in Phobos’s microgravity. “If we were to drive our rover faster, then it would actually be more like we were swimming through instead of driving across the surface,” says Cecily Sunday, a doctoral student involved in testing Idefix’s WheelCams at the Institut Superieur de l’Aeronautique et de l’Espace (ISAE-Supaéro) in Toulouse, France.

The WheelCams, a pair of cameras placed on the underside of the rover, will observe the wheels and their tracks during Idefix’s planned 100-Earth-day primary mission. The images will help researchers study the size and distribution of grains in Phobos’s regolith and how cohesive they are. How much or how little the grains stick together will greatly impact how Idefix moves. Sunday likens this to the difference between driving on dry and wet sand. “Think of trying to build a sandcastle with dry sand,” she states. “You can’t. Add water, and suddenly you can.”.

The Idefix rover was mounted between the MMX spacecraft’s landing legs for the journey to Phobos.DLR.

Industry observers note that the team tested the rover’s nine-bladed wheels on a variety of materials, including Phobos regolith simulants provided by JAXA and DLR, lunar simulants, glass beads, quartz sand, and clay pebbles. “We characterize the mechanical properties of each simulant precisely, then test across the full range, with varying grain size, angularity, and even color, so we can map what we see in the WheelCam images back to actual surface properties,” Sunday indicates.

Despite the microgravity and Phobos’s rubble-pile nature, Sunday says Earth-based tests can approximate the rover’s motion on the surface of the small moon fairly well. While Phobos’s reduced gravity lowers the rover’s effective weight, there is also reduced pressure between the grains beneath its wheels. “As long as you’re moving very, very slowly and using the same materials and the same weight of the system, they should be representative,” Sunday says.

With four paddle-like wheels and deployable solar panels, Idefix is designed to crawl across Phobos.Ardan Fuessmann/Imago/Alamy.

Idefix’s interactions with its new home will offer “sub-millimeter resolution and information on porosity, on grain size, on surface strength, on how hard is the material,” Ulamec states. “It fills a gap between remote observations from orbit and detailed observations of the return samples back on Earth.”.

According to recent reports, what Idefix finds on this rocky, rugged world will help determine how and where JAXA attempts to land the main spacecraft. Michel says the touchdown will provide ground truth for understanding of Phobos. When NASA’s OSIRIS-REx spacecraft touched down on the asteroid Bennu to collect a sample, its sampling arm surprisingly sank nearly half a meter into the loose material. But Ulamec doesn’t think Idefix will sink deep into Phobos, noting that Bennu is very different and much smaller, with a diameter of 500 meters.

Once Idefix has investigated the surface, MMX will face an even greater challenge: landing its much larger exploration module on Phobos. The spacecraft will make a controlled descent to roughly 10 meters above the surface, then drop the remaining distance in free fall. With so little gravity to pull it downward, even a small sideways motion could cause the lander to tip or bounce away. A successful, upright landing would mark the start of up to two hours on Phobos for the crucial sampling phase.

The MMX mission draws on the experience and technologies of Japan’s two Hayabusa sample-return missions, which landed on the asteroids Itokawa and Ryugu. But this mission has many more moving parts. MMX’s exploration module will use two sampling devices—a coring sampler developed by JAXA and a pneumatic sampler provided by NASA and fabricated by Honeybee Robotics, a subsidiary of Blue Origin. Data from these tools, and those carried by the Idefix rover, could answer questions about the origin of Phobos and how the Mars system has evolved.

The coring sampler uses a robot arm and a cylindrical corer designed to reach at least 2 centimeters below the surface. The arm can maneuver to find the best site for digging. “That by itself is a challenge because we’ve never done it,” Michel says. “You never know what can happen at the very sampling site itself, where you might have a boulder and the arm cannot move.”.

Sources indicate that probing beneath the top layer will be valuable because solar radiation, galactic cosmic rays, and micrometeorites have battered and weathered the surface. The material below should offer a better record of the moon’s origins, and JAXA aims to collect at least 10 grams of it.

MMX will carry both the Idefix rover [bottom] and a robotic coring sampler [top] designed to dig beneath Phobos’s weathered surface.JAXA.

The pneumatic sampler takes a different approach. Mounted on one of the lander’s legs, it will inject pure, non-reactive nitrogen gas into the surface and capture the grains stirred up. This sample could illuminate the changes Mars and its moons have undergone over time. The dual system also adds redundancy in the face of Phobos’s unknowns. “If the surface of Phobos proves to be very hard, [the coring sampler] may struggle to penetrate the ground. [The pneumatic sampler] would not experience this issue and still be able to gather material,” Kawakatsu states.

It has been revealed that one of the most intriguing aspects of MMX is the additional possibility of collecting material from the planet below. It’s likely that Phobos has been peppered by Martian ejecta thrown into space by meteor impacts, so MMX also provides an opportunity to return the first Martian samples to Earth. Michel estimates that the samples could contain “a few hundred grains coming from Mars.” Scientists can distinguish those grains from native Phobos material by analyzing their oxygen isotopes.

In a recent development, that possibility raises a planetary-protection question. A direct Mars sample-return mission would have to follow strict rules to ensure that potentially living biological material from Mars doesn’t contaminate Earth. But those protocols don’t apply to MMX, even if its sample does collect grains of Martian soil. A panel of experts concluded that any microbes blasted off Mars wouldn’t survive the violent impact and ejection or the intense radiation exposure on the way to Phobos. This saved MMX from implementing expensive and time-consuming quarantine and containment protocols for the returning sample.

After landing on Phobos, MMX will have roughly two hours to collect samples from the moon’s surface before lifting off again.JAXA.

In a recent development, during the brief surface operation, the robotic arm will deposit the samples in a storage unit, from which they’ll be transferred into a capsule aboard the return module and sealed in a vacuum. After that, lift off.

It has been revealed that once back in Mars orbit, the exploration module will resume its observations of Phobos and make several flybys of Mars’s other diminutive moon, Deimos, to gather data on its surface, structure, and composition. In November 2030, during a favorable alignment of Mars and Earth, MMX will begin the homeward leg of its trip. The return module will separate from the exploration module and power the voyage home, its sole objective to bring the dust of Phobos to Earth.

MMX’s sample return capsule will carry material from Phobos through Earth’s atmosphere in 2031.JAXA.

Finally, in 2031, the 60-centimeter-wide sample capsule will plunge into Earth’s atmosphere at roughly 12 kilometers per second. Assuming it survives the extreme heat of reentry and lands safely in Australia, scientists will begin to tease out clues about Phobos and the early solar system. JAXA’s Institute of Space and Astronautical Science will receive and curate the samples, which will also be shared with mission partners.

Industry observers note that “We have macroscale measurements from the spacecraft, microscale measurements with the rover, and then sample analysis,” Michel states. “So we can relate the three kinds of scales together because we have all of them.” The insights gleaned from orbital images, close-up images of the regolith, and the chemical analysis of the samples could have wider implications for our understanding of our solar system.

Sources indicate that “MMX is a mission to understand the Mars system and shed light onto how terrestrial planets like the Earth, and maybe Mars, develop a habitable environment,” Kawakatsu says. “We strongly suspect that our terrestrial planet region formed dry, and water and organics were scattered inwards from the icy-rich outer solar system.” Mars, he says, sits at the gateway between the inner and outer solar system, making its moons valuable witnesses to the processes that shaped potentially habitable worlds.

  • According to recent reports, the problem with the difference between plan and apply jobs is that plan can't possibly emulate every actual API call against a live infrastructure.
  • Recent findings suggest that there are multiple tools that can emulate AWS services either partially or in full, but what they lack is the actual knowledge of the service architecture.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Terraform plan passes and indicates all green and all the necessary resource changes. You trigger apply and... the job fails with some obscure error that a resource can't be changed. You open another pull request and try again. And perhaps you encounter an error again. Sounds familiar? I bet it does. I encountered problems like this so many times I'm afraid to count. But recently AWS released a upcoming tool called Emulator that emulates actual AWS API endpoints. And it should be great for tasks just like that!

According to recent reports, the problem with the difference between plan and apply jobs is that plan can't possibly emulate every actual API call against a live infrastructure. It's a safe assumption based on the static declarations we put into it – the order of application, the necessary parameters, the proper configuration values. These mock calls can't know for a fact that you already have a resource in AWS called "my-bucket-asdasdasd" or that you're trying to upgrade a PostgreSQL RDS instance from version 14 to version 18 without an explicit "apply immediately" flag. One may argue that one can always try to apply changes locally, but this kinda undermines the whole automation workflow. So what is the answer?

Recent findings suggest that there are multiple tools that can emulate AWS services either partially or in full, but what they lack is the actual knowledge of the service architecture. It may be similar, but it won't be authentic, and sometimes this small difference may cause a lot of problems. After all, what can be the closest to an AWS API, if not the same AWS API, but ephemeral?

Industry observers note that the benefit of the AWS Emulator is that it's a self-contained binary (or Docker container) that can be utilized locally or in a CI workflow. This means the usual "Initiative > Apply" terraform workflow changes to "Plan > Apply against mock AWS infrastructure to test the plan > Apply on actual AWS Infrastructure". This means slightly longer jobs, but if you're like me and apply jobs run on commits to the main branch after a PR, this saves you the hassle of creating a new branch just to fix the matter.

Let's start with a local setup and see how we can utilize AWS Emulator with the actual Terraform code. All code is available in my example GitHub repository.

First up, installation. You can either install aws-emulator via package manager, or build it with Docker. I'll use Docker to keep my system clear of yet another package:.

In the example above I set the container to live without limits (official AWS documentation proposes to set memory and swap limits: --memory=2g --memory-swap=2g, but for local that's fine). I also disabled authorization (flag -a off) to simplify things a bit.

To be sure aws-emulator is up and running, let's query the admin endpoint:.

Okay, fake AWS is live, let's deploy some infrastructure!

It has been revealed that I created an example AWS stack for Terraform and will use it in this article. First, let's configure Terraform to act against aws-emulator and not real AWS APIs. providers.tf will look like this:.

The difference between actual live infrastructure and a fake one is that we set up a bunch of flags to allow insecure connections (perhaps turning authentication off wasn't actually simpler?) and we set up an endpoint for each service we use in the setup to an emulator endpoint, which lives in the local Docker container:.

Recent findings suggest that the rest of the configuration is as usual: resources, variables, modules (if any). Just what your project has.

Sources indicate that let's proceed and test our setup. (I'll omit full terraform output otherwise this article would be 3 kilometers long).

In a recent development, strategy works! That's good to see, but not what we're here for. Still, a good sign. Now for the real test.

Sadly, the running aws-emulator container doesn't show in its logs which API requests it receives and what's happening under the hood, but I guess the tool is good enough as it is.

When you're done, stop the container:.

A container started with --rm removes itself after stopping, so no additional cleanup is needed. And as for the emulator -- it stores its state in memory, so each container restart drops all record of previous actions and any stale state.

Industry observers note that now for the real test: can we wrap the desired logic inside a CI pipeline? Let's think.

For successful invocation in the pipeline we will need almost everything the same, but we will be limited by time (the faster -- the better, and overall reasonable timeouts) and resources.

According to recent reports, the workflow with terraform apply against aws-emulator is shown down below. For it I decided to try out package manager installation (builders are ephemeral anyway) and proper authentication. Full workflow with actual successful runs can be found in the example GitHub repository.

This is a crude excerpt of the actual glorious workflow file that outlines the most important steps: emulator installation, terraform setup, proposal and apply. On the example terraform architecture the whole pipeline took 1m25s, which is okay in my opinion, but there is room for improvement: sprinkle some caching on top, leave validation, format check for local hooks, etc.

It's always nice when code someone wrote on the internet works from the start after you copy-paste it onto your machine. That's why I always run the described processes myself -- building, testing, fixing, retrying -- before publishing an article. But showing only the positive scenarios creates a false sense of trust in the tool.

Let's break something on purpose.

Recent findings suggest that in the example codebase I added a variable that, when enabled, makes the stack try to deploy a resource with an erroneous declaration. It will pass the plan job, but fail on apply.

Setting this variable to true at runtime will break our stack. Let's see:.

Recent findings suggest that and there we have it. The exact problem that arises only against actual API calls and not during a proposal job.

For scenarios exactly like this, the emulator is priceless.

AWS Emulator is AWESOME. I'm rarely that excited about new tools lately (mostly because almost all of them are near/about AI), but this one is just so good and scratches that exact itch I felt for so long.

It has been revealed that for starters, it can't effectively emulate IAM policies and permission checks. This is a bummer, because permission validation is such a crucial step for production-ready security. Here's hoping that the tool will evolve further and it will be included in future updates.

Sources indicate that second, as a tool still a work-in-progress[1], its capabilities are quite limited. Even while writing the article I encountered several cases of 501 NotImplemented. It complicates things a bit if your infrastructure setup is huge and has a lot of quirks and weird configurations and super fresh services. Still, AWS releases new versions quite often, and they're quite open about Emulator limitations, which is nice.

According to recent reports, and last, but not least, is telemetry. AWS is explicit that it gathers telemetry and what this telemetry includes. This is honest behaviour and I like that approach. They even allow you to disable the telemetry, which further increases my trust in this tool. I understand the rationale behind this functionality (the tool is actively developed, they need the data to understand usage patterns and what goes wrong), but in the age of constant surveillance from Substantial Tech at every corner it still raises a slight concern. But then again, for the ultra-paranoid folks the code is open source and can be rebuilt with telemetry torn out of it.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that gemini Notebook, Google's AI tool for study and research, already lets you do a lot with your notes: You can turn them into flashcard quizzes, interactive podcasts, video explainers, mind maps, and infographics, as well as interrogating the sources you've collected through AI-powered prompts and responses.
  • That might not immediately seem like the most obvious fit, turning your research notes into a mass of HTML code.
  • In a recent development, website building is rolling out now for Gemini Notebook's web app for all customers, and is "coming soon" to the mobile app.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that gemini Notebook, Google's AI tool for study and research, already lets you do a lot with your notes: You can turn them into flashcard quizzes, interactive podcasts, video explainers, mind maps, and infographics, as well as interrogating the sources you've collected through AI-powered prompts and responses. Now there's something upcoming. You can also build interactive websites from your notebooks.

That might not immediately seem like the most obvious fit, turning your research notes into a mass of HTML code. But it gives you another way to look at your material and to get insights from it. Here's how it works, what you could potentially do with it, and how impressively it worked when I put it to the test on some early 20th-century Irish literature.

In a recent development, website building is rolling out now for Gemini Notebook's web app for all customers, and is "coming soon" to the mobile app. You won't see a website option in the Studio panel alongside Audio Overview, Reports, Quiz, and the rest; instead, you type something along the lines of "make me a website" in the prompt box.

To make a website, you need sources, so I set Gemini Notebook to collect information about James Joyce's 1914 collection of short stories, Dubliners. As I studied Dubliners many years ago (I highly recommend it), I was hoping I'd spot any AI errors and hallucinations, and be able to properly assess the quality of Gemini Notebook's analysis.

According to recent reports, with a suitable amount of information absorbed into the AI brain, I got Gemini Notebook to make me a website. Google doesn't give too much official guidance here, but indicates you should add "a description of what you want to build for work or study," so if you have a particular style or angle in mind, include it.

Here was my prompt: "Build a website using all the sources and information collected so far. Make it an interactive guide to the individual stories in Dubliners, as well as the overarching themes and context. I want to use it as a study aid to explore different aspects of the story collection.".

According to recent reports, the finished website pops up in the Studio panel, and in my case it took around five minutes to put something together from 26 different sources. Click on the website, and it opens in a new window—you can use it from there, open it in a separate tab, or download the code to your computer.

In a recent development, I was honestly impressed by how much Gemini Notebook managed to pack into a single website: I got plot summaries, analysis, critical context, and some of the main themes and motifs outlined. There was an interactive quiz at the bottom of the page to test my knowledge, and even a graphic I could click through to reveal different elements of how the stories fit together.

According to recent reports, everything was well laid out and functional, albeit with the standard "sheen" you get from anything made by AI (which tends to always pick the same colors and fonts). I wouldn't have necessarily thought that I needed a website if I was still studying Dubliners today, but I can definitely see how it would have helped.

For something like my project, a website really works well as a study aid, since it offers a different way of interrogating the information. You can already do that in the main chat, and with tools such as the audio and video overviews, but this is different. It's a bit like having a mini-Wikipedia focused just on whatever you're researching.

The interactive elements that are included—so in my example, I could click from story to story, and theme to theme, within the same page—make a site more engaging than a standard report document and a static wall of text, and should help the information stick if you're trying to study it.

In a recent development, I can also see how this might be useful for sharing data with others. Maybe you need to analyze monthly report figures, or you want to chart how your organization has developed a product over time—perhaps an interactive website will relay that information in a more compelling way than a slide deck or PDF.

Industry observers note that maybe you have a notebook stuffed with details of a substantial family vacation. Putting together a website through Gemini Notebook would give your family a hub that they could use to easily check up on the details of the trip—where you're going and when, what you'll see there, what they need to pack, and so on. Another idea might be a family tree, if you have ancestry data and sources packed together in a notebook. Putting together a website would be a great way to visualize it, and, again, it's something you could share with relatives. If there were updates to the data you've collected, you could generate a newly introduced website.

Bear in mind that you can do a lot with your prompt. My website turned out the way it did because that's what I asked for, and if you need more interactivity or specific types of sections, then you can ask. Based on my follow-up prompts, you can also specify colors and certain layout choices, though it's not quite a full-scale website builder.

It looks like these sites are single-page creations, though they do have interactive elements and sections that change as you click around. It might be better to think of them as mini apps rather than sites. As of yet, there's no built-in option for publishing a site online or sharing it with others, so you need to download the HTML and do that manually.

Recent findings suggest that heal: A Princess of Wales Story will air November 30 on NBC, a day after it premieres on the BBC. The documentary follows Kate Middleton as she reflects on her cancer battle while completing the Three Peaks Challenge — climbing the tallest mountains in England, Scotland and Wales in the span of 24 hours — this past June in support of the Royal Marsden Cancer Charity, the hospital where she was treated; proceeds from the distribution of Heal will also benefit Royal Marsden.

“Cancer does change you. It changes your body, it changes you physically. But there’s a much, much deeper part to what a cancer diagnosis shifts in you,” the Princess of Wales states in the trailer.

Sources indicate that “It’s clear we’re not meant to carry life’s challenges alone. Things can renew and grow. After it is through pain that we realize there’s a greater beauty that lies beyond that.”.

The news of Middleton’s initial diagnosis was disclosed to the public in March 2024, following an abdominal surgery in January. In a video statement, Middleton said, “At the time, it was thought that my condition was non-cancerous,” referring to her surgery. “The surgery was successful, however, tests after the operation on cancer had been present,” she added. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • SUNDAY AM: Lionsgate and Suzanne Collins accomplished what no other Harry Potter movie has pulled off at the box office: Seeing a preview/spinoff opening to north of $100M at the domestic B.O., which is exactly what their Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping did with a North American start of $120M.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

SUNDAY AM: Lionsgate and Suzanne Collins accomplished what no other Harry Potter movie has pulled off at the box office: Seeing a preview/spinoff opening to north of $100M at the domestic B.O., which is exactly what their Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping did with a North American start of $120M.

In addition, Sunrise on the Reaping ranks as the second best U.S./Canada opening for a prequel after 2016’s Rogue One: A Star Wars Story which debuted to $155M. This is also Lionsgate’s biggest opening post Covid, and their first $100M+ opening in 11 years, the last being 2015’s The Hunger Games: Mockingjay Part 2 with $102.66M.

Industry observers note that as rich as Harry Potter was in its sequels, Warners wasn’t able to get Fantastic Beasts to shine greater than a $74.4M opening, which is what the first prequel/spinoff title opened to in 2016. Hence, the Fantastic Beast movies became industry comps (along with 2019’s Hobbs & Shaw with a $60M start) in regards to the ceilings of what a spinoff/prequel franchise could open to at the box office.

Industry observers note that the reason why we’re banging this drum is because when Lionsgate opened The Hunger Games: Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes to a ho-hum $44.6M three years ago, it felt like the popularity of the Collins franchise had hit the bottom of the well, destined to live in a middling range for the rest of its days. Nope.

Industry observers note that thumbs up to Collins for getting the franchise back on track in the backstory of Woody Harrelson character Haymitch Abernathy, making the sixth novel in the 14-year old series feel like the biggest Games yet, and to Lionsgate Motion Picture Chairman Adam Fogelson in the continued belief that Hunger Games could see a renaissance among its fanship. It also helped that Collins’ latest novel Sunrise on the Reaping sold way more, and was received with more warmth than Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes which debuted during Covid.

Remarked Fogelson, “When you have filmmaking giants as talented as Francis Lawrence, Nina Jacobson, and Brad Simpson guiding the vision established by the brilliant creator Suzanne Collins, who started it all, you are in enormously capable hands. This success is a testament to their remarkable film, the performances of our incredibly talented cast, and ultimately, the love of Hunger Games fans worldwide, who embraced a film that told a story they had been asking to see for many years. Because of the incredible work of every part of our Motion Picture Group and our amazing filmmaking team, combined with the passion and devotion of the Hunger Games family of fans, the franchise is as strong and vibrant today as when the first Hunger Games film was released nearly 15 years ago.”.

Recent findings suggest that how Lionsgate got Sunrise on the Reaping to shine brighter than the sun: That teaser, which released a year ago, was the second most-watched in the studio’s history after Michael with 109M global views in its first 24-hours. If you want to bridge the gap in a legacy franchise between old fans and a new generation, you have to honor the old with the new. As such, to make fans go bananas, it was leaked back in December that OG Hunger Games stars Jennifer Lawrence and Josh Hutcherson were reprising their characters in the prequel — a scene that fans were also treated to in the book. Lionsgate leaned into them and Harrelson in the marketing with appearances on The Tonight Show and Watch What Happens Live.

When Lionsgate confirmed the 16 individual castings, those yielded 541 million views and 35.2 million engagements, an early driver and indicator of fans excitement.

The top movie titles where the trailer was previewed in-theaters included Spider-Man: Brand New Day, Michael and The Housemaid.

According to recent reports, overall, the marketing campaign for Sunrise on the Reaping generated 1 billion owned social views and 74 billion views of fan-generated content across relevant Hunger Games TikTok hashtags and 1.5 million new followers across official social channels. The pic ranked No. 2 on TikTok’s Trending Chart behind Avengers: Doomsday. There was renewed audience enthusiasm among women 17-34 with Sunrise on the Reaping notching a 36% first choice over Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes.

Sunrise on the Reaping pulled in 7.1M admissions this weekend according to EntTelligence (+122% off the 3.2M opening weekend admissions of Songbirds & Snakes) off a $16.06 average ticket price, $13.80 children ticket price, and general PLF ticket price of $19.62. Matinees before 5PM repped 45% of the foot traffic yesterday.

Rentrak reports that the YTD B.O. for Jan. 1- Nov. 22 is $8.97 billion, +20% from the same frame in 2025. All pics this weekend counted $168M, -8% from a year ago when Wicked: For the Good opened.

SATURDAY AM: Lionsgate has gotten The Hunger Games franchise back in the $100M+ opening range that this Suzanne Collins IP is known for on the substantial screen as the sixth film, The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, is now posting a $120M North American start after a $56M Friday, which includes previews. In addition, the CinemaScore jumped from a B+ on the last film, Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes, to an A- here.

PostTrak exits have increased to an 80% definite recommend, and 93% positive. The pic is playing evenly throughout the nation, however, strong in South, South Central, Midwest and Mountain. PLFs and Imax are repping 47% of the weekend (15% Imax, 32% PLFs). AMC Lincoln Square is the highest grossing venue for the Francis Lawrence directed title at $168K as of Friday.

According to recent reports, walk-up business for Sunrise on the Reaping was 36% yesterday in PostTrak exits (meaning those who purchased tickets same day). That’s similar walk-up business to Wicked two years (37%), and higher than last year’s Wicked: For Good (26%), but it’s lower than Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes (47%). Realize though that movie didn’t have a majority of fans buying tickets in advance like Sunrise on the Reaping (54% to 64%).

Women at 68% remain the big turnout for the latest Hunger Games movie which is no surprise. Forty-nine percent of the women who saw the movie came with one friend or more to watch the film (similar to Songbirds & Snakes 50% who came with one to five people), while 22% came with a date, spouse or partner (same as the 2023 film). The overall audience at 64% bought tickets because it’s for a franchise they love, while 33% mentioned it was because of the cast.

Recent findings suggest that diversity demos on Sunrise on the Reaping are 49% Caucasian, 27% Latino and Hispanic, 9% Black and 9% Asian American, which is similar to the previous pic’s 50% Caucasian, 24% Latino and Hispanic and 10% apiece for Black and Asian American audiences. The percentage of 18-34 year olds showing up remained huge at 74% for Sunrise versus 76% for Songbirds & Snakes.

Sunrise on the Reaping at the moment is the fourth best opening in the franchise, but will likely be the third best, overtaking 2014’s Hunger Games: Mockingjay Part 1 ($55.1M Friday/previews and $121.8M 3-day) by tomorrow. The top two domestic starts in the Collins series are 2013’s Catching Fire ($70.9M Friday/previews, $158M 3-day) and the original 2012 Hunger Games ($67.2M Friday/previews and $152.5M opening). Catching Fire stills stands as Lionsgate’s top opening at the domestic B.O.

Amazon MGM Studio’s I Play Rocky is coming in ligher than expected with $9.3M despite scoring a rare A+ CinemaScore (which no Rocky movie in CinemaScore history has done even though this pic is about the making of the 1976 Sylvester Stallone movie). Note the movie is older skewing with 52% over 45, and that audience will take their time to come out, likely discovering the movie later this week. The exits here are powerful enough with an 87% definite recommend. 59% to 41% male-to-female with 50% men over 25, 37% women over 25 and 9% men under 25 and 5% women under 25. Very strong positive scores and definite recommends in every single demo. Caucasian turnout at 57%, Latino and Hispanic at 22%, Black at 8% (giving pic a 100%), Asian American at 7%, and Native American at 7% (also a 100% score).

Sources indicate that no major PLFs on this pic. The Peter Farrelly directed movie is playing best in the West, East and South Central. To give you an idea of how older skewing it is, the Cinemark Palace 21 in Boca Raton, FL is the leading single-location gross at $11.2K yesterday.

It has been revealed that the entire theatrical marketplace is around $172.1M, just -5% off from a year ago when Wicked: For Good opened to a franchise best of $147M. With no Moana, Zootopia, or Wicked in the marketplace, there was some concern that we would hit a dry spell at the Thanksgiving box office, which would be unfortunate given the great resurgence we’ve had at the domestic box office, now coursing to $9B by the end the holiday with an eye at $10B by the end of the year. Thanks to Lionsgate, Sunrise on the Reaping is going to get us through. With Disney’s Hexed and Universal’s Focker-in-Law expected to post around $45M a piece over the Wednesday-Sunday stretch, it wouldn’t be shocking if Hunger Games takes the lead with $50M+ over the 5-day box office as the franchise typically rallies over the Thanksgiving holiday.

Sources indicate that focus Features/Studio Canal’s highly buzzed Andrew Scott Best Actor movie Elsinore is seeing a solid opening theater average of $40K from 6 theaters in NYC and LA for a 3-day of $240K. Friday was $140K with $33K coming from AMC Lincoln Square and LA’s AMC Grove with $32K. Both had Q&As boosting ticket sales. RT critics are at 87% certified fresh.

Recent findings suggest that sumerian’s acquisition of the Sundance Grand Jury Prize and Audience winning drama Josephine from Beth de Araújo is looking at an estimated $35K Friday and 3-day of $138K at four locations in NY and LA. AMC Burbank is leading the way with $15K yesterday. The Channing Tatum and Gemma Chan starring pic is 97% certified fresh with RT critics. Opening per theater for the weekend is $34,5K.

According to recent reports, mubi has the Andrey Zvyagintsev directed crime thriller Minotaur which is France’s international film Oscar entry. The pic did $52K yesterday for what looks to be an estimated $123K opening at six sites in NY, LA, Toronto, San Francisco and Chicago. LA and NY are driving the ship with the latter’s Angelika Film Center minting $21K on Friday. The pic won Cannes’ Grand Prize of the Festival. Pic is 96% certified fresh with critics.

Sources indicate that FRIDAY MIDDAY: Lionsgate’s The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping is heading for the fourth highest opening for the Suzanne Collins franchise as of now with $110M stateside at 4,108 theaters after a Friday that’s $51M which includes those $21M previews. If the movie isn’t front-loaded, it has a shot at possibly becoming the third highest North American opening for the franchise.

It has been revealed that the industry overseas outlook is $97M, which if that holds means a $206.7M global opening. That latter number is not according to Lionsgate. A high $80M+ foreign start is within reach.

It has been revealed that top Hunger Games openings at the North American B.O. belong to 2013’s Catching Fire ($70.9M Friday/previews, $158M 3-day); the original 2012 Hunger Games ($67.2M Friday/previews and $152.5M opening), and 2014’s Hunger Games: Mockingjay Part 1 ($55.1M Friday/previews and $121.8M 3-day). Sunrise on the Reaping is the sixth movie in the Collins’ franchise, the fifth directed by Francis Lawrence. Altogether the previous five movies count $3.3 billion at the worldwide box office.

Again, the jaw drop here is how this franchise turned its fortunes upward after hitting an all-time low in its opening three years ago with Hunger Games: Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes ($44.6M). Comps to other sixthquels are hard, and the opening jump between Songbirds & Sunrise is +147% — which is unheard of. The surge in domestic openings between Christopher Nolan’s Batman Begins and Dark Knight was +225%.

Among all openings in November at the domestic B.O., Sunrise on the Reaping is currently 13th in a list of 16 movies that have bowed to over $100M for the month.

It has been revealed that relishMix beams that the great word-of-mouth that the pic has “book loyalists showing up in full force, insisting this adaptation finally respects the source material. There’s trust running through the comments, ‘Director Francis Lawrence’s track record and the franchise’s unbroken prequel streak as reasons to believe this one sticks the landing,’ and, ‘We’ll need therapy after this,’ read as proof of the story’s emotional weight. Comments marvel, ‘Dang from Voldemort, Moriarty, Hades, and Ramses to President Snow, Ralph Fiennes catching literary villain roles like Pokémon.’ Others draw sharper comparison, saying ‘this is like the and/or of the Hunger Games I feel it, I know it, I read the book and they are going to break your heart.'”.

Recent findings suggest that overall social media reach is 652M across TikTok, YouTube, Instagram, X and Facebook which is not far from The Odyssey‘s pre-opening reach at 680M and +66% above where Hunger Games: Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes was in its social media universe, bowing shortly after the actors strike ended (393M). That 652M reach for Sunrise on the Reaping is 95% above other action-sci-fi-fantasy sub-genre features.

“Hunger Games cast activation index clocks 21 of 24 cast/creators activated with 40.4M total fans,” adds RelishMix in their weekly report.

“Notably, Jennifer Lawrence and her newly rebooted Instagram with 9.2M fans activated a video from Fallon shot in an elevator at 30 Rock with 25+M views and 40+M views on the Fallon IG. Peter Farrelly’s I Play Rocky from Amazon MGM Studios is looking at $10M in second place after a $3.9M Friday in its third frame 2,477 wide break and a running cume of $11M by EOD Sunday. The exits are excellent, so let’s hope there’s long legs on this Sylvester Stallone biopic which is 89% with Rotten Tomatoes critics and 98% with moviegoers.

FRIDAY AM AFTER THURSDAY EXCLUSIVE: Lionsgate’s Francis Lawrence directed The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping came in with $21M in overall previews since Wednesday. As we told you, that’s the second best for the Suzanne Collins franchise behind Catching Fire‘s $25.2M in 2013 and the second best for 2026 behind Spider-Man: Brand Fresh Day‘s $72M.

Industry observers note that note that all the movies that have posted $20M+ in previews went on to cross $100M+ in their opening weekends. This is a big deal for Lionsgate following its success with Michael, which went on to make $1 billion at the global box office, one of five movies to clear that threshold this year.

Out of the gate Thursday night, Screen Engine and Rentrak’s PostTrak shows 79% “definite recommend” and 5 stars with a 92% positive for general audiences. Women showed up at 67%, with 38% females under 25 and 29% over 25. Biggest definite recommends are from women under 25 (89%), the 13-17 set (92%) and 18-24 demo (82%). The 18-34 showed up at a massive 77%. Close to 70% of Thursday night’s audience bought their tickets within the past week or more than a week ago.

Excitement among fans was apparent a year ago this week, when Lionsgate dropped the first trailer for Sunrise on the Reaping: It went on to clock 109M views in its first 24 hours, becoming the second-most viewed trailer for Lionsgate after Michael‘s 116M global view traffic.

In a recent development, EXCLUSIVE: No Wicked, no Moana, no problem, because Lionsgate is saving the Thanksgiving week box office with The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, which is posting $21.25M in previews, the second-best ever for the franchise behind 2013’s Hunger Games: Catching Fire, which lit $25.2M in its previews. Sunrise‘s money is currently the second-best previews YTD after Sony’s Spider-Man: Brand Newly introduced Day ($72M, $360M) and ahead of Universal’s The Odyssey ($17.6M previews, $123.5M opening).

RELATED: All The Best Picture Oscar Winners – Photo Gallery.

Other previews that Sunrise on the Reaping is beating include Universal’s Wicked from two years ($19.2M; $112.5M opening); for the longest time we heard that the latest feature take of a Suzanne Collins novel was outstripping the presales of that female-skewing musical starring Ariana Grande and Cynthia Erivo. It’s also ahead of Lionsgate’s Michael ($12.6M previews, $97.2M opening), The Devil Wears Prada 2 ($10M, $76.7M opening) and light years ahead of the previous Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes ($5.75M previews, $44.6M opening), which had its campaign impacted by the 2023 actors strike, not to mention the Collins novel about the origins of Coriolanus Snow wasn’t a fan fave. Sunrise on the Reaping was beloved by fans in its early story about the Woody Harrelson mentor character, Haymitch Abernathy.

When it comes to the all-time preview record for a Lionsgate title, that belongs to The Twilight Saga: Breaking Dawn – Part 2, which made $30.4M from midnight highlights leading to a $141M opening back in mid-November 2012.

RELATED: All The Best Actress Oscar Winners – Photo Gallery.

Now, Sunrise on the Reaping‘s advance money was minted with $5M via early access PLF showtimes on Wednesday, with another $16.25M collected tonight per sources. Catching Fire‘s back in the day began warming up with 10 p.m. Thursday night reveals. Note that Wicked‘s previews were composed of Amazon promotional screenings, Wednesday night PLF shows and an $8M Thursday.

With a great preview start, it’s fair to say that a $100M opening is well in store for the net-$150M priced Sunrise on the Reaping, especially with a 95% audience score on Rotten Tomatoes, which is the best ever in the franchise ahead of Catching Fire (89%), Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes (89%), Hunger Games (81%), Mockingjay Part 2 (71%), and Mockingjay Part 1 (66%).

Overseas, industry projects have risen from a $70M forecast to $86M opening.

Sources indicate that critics aren’t hot on the fifth Hunger Games movie from director Francis Lawrence (the original 2012 movie was helmed by Gary Ross) with an RT score of 68% fresh. However, even if Katniss was shooting Cupid’s arrows at critics, they’d still play hard to get, for the best reviews in the series were a a while ago with Catching Fire (90% certified fresh) and Hunger Games (85% certified fresh). Ever since the Mockingjays (both at 70%), critics’ love for Hunger Games has waned with Songbirds and Snakes being the worst reviewed in franchise at 64%.

The Hunger Games franchise through its five previous movies has minted $3.3 billion at the global box office.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that netflix's newest streaming hit, The Body, is drawing in millions of viewers, great reviews, and a gaggle of protests from people who didn't much care for the trailer. But if your lesbian-forward supernatural horror series isn't drawing cries of "blasphemy!"...what are you even doing? In that spirit, we'll conjure up some other highlights dealing with the (extremely) dark side of high school.

According to recent reports, this time-hopping survival drama is about a group of teenage girls who are stranded in the wilderness in 1996 and do terrible things to survive—the extent of which we only learn about via flashbacks from the present day, where the events of 19 months spent in the wild continue to resonate. There are ambiguous teases of the supernatural here (much more ambiguous than in The Body), but there's plenty of human-level horror as well. The show explores the nasty things we get up to when in survival mode (whether trapped in the wilds, stuck with other teenagers—or god forbid both at once), while also cynically (but accurately) positing that there's a huge difference between the version of the past we talk about and the one that really happened. Stream Yellowjackets on Paramount+.

Situated between flashbacks and flash-forwards (not entirely unlike Yellowjackets), mystery/thriller The Wilds sees an airplane full of teenage girls crash on the way to an empowerment program in Hawaii. It swiftly becomes clear that the accident was engineered and that the whole thing is some sort of social experiment, and the survivors are forced to compete against each other if they want to live. The show understands the ways in which young women are exploited and expected to compete against each other in the real world, and the ways in which we'll do just about anything when survival is on the line. Stream The Wilds on Prime Video.

Recent findings suggest that when pretty, popular girl Kate Wallis (Olivia Holt) goes missing without a trace in 1993, awkward Jeanette Turner (Chiara Aurelia) steps in to fill the gap, modeling herself after Kate by working her way into the missing girl's social circle and getting close with her boyfriend. That's all going great until Kate reappears two years later, accusing Jeanette of having witnessed the events around her disappearance and keeping quiet. Whoops. There's even more going on, as the show shifts back and forth between 1993, 1994, and 1995 to slowly reveal the missing pieces. Season two takes on a different story set in 1999 and 2000, and the forthcoming (surprise) third season will shake things up again. The emphasis here is on mystery, but it's a show about the aftereffects of trauma and of the dark secrets that can tear families and communities apart. Stream Cruel Summer on Hulu.

Juicy import Elite follows a group of working-class friends who earn scholarships to Las Encinas, a fictional private school that is, in the show’s universe, the most exclusive in Spain. What they find there is snobbery, mystery, murder, and lots and lots of sex (between and among characters of various sexual orientations and numerical groupings). The smart, wonderfully trashy show ran for a shocking (in our modern streaming era) eight seasons, with a couple of regional remakes. There's no supernatural stuff here, but plenty of dark deeds done with youthful vigor. Stream Elite on Netflix.

A teenager, Mae (Madeleine Arthur), is discovered by the side of the road with weird religious symbols carved into her skin. The hospital psychiatrist who treats her (Emily Deschanel) takes pity on, and interest in, Mae, deciding to take her in while arrangements can be made for a more permanent home for the cult escapee. Mae is, after all, level-headed and quiet, and couldn't possibly be any trouble. Hoo boy, yeah, that turns out to be a bad call on the good doctor's part. Stream Devil in Ohio on Netflix.

A different type of blasphemy at play here, in that Joan Lindsay's novel was already adapted brilliantly by Peter Weir in 1975, in a film often referred to as the greatest to come out of Australia. And yet, this Natalie Dormer-lead take is an achievement in its own right, the extended running time of a miniseries offering up more time to sit with the story's deliberately ineffable mysteries. Dormer plays Hester Appleyard, headmistress of a school for young ladies in the Australian bush. It's going well until a Valentine's Day picnic to the title's Hanging Rock sees three students and a governess disappear, impossibly, without a trace, bringing about the slow unravelling of pretty much everyone left behind. Stream Picnic at Hanging Rock on Prime Video and Tubi.

Mariam (Andria Tayeh) is brutally bullied by the cool clique at her private school in this Jordanian import, a high school drama that's both universal and distinctly Muslim in character. Fed up, Mariam convinces a couple of similarly outcast friends to join forces with her in a revenge plot that quickly gets out of hand. The show deals with Jordanian-style patriarchy head-on, without drawing any easy conclusions about its characters—Mariam catfishes one of her bullies and convinces her to send a revealing picture, one that she immediately posts, exploiting the very same repressive cultural elements that she claims to deplore. It's a smart, realist drama with soapy elements and nothing by way of the supernatural, but it's still a very sharp picture of the extremely cutthroat nature of high school life. Stream AlRawabi School for Girls on Netflix.

It has been revealed that peyton List stars as Maddie, a teenager in small-town Wisconsin for whom her death is very much just the beginning. Stuck in a high school in the afterlife (because hell is definitely for children), she goes on a journey to solve her own murder while uncovering secrets and lies in both worlds. It all sounds a bit grim, but the show has a sense of fun about it: While Maddie does develop the ability to communicate with the living, her world is populated by ghost teens from various eras and generations, with customs, mores, and cliques having developed in ghost high school just as in our world. Stream School Spirits on Paramount+.

In a recent development, the latest Girigo app, claiming to grant wishes, sounds like harmless fun. Except, of course, that the things that teenagers want aren't always beneficent, and the app has already been the conduit for some incredibly dark deeds by the time it gets into the hands of the five high schoolers who find themselves caught in a Ring-like web of shamanistic horror and death countdowns. This is why we tell you to put your phones down once in a while... Stream If Wishes Could Kill on Netflix.

Sources indicate that four one-time best friends reunite at Rosewood High School a year after the disappearance of the leader of their little clique, all having received threatening messages from the mysterious "A," who knows everything they did last summer...and pretty much all the rest of the time. Shoplifting, parents having affairs, students hooking up with teachers—you name it, it's happening in town, and A knows it all. After the prime suspect turns up dead, the girls are caught in the killer's web while trying to keep their secrets hidden. If seven juicy seasons and three A's aren't enough for you, there are three spin-offs. Stream Pretty Little Liars on Hulu and HBO Max.

Tech Report: The Transvoxel Algorithm

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (815 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Transvoxel

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Transvoxel Algorithm is a method for seamlessly stitching together neighboring triangle meshes generated from voxel data at differing resolutions so that level of detail (LOD) can be used with large voxel-based datasets such as volumetric terrain in next-generation video games.
  • In a recent development, voxel-based terrain systems are increasing in popularity because they remove the topographical limitations of conventional elevation-based terrain systems and provide the ability to create more complex structures like caves, overhangs, and arches.
  • Triangle meshes for adjacent voxel terrain blocks are rendered at two different resolutions near a cave entrance.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Transvoxel Algorithm is a method for seamlessly stitching together neighboring triangle meshes generated from voxel data at differing resolutions so that level of detail (LOD) can be used with large voxel-based datasets such as volumetric terrain in next-generation video games. The algorithm was invented by Eric Lengyel in 2009 and implemented in the C4 Engine. This web page provides a high-level overview of the Transvoxel Algorithm, links to additional information, and data tables that can assist in an implementation.

In a recent development, voxel-based terrain systems are increasing in popularity because they remove the topographical limitations of conventional elevation-based terrain systems and provide the ability to create more complex structures like caves, overhangs, and arches. Triangle meshes are typically generated from voxel data using the Marching Cubes algorithm, and the larger numbers of triangles that it generates makes a level-of-detail (LOD) system even more important for high-performance rendering of large terrains. A natural way to implement level of detail for voxel-based terrain is to simply triangulate the voxel data at multiple resolutions, but this leads to the well-known problem of cracks forming along the boundary between meshes representing different resolutions, as shown in Figure 1. While it is relatively simple to patch these types of cracks in a robust manner for elevation-based terrain, the topographical freedom allowed by voxel-based terrain makes the patching process vastly more difficult because the structure of edge mismatches on the boundary plane can be much more complex. The Transvoxel Algorithm introduces the concept of a “transition cell” to smoothly and seamlessly connect voxel terrain meshes across multiresolution boundaries. The algorithm is designed so that only local voxel data is required for each transition cell, and this allows fast retriangulation in cases where the voxel data is dynamically changing in a real-time application.

Figure 1. Triangle meshes for adjacent voxel terrain blocks are rendered at two different resolutions near a cave entrance. (a) Cracks are visible along the boundary between the blocks, allowing the sky in the background to show through, and a large hole appears where the terrain surface is nearly tangent to the boundary plane between the blocks. (b) A wireframe is overlaid to show the triangles generated by Marching Cubes. (c) The surfaces of differing resolutions are seamlessly joined by triangles generated for transition cells using the Transvoxel Algorithm, which follows in the footsteps of Marching Cubes but operates on an alternate arrangement of voxels at the boundary between cells of different resolutions. (d) The wireframe overlay reveals the triangles corresponding to the transition cells.

The Transvoxel Algorithm works by inserting special transition cells in between regular cells along the boundary between voxel data sampled at one resolution and voxel data sampled at exactly half that resolution. Instead of considering all possible combinations of voxel state for both the full-resolution and half-resolution data at a transition boundary, which would require that approximately 1.2 million cases be handled, we consider only nine samples of the high-resolution data. This gives us a much more manageable 512 cases to handle, and these cases happen to fall into the 73 equivalence classes shown in Figure 2. Every transition cell is filled with one of these triangle patterns in order to perfectly fill the seams, cracks, and holes that appear between meshes of different resolutions, as was done for the cave in Figure 1.

Recent findings suggest that in Figure 2, black dots represent voxels that lie inside solid space, and corners without a dot represent voxels that lie outside in empty space. Green triangles are front-facing polygons, and red triangles are back-facing polygons.

Get print version (18 × 24 inch wall poster).

Figure 2. These are the 73 equivalence classes into which the 512 possible transition cell cases fall.

Sources indicate that like the Marching Cubes algorithm, the Transvoxel Algorithm is efficiently implemented using a set of look-up tables that provide information about each of the 512 possible cases that can arise. These tables are not easy to generate, so I am providing the tables that I made in the following repository. There are comments in the .cpp file that describe what the numbers mean.

Transvoxel data tables on GitHub.

Recent findings suggest that eric Lengyel’s Dissertation, University of California at Davis, 2010. This dissertation goes into great detail about the Transvoxel Algorithm and multiresolution voxel terrain in general. It also describes how the algorithm can be efficiently implemented.

According to recent reports, lengyel, Eric. “Transition Cells for Dynamic Multiresolution Marching Cubes”. Journal of Graphics, GPU, and Game Tools. Vol. 15, No. 2 (2010), A K Peters. DOI: 10.1080/2151237X.2011.563682.

A complete implementation of the Transvoxel Algorithm is included with the C4 Engine.

Please cite the dissertation in which this algorithm was originally described:.

Industry observers note that electronic products now pack circuits, structures, thermal paths, and packaging into very small spaces. These physical domains interact with one another. A packaging choice can change how a shock load reaches a circuit board. Such interactions are hard to predict. Most are found during physical qualification, late in development. At that stage, the design is mostly fixed. A failure leads to redesign, rebuilds, and retesting. Physical tests give strong evidence of robustness, but they give limited insight into load paths and failure margins. Traditional simulation gives more detail, but it needs specialist skills and long manual setup. This white paper explains how guided virtual validation brings shock and drop assessment into the design phase. It reviews common test configurations, model inputs, and acceptance criteria. A packaged drop case study then indicates how packaging can be optimized across all drop orientations and checked against physical test results.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

My Chemical Romance didn’t waste a minute of their way-too-abbreviated recording career, making one of rock’s last great concept albums on their third try in the studio, 2006’s The Black Parade. It was Tommy in a white belt and eyeliner, vastly expanding the band’s sonic palette beyond the punk-thrash of their first two albums. It felt like the beginning of what should have been a long, ambitious newly introduced phase of My Chem’s career, but instead, they released the underrated Danger Days: The True Lives of the Fabulous Killjoys in 2010 and broke up three years later.

Their welcome return to the road has yet to be accompanied by newly introduced music, but the band — frontman Gerard Way, lead guitarist and backing vocalist Ray Toro, rhythm guitarist Frank Iero, and bassist Mikey Way (drummer Bob Bryar left in 2010 and died in 2024) — is promising that will change soon.

In a recent development, welcome to the Black Parade recently celebrated its 20th anniversary, and a upcoming vinyl edition made a surprise Number One debut. That album’s producer, Rob Cavallo (who also worked on much of Green Day‘s discography, among many other projects) joined Rolling Stone by Zoom for an in-depth look at the making of a 21st-century rock masterpiece.

According to recent reports, what did My Chem first play for you that got you excited to be involved in this album?They were interviewing other guys as well, but I’ll never forget, ’cause it was so freezing cold in Latest York, and we went to SIR, and they played me a few things. But the one that blew my mind was “Mama.” When I heard that, I remember just jumping off the couch just going, “Oh, my God, you guys. That is so great and original,” and you could tell it was part of a deeper picture of something, even though I was new to the band. It felt notable to me right away that this band was existing on a higher conceptual level.

In a recent development, that song sounds like the Doors version of “Alabama Song.” It’s very un-punk at first, and then it kicks into the—The heavy part, right. Yeah, I kinda likened it in a weird way rhythmically to the Doors. I was also thinking of [the Rolling Stones’] “Mother’s Little Helper.” Almost like you could see the Cossacks-style Russian dancing to it. It’s like this sort of head-bopping thing that just felt very edgy, and very anti-establishment rock in a weird way. It was definitely like the we-don’t-give-a-fuck kind of rock. Recent findings suggest that but then there was this story in there. I was like, “What is this guy going on about? What is happening here? This is heavy stuff.” So that’s why I jumped up off the couch on that song.

Industry observers note that and of course, a lot of the record at that point had not been written. And then I got this call and they noted, “Meet us at this steakhouse near SIR.” And I remember walking there and I thought my legs were gonna freeze off. And then we got in and we had the greatest dinner ever, and they said, “All right, you wanna be our producer?” I said, “Yeah, I do.” And that was it. They decided a couple hours after the first meeting.

Do you think your enthusiasm put it over the top for them? Obviously it couldn’t have hurt that you had just done American Idiot, which had similar levels of ambition.I think I was told that they liked what I said about the music, and they probably liked that I had done two records that I think stood out in their minds. Yeah, I had just done American Idiot, which was of course really big and was working, and I think they liked that. And then I think the other record they mentioned was Jawbreaker, Dear You, which is a band and an album that had an infamous history of being a dismal failure, in a way, commercially when it first came out.

But also then received its just deserts many years later, in the fact that it was now considered one of the seminal emo records of all time. And of course, we all know the history about how the band got back together and then all of a sudden on one show there were 60,000 people singing every word to every song on that record. But at the same time we also know that Kurt Cobain was, like, one of their biggest supporters — they were opening for Nirvana. So it was kinda cool. Industry observers note that how did My Chem define their ambitions on that first day?It wasn’t necessarily something that we actually talked about. I think Gerard [Way] had it in his mind, but a lot of it happened when we went into this place called the Paramour. The band was looking for a place where they could live and work and write.

A sort of haunted mansion, apparently.Oh, it was haunted all right. Crazy stuff was happening all the time. You could just feel the vibes of the insanity that was happening — doors closing by themselves, and probably the eeriest hallway. To this day, I still remember that hallway going down to where the bedrooms were on the top floor, and it just looked like you were in the scariest movie. And the coat of arms and the polar bear, the stuffed polar bear, all the weird stuff that was just everywhere.

In a recent development, and it was also kinda freezing in there. It was such an old building that we had to bring in space heaters, and so a lot of the writing actually ended up taking place over a couple of months in that particular space. And Mikey [Way] eventually, as you probably heard, he had to move out. He couldn’t take it after a while. It was just too scary.

But we had a lot of fun there, and we got a lot of the work done. So the record, I would say, was probably 90 percent written by the time, or 95 percent written by the time we got out of there and headed to the studio. With, of course, the notable exception of the song “Black Parade” itself, that has its own sort of strange and storied history.

While they’re writing in the house, where are you and what are you doing?Every day, Monday through Friday, I’d show up with my engineer, Doug McKean, and I set up some fancy microphones in this giant, crazy living room that they had. The great room in that house looked like it was, like, 1,500 square feet. And we put the band in there with a PA, like a smaller PA, so that we could record whatever the band was writing and doing. So the writing was done almost live.

Sources indicate that gerard liked to just sing over the band. And someone would bring in a riff and we would just start jamming and recording. And the great news is that all of those recordings actually are now available online. I think there was a big box set of these live two-track recordings that are sort of the precursor — they’re the demos that we made the album from.

Recent findings suggest that yeah, those are available to stream now.We put them on these DAT tapes. I had a special digital audio tape recorder, which was basically a tape that would be equivalent to CD quality. We would set about writing and creating and capturing these compositions, and working on the structure of them and what have you, so that we could then go into the studio, which is, of course, radically more expensive, and make the record.

Was Gerard having his night terrors at the house, and did he think they were caused by the house?You’d have to ask him if they were being caused by the house. But one thing for sure is the house had an effect on him, because it was a strangely haunted, dark place.

Industry observers note that and he did talk about the night terrors, and he did talk about that he was going through a lot of things at that particular time. I think he was, like, a young man at the cusp at that time. I didn’t know where he was with his significant-other situation. There might have been something going on there. I don’t really know. But I would say this, I could tell he had a great record in him.

They’re a very emotional band, and they’re the nicest people. They’re very cordial to each other, and everything is on the up and up. But they also kinda would wear their hearts on their sleeves; if they were upset about something else in life, you could hear about it, you know? I was there to be very supportive. But the one thing for sure is that nothing ever got in the way of the music. We went to work. It was serious. We seriously worked 10, 12 hours a day.

When Mikey has to leave because it’s psychologically oppressive, does it make anyone else wonder, “Hey, maybe we should get the hell out of here too?”I think there was some conversation about it, but I also think, certainly, there were financial considerations. I think that there was a lease that we had to let expire, and, like, where were they gonna stay if they go, and what other money is that? ‘Cause we were responsible and [we were] on a budget.

And you’re writing all this great stuff, so why not stay?That’s the other thing. The vibe in the daytime and into the evening, in terms of getting work done, it was working. You’re really correct on that.

Recent findings suggest that so you go in the studio. Let’s talk about “Welcome to the Black Parade,” which started as “The Five of Us Are Dying.”So what was interesting is that it was a song that we thought was good, and we knew we were gonna put it on the record.

In a recent development, but there [were] two things about it that kinda didn’t work.
