And then the other thing was the chords on the chorus were… If you listen to “Five of Us Are Dying,” you’ll see that the chord structure was slightly different, and it didn’t feel like a hit record. It just felt like an OK song.

Industry observers note that so what happened?I really gotta give credit to Gerard and the band. So I, for whatever reason, one day showed up to the studio early. And nobody was around, and we were at the Eldorado Studio in Burbank. And so I would sometimes sit there and just play the piano in the morning and just get my ears opened up and refreshed or whatever.

And lo and behold, Gerard shows up five minutes later. We were a good half an hour, 40 minutes before everybody. And so I’m just playing the piano, and he liked that ’cause I could play Queen songs and whatever. I remember him pointing at me once when we were up at the Paramour mansion, and I started playing things. He goes, “Oh, hey, listen to Cavallo. He can actually do shit on the piano. We should use that.”.

So now here we are, like a month or two later, and we’re at Eldorado. And he goes to me, “Can you play…” And he cited the graduation theme, like “Pomp and Circumstance.” He goes, “But can you do that, but just make it go down?” And so I had one of those weird moments where I said to myself, “Don’t think, just play.” And my fingers literally started playing, and Gerard almost immediately started singing, “When I was a young boy…” And it was really a magical thing, and we had a little voice note recorder or voice memo thingy, and we recorded it, and he goes, “OK, so this is the parade.” We were thinking of it as being, like, an interstitial moment in the record where you would hear a parade from half a mile away or a quarter mile away, and it’d start very light.

Recent findings suggest that that’s why I played it with one finger at first. And then I started playing it with two hands, and then I started playing it as big as I could make it — loud. And then, now that the parade has passed you, it gets quieter again, right? So I worked it all the way back up to just the single-note thing, right? And the thing probably lasted two, two and a half minutes. And so then the idea was, OK, we’re gonna have marching bands, and we’re gonna have orchestral percussion and the horns and the whole thing.

But I went away with my family for a few days, and when I got back on Monday, Gerard claims, “You gotta hear this. You gotta hear this.” And what they had done was they had taken the first half of “The Black Parade” and attached it to what would become the extended intro to [“The Five of Us Are Dying”]. And I was like, “Oh, my God, that totally works.”.

What else did they change?I think Ray [Toro] or somebody fixed the chords on the chorus. The chorus became much more sing-along. And then all of a sudden that made sense. But what it really also did was, because we had a marching band and giant orchestrations in the intro, it afforded us the ability for me as a producer to say, “Now I can afford to have all these big orchestrations and all those things during the body of the song,” which normally you wouldn’t have a reason to do. It raised the bar of the song creatively to such a level that we could do something that in a weird way maybe on a pop-punk record had not been done before.

Recent findings suggest that I remember I played it for one of my great mentors, Lenny Waronker, who was the longtime president of Warner’s, famous dude, and he went, “Holy shit. What the hell is that? I’ve never heard anything like that.” It actually worked, you know? So I remember thinking, “Wow, Lenny likes it. Yay.”.

Let’s talk about “Teenagers.”He really did mean what he was saying, but sometimes an artist can do what they would call a throwaway. Because he was concerned with — this is when Columbine happened, and kids were getting violent. And that song almost didn’t make the record.

Sources indicate that what happened was there were some people that thought, “This is like an old-school rock & roll song.” And the argument was, “Why are we doing an old rock & roll song?” Like what they call a I-IV-V [chord-progression] song, like Chuck Berry. But what’s great about that is that my argument was, how do you write a contemporary I-IV-V song that is so great? And have the lyric be that meaningful? To me, that was the argument to do it. Right?

Industry observers note that it’s just an key record. And to be fair, it worked out, you know? Everybody agreed. It took a week or two. It was definitely a conversation, ’cause if you do listen to the record, I admit that it is an outlier on the album.

But there was just something so compelling about that. At the beginning, it wasn’t obvious even how to cut it, but we did. I remember we all took turns at, “What should the bass be like?” You know? And I think Ray actually kinda figured it out. But anyway, the point is that the record came out and look what happened. It just exploded.

I believe it was your phone call that got Liza Minnelli on “Mama.”Yeah, so we were talking about, on “Mama,” who should play Mother War? The idea of this was like Mother War is this weird character. And there was a wonderful lady — Liz Rosenberg, Madonna’s publicist. And so I was kicking around Warner’s, like, does anybody know Liza Minnelli? I think it was Gerard’s idea. It was definitely the band’s idea. And I said, “Let me see if I can get it.” So I called Liz Rosenberg and she said, “I can do it. I think I can get her.” And anyways, the fucking miracles, she did it. She got her.

According to recent reports, what was working with Liza like?One of the things that was so great about Liza is that she was so consummately professional that we got the takes that we wanted, and she was not done. She was like, “No, I need to keep doing this. Let me keep trying. Let me perfect this. Let me get this crying part down. Let me figure out how I can truly nail this performance.” And her attention to detail, I have to say, I was just so blown away by her.

We haven’t necessarily had a ton of great guitar solo albums this century, but this is definitely one of them. Do any memories stand out?Both Ray and Frank [Iero] are great guitar players, and they did amazing things. But the thing that always stands out is the song “Dead!” And that first solo, because what’s crazy about that solo is that that happened by accident. It was supposed to just be the chords, and we weren’t gonna actually have a solo there. The chords were, like, enough.

Industry observers note that but Ray being as great guitar player as he is, I think we just hit record or whatever, and he had the guitar in his hand, and he just ripped that solo, actually just as like a warmup or something. And we went, “We gotta use it. We gotta use it,” and he was like, “No, no. We can’t use it. We can’t use that. That’s just…” And then we printed a rough mix of the whole thing and we kept living with it, and over the course of the next week or two, I was like, “Ray, we gotta use it. It’s too good.” And eventually he said, “OK, fuck, we’ll use the solo.” But what’s amazing is it shows you how good a player he is, because that was something that was — how do I explain it? — an off-the-cuff, unplanned solo. How good is that? That this guy could just do that without even thinking about it.

Recent findings suggest that the band hung out in a house for two months writing, and then recorded at a great studio. Would it be very difficult to get all that together in the current music industry, on a major label?Yes and no. It’s funny, if you look at the budgets back then for a band like that and the way the music business is now, it’s really comparing apples and oranges, right? I don’t think that Paramour was, like, that expensive, because if it’s 15 or 20 grand a month and you do it for two months, and you’re housing like five, six, seven guys, that’s actually cheap. And also rehearsing. That’s actually kinda inexpensive if you’re thinking about it in terms of real estate. If you were to pay a rehearsal place and hotels and all that kind of stuff, it’d be a lot more.

And then we went to Eldorado, which was not an A++ expensive three-grand-a-day place. It was actually more in the middle level. Like $1,200 or so — and I think we were able to crank that album out in, tops, two and a half months. So 10 weeks or something. That was a budget-conscious record, which made sense because they were a band on their way up. The prior record did well, but it wasn’t like there was like oodles of money running around all over the place.

I was kinda known as a producer that could stay on budget. So we probably did this one in the $200,000 to $250,000 range, but that’s just a total fucking guess.

Was there any sense, working on Black Parade, that this was a band about to make just one more album and then not make one for a very long time?There was no indication during making Black Parade that it was gonna be only one more album, but there was indication near the end of Danger Days that there were feelings afoot, shall we say.

It has been revealed that the band has said there’s a new album coming. Are you working with them now?No, I was supposed to go see them at the Hollywood Bowl, and then I got the flu, so I didn’t go. But I’ve been in contact with Ray and Mikey. I really don’t know what their intends are. Sources indicate that meanwhile, you have a hit record again, 20 years later. It just reveals you the state of the music business being in such a weird place. But it’s also a good place. When I looked at it, just the idea that there’s a latest piece of vinyl — I think when a band is really good and makes really good music and there’s also a bit of a scarcity about it, right? They haven’t made music in a long time. You put out this new piece of product and the hardcore fans will buy. I actually bought one myself the other day. I was at Amoeba and I said, “You know what? I should just buy one for good luck.”.

It has been revealed that you pushed it over the top. It would’ve been Number Two if you didn’t jump in there.I bought a whole one copy at $40. It’s amazing, and they sold something like, I think, 70,000 of them or something. And I think that was just in the United States, unless that was worldwide, I don’t know. But I also know it was Number One in the U.K. But what’s interesting is those numbers are, in a weird way, like old-school, unheard-of numbers, because if you sell 70,000 at $40 list price, the gross is 2.8 million bucks.

  • It has been revealed that it premiered quietly on Netflix back in February, earned glowing reviews, and then more or less vanished, skipped by audiences and passed over for a second season despite being one of the smartest things the streamer put out all year.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that too many murder mysteries telegraph their twists a mile away. This scrappy little series takes a familiar setup and pushes it somewhere much weirder and funnier than you’d expect. Three women in their late 30s reunite for the funeral of a childhood friend, only to start suspecting her death was no accident. That’s how “How to Get to Heaven from Belfast” opens — and it might just be the funniest, most underrated show most people never bothered to watch this year.

It has been revealed that it premiered quietly on Netflix back in February, earned glowing reviews, and then more or less vanished, skipped by audiences and passed over for a second season despite being one of the smartest things the streamer put out all year. The show comes from Lisa McGee, the creator of the beloved “Derry Girls,” though you shouldn't walk in expecting more Catholic-schoolgirl hijinks. This is a darker, twistier beast: a genuine murder mystery that happens to be laugh-out-loud funny, trading teenage chaos for middle-aged mayhem. Across eight tightly wound episodes, McGee’s razor-sharp writing and a trio of electric lead performances turn a simple whodunit into a story about grief, friendship, and the secrets we bury—all set to a killer ’90s soundtrack.

If you’re ready for a wickedly funny mystery that’ll have you laughing one minute and gut-punched the next, keep reading.

According to recent reports, saoirse (Roisin Gallagher), Robyn (Sinéad Keenan), and Dara (Caoilfhionn Dunne) were inseparable as teenagers in Belfast, part of a tight-knit group of four. Now in their late 30s, they’ve drifted apart and moved on with their lives — until the sudden death of the fourth member of their group, Greta, brings them back together for her funeral.

Recent findings suggest that what should be a simple reunion quickly spirals into something a lot weirder. The women start to suspect that Greta’s death wasn’t the accident everyone’s calling it. In fact, it may tie directly to a secret from their shared past, one they’ve spent years trying to forget.

Determined to find out what really happened, the trio introduces an investigation that takes them well beyond Belfast — even landing them at a resort in Portugal — as the past they’ve been outrunning finally catches up with them.

Recent findings suggest that I’ll keep this simple: The show is funny, the mystery is sharp and the two actually work in tandem. Most of the credit goes to Lisa McGee’s writing. She pulled off the same balancing act on “Derry Girls,” where the comedy never undercut the emotional gut-punches. Doing it again here with older characters and darker stakes makes the show feel far more grounded than most mysteries in its lane.

Sources indicate that roisin Gallagher, Sinéad Keenan, and Caoilfhionn Dunne play women who’ve known each other since childhood, and you buy it immediately. They bicker, cover for each other, and slip back into old habits the way real lifelong friends do. Their chemistry is electric—and given how much time they spent together on set, it’s easy to believe that bond carried over off-camera.

Best of all, it’s a self-contained eight-episode miniseries, meaning the whole story is here and it actually has an ending—no cliffhangers. You can knock it out in a weekend without worrying about Netflix abruptly pulling the plug on a resolution.

It didn’t get nearly the attention it deserved the first time around, which is exactly why it’s worth seeking out now. If you want a smart, funny mystery you can start and finish without a massive commitment, it’s streaming on Netflix — so make sure to catch it (and “Derry Girls” too, if you haven't already).

Stream "How to Get to Heaven from Belfast" on Netflix.

Industry observers note that upgrade, November 19, 4:46 p.m. ET: The release candidates are now available to public beta testers, with the same build numbers as the developer RCs.

Recent findings suggest that in addition to macOS 27.3 beta 2, Apple is also rolling out the first Release Candidates for macOS Sequoia 15.8.4 and macOS Tahoe 26.7.4. Here are the details.

Two weeks ago, Apple released macOS Tahoe 26.7.3 and Sequoia 15.8.3, along with macOS 27.2.1 Golden Gate, all of which included security fixes related to AirPlay, Bluetooth, and Messages, among others.

Today, the company released the first RCs for macOS Sequoia 15.8.4 and macOS Tahoe 26.7.4, along with the second developer beta for macOS 27.3.

As is usually the case with direct-to-RC rollouts, Apple’s notes mention only that the updates provide ”security fixes for your Mac.” The actual release notes will likely become available soon after Apple officially releases macOS Sequoia 15.8.4 and macOS Tahoe 26.7.4 in the coming weeks.

The build for macOS Sequoia 15.8.4 RC 1 is 24H319, and the build for macOS Tahoe 26.7.4 RC 1 is 25G422.

Industry News: If You Loved 'Yellowjackets,' There's One Movie You Need to Watch Next

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (994 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that yellowjackets is a vibe.
  • Based on the true story of a rugby team whose plane crashed in the Andes Mountains in 1972, Alive will satisfy anyone whose favorite part of Yellowjackets is the core premise: Survivors of a disaster are stranded in the wilderness without supplies, and have to figure out how—and, er, who—they’re going to eat.
  • In a recent development, the survivors are initially as calm and resourceful as someone could be under those circumstances.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that yellowjackets is a vibe. The story of a high school girls’ soccer team that crashes into the wilderness and spends years fending off madness, starvation, and despair (and not always doing a very good job of any of those things) is equal parts funny and terrifying. The dual timelines build tension around the story’s many mysteries, and the complex characters (no one’s completely good or evil on this show) make for a lot of surprising plot swerves that feel grounded despite the supernatural implications all around them. If you’re looking for more of that specific flavor of horror, you should probably watch Alive.

Based on the true story of a rugby team whose plane crashed in the Andes Mountains in 1972, Alive will satisfy anyone whose favorite part of Yellowjackets is the core premise: Survivors of a disaster are stranded in the wilderness without supplies, and have to figure out how—and, er, who—they’re going to eat.

In a recent development, the survivors are initially as calm and resourceful as someone could be under those circumstances. They use the wrecked plane as shelter in the withering cold, they scavenge for anything that could be useful, and they ration out the only food they have: Some chocolates and a case of wine. But an early mistake leaves them without any food at all, and slowly they come to the sickening realization that their best chance at survival is to treat the corpses of their friends and families scattered around the crash site as a food source.

It has been revealed that there’s no supernatural aspect, but the story has a similar tone of desperation and despair as Yellowjackets. These are people determined to survive in an impossible situation, and they do things that no one outside of their shared experience could possibly understand. The real-life origins of the story add a sense of horror that more than matches the fictional “It” that haunts the girls of Yellowjackets; putting yourself into that very real experience makes it clear just how terrified everyone was. Rent Alive on Prime Video.

If you’re craving more cannibals, cults, and crazies at the mercy of nature itself, here are a few more movies you should check out.

According to recent reports, if you want to watch a movie that is essentially an adaptation of Yellowjackets, check out Eden. Even though it was released years before the show, the stories are so similar (albeit largely gender-flipped) that the producers of Eden actually sued, claiming plagiarism (they lost). In the film, a men’s soccer team (and two women on the same plane) crash-land on a deserted island, and as they fight for survival, things descend into, yes, madness and cannibalism as the survivors suffer dwindling food and water supplies and the rise of two violently opposed factions. It’s not nearly as deeply imagined as Yellowjackets, and it doesn’t have the supernatural hints of the show, but if you want a truly similar story, it’s a good choice. Stream Eden on The Roku Channel, Hoopla, or Tubi, or rent it on Prime Video.

Recent findings suggest that you obviously cannot discuss Yellowjackets without discussing Lord of the Flies, William Golding’s 1954 novel about a group of schoolboys who descend into brutality and savagery when they’re stranded on a deserted island. The book has been adapted many times, but the 1963 version directed by Peter Brook is still the best version. Brook managed to elicit remarkably naturalistic performances from his young actors, giving the story a realistic tone that is somehow more terrifying than any amount of horror vibes. Stream Lord of the Flies on Kanopy or rent it on Prime Video.

A slower and more haunting story, Picnic at Hanging Rock explores some of the same themes as Yellowjackets in an entirely different way. On Valentine’s Day in the year 1900, several students and teachers from an all-girls private school in Victoria, Australia, head to Hanging Rock for a picnic. Four students head off to explore and fall inexplicably asleep, and then three vanish, along with one of the teachers. Dreamy and drenched in dread, the story never offers any easy answers, and it explores themes of invading natural areas where you’re not wanted, burgeoning (and confusing) adolescent sexuality, and how our fear of the unknowable warps our perspective and often diminishes our humanity. Stream Picnic at Hanging Rock on HBO Max or rent it on Prime Video.

You can never really go wrong with a Hitchcock film, and if you’re looking for another story about a disparate group of people forced to make terrifying decisions in order to survive, watch Lifeboat (based on a story by John Steinbeck). One of the director’s most underrated films, it’s the story of a group of survivors in a lifeboat after a German U-boat sinks their ship during World War II (including one survivor from the German boat). It’s a masterful suspense engine that’s not afraid to have its characters discuss the moral and ethical quandaries facing them as they struggle to survive and maintain their humanity under a constant threat of death. Stream Lifeboat on Hoopla or rent it on Prime Video.

If you love the supernatural aspects of Yellowjackets as the girls come to believe a force they call “It” is out in the woods, check out The Ritual. Four friends embark on a hike in the wilds of northern Sweden to honor their deceased friend. When one of them is injured, they leave the marked trail to take a shortcut through the forest—where they are soon forced to shelter in an abandoned cabin, just like the Yellowjackets—and things begin to slide into the terrifying when they encounter a cult worshipping an ancient deity that grants them immortality in exchange for human sacrifices. It’s as if the show was condensed to an hour-and-a-half and the terror quotient was turned way, way up. Stream The Ritual on Netflix.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that bloomberg reports that Apple is hiring engineers to develop an autonomous AI agent capable of browsing the web, writing code, and controlling apps on behalf of users. Here are the details.

In a report published today, Bloomberg notes that newly introduced job listings on Apple’s website indicate the tech giant’s efforts to develop an autonomous AI agent capable of performing complex tasks on the user’s behalf.

Since the breakout success of OpenClaw, autonomous AI agents have become increasingly popular, with companies such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, and SpaceXSI among those offering their own solutions.

The increasing popularity of these agents has put Apple under pressure to catch up, while the company has also introduced new restrictions on how third-party AI agents can access and control Macs.

Last month, Apple announced aims to tighten macOS privacy controls around Full Disk Access, with changes introduced in the macOS 27.3 beta that give owners more granular control over which apps and information third-party AI agents can access.

Over at the App Store, Meta’s Muse has become one of the fastest-growing apps in US history, surpassing 10 million downloads in just 40 days, according to Sensor Tower, and spending weeks at the top of the charts. As of today, it sits at No. 2 among free apps, behind TikTok.

And while there are differences in how phone-based and computer-based agents operate, these systems can usually work together, coordinating tasks across devices and apps to accomplish increasingly complex goals.

Back to Bloomberg’s report, it notes Apple recently posted new job listings that offer a closer look at its plans to develop autonomous AI agents:.

In one, Apple remarked it’s seeking a senior engineering manager for a proactive, agentic AI assistant. The system will write code, browse the web, control apps and navigate devices on a user’s behalf, according to the post.

One job listing, which is for “Senior Engineering Manager, Agentic AI – Proactive,” features the following summary:.

In a recent development, “Imagine an AI agent that can use a computer the way a capable person does. It browses the web, works across apps, runs commands, writes and debugs code, and calls services, and it chooses the right tool for each step. It does all this privately and with the polish people expect from Apple. Our team is building the foundation for that future, and we’re looking for a senior engineering leader to make it real.”.

The listing also notes that Apple is building agents that can “strategy and carry out multi-step tasks across apps, browsers, command lines, code, and APIs, and they can coordinate specialized sub-agents along the way,” much like existing solutions from frontier AI labs.

In a recent development, today’s report on the fresh job listings comes just days after Bloomberg reported that Apple wants to make Siri more like an autonomous AI agent, with the ability to proactively carry out tasks without requiring owners to initiate every step. According to Mark Gurman, the tech giant could introduce these capabilities as soon as next year.

With the upcoming job listings, Apple has offered a more detailed look at its plans for autonomous AI agents, although the language suggests that development is still in its early stages.

Of course, given how quickly the technology is evolving, the landscape could look very different by the time Apple is ready to introduce its own solution next year, much like how the industry had already moved toward autonomous agents by the time Apple finally released its long-awaited Siri AI overhaul.

  • With advice from two sleep experts, we're exploring why bedroom environment matters, what to consider changing and why those adjustments are important for sleep.

Industry observers note that here at Tom's Guide, we know that nighttime wake-ups are a significant problem for many people. Which is why, if you've found yourself repeatedly awake at 3 a.m. and unable to fall back to sleep, it's time to take a look around your bedroom.

Industry observers note that you might not realize it, but elements of your sleep space could be contributing to your disrupted rest — from technology and light usage, to elements of your bed itself. The simple act of removing them might be the difference between another broken night's rest and staying asleep all night.

With advice from two sleep experts, we're exploring why bedroom environment matters, what to consider changing and why those adjustments are important for sleep.

Industry observers note that temperature, light and sound pollution can all stop you from staying asleep all night."People sleep better when it's dark, when it's quiet, when it's cool, when it's free of disturbances [and] when it's safe, notes Dr. Aric Prather, sleep scientist and expert at UCSF and BetterSleep. "And so, trying to optimize that environment on those facets, is certainly a step towards a better night of sleep.".

Sources indicate that while 3 a.m. wake ups have a variety of causes, there are environmental factors that can contribute to them happening, and keep you awake. Here, we explain what they are, and how removing certain items from your room can help.

Both experts we spoke to advised, where possible, to keep work outside of the bedroom. And since many of us work on computers or laptops at home, removing these from your sleep space can help eliminate distracting light sources and potential stress they're associated with.

Sources indicate that the Sleep Foundation points out that having electronics near the bed can contribute to nighttime wakeups through the noise and light they can emit. So, we asked Heather Darwall-Smith, a UKCP psychotherapist specializing in sleep and author of The Science of Sleep, if laptops in the bedroom can be impactful on sleep, through the association with work or light from charging cables.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

It has been revealed that if it's your work laptop and it's near your bed and you see the light [this can prompt], 'Oh, that's my work laptop. Oh, God, did I send that email?'.

"It's both," she notes. "The mind needs to know the day is done. It's like putting work away. It's creating that boundary between work and home," she explains.

Recent findings suggest that dr. Prather also points out that waking and seeing a light from a laptop charging cable can carry anxiety. "Because if it's your work laptop and it's near your bed and you see the light [this can prompt], 'Oh, that's my work laptop. Oh, God, did I send that email?'" he says, adding that it can also lead to ruminating over the next day being a work day.

He adds that "some people's computers have fans that are constantly running and there's heat coming out of them. So that can change the the temperature of the room or the temperature near their body.".

As temperatures drop over the winter, keeping your heating on overnight can appear to be a sensible way to combat the seasonal chill — but being mindful of temperature is key to avoiding waking up.

Industry observers note that “High temperatures in your bedroom can interfere with your body’s natural cooling process, which is essential for falling and staying asleep,” Dr. Hannah Patel previously explained.

But turning your heating off in the lead-up to bedtime — ideally anytime from around 9 p.m. (though that's not a hard and fast rule if you're an early bird or a night owl!) — you'll allow your bedroom time to cool down.

Similarly, sleeping with an electric blanket is another nighttime practice to be particularly careful with.

Not only is it unsafe to keep an electric blanket on all night (the Electrical Safety Foundation International notes they should never be used while sleeping), even modern models with built-in protection to prevent overheating, advise turning off before falling asleep.

Removing your phone from the bedroom is something the Tom's Guide sleep team swears by, in part because expert advice suggests that scrolling your phone late at night can cause a state of mental arousal that may lead to disrupted sleep.

Recent findings suggest that not to mention, a recent study found that every hour spent on screens before bedtime increases the risk of insomnia by a whopping 59%. As Dr. Prather points out, "phones on their own aren't really problematic, but if people can't keep their hands off them, then they are.".

And while the jury is still out on how much blue light from screens is really going to affect your sleep, looking through your phone in the middle of the night can stimulate your brain and prolong awakenings.

However, Darwall-Smith notes that she often finds "people are more stressed by taking the phone out of the bedroom than having it there.".

If that's you, consider "turning off your notifications, thinking about how checking the screen or getting into live activity on your phone is going to keep you awake," the sleep psychotherapist advises.

It's the literal foundation of your sleep, but you might not have considered that your mattress could be playing a significant part in disrupting it.

Waking up with back pain or stiffness, aching shoulders and hips, overheating during the night, tossing and turning, and even waking up coughing and sneezing can all be signs that your mattress is the culprit behind your nighttime wake ups.

"If you're constantly having back pain or your mattress isn't okay... look into it," states Darwall-Smith, though she points out that back pain might be caused by factors outside of your mattress.

According to recent reports, dr. Prather suggests finding a mattress that is "the right comfort for you, and that probably changes as you age," and recommends "one that supports your posture [and] that doesn't cause pain.".

In a recent development, however, as Darwall-Smith notes, "sometimes it's not in [people's] control to change their mattress. So what can you do to make the mattress comfortable? You might want a topper." The best mattress toppers can adjust the comfort and feel of your mattress, and even help with regulating the temperature, all without the cost involved in replacing your existing bed.

Having the wrong pillow for your sleep position, one that has lost it's shape and support, is aggravating allergies or is causing neck pain can all contribute to nighttime wakeups.

Research highlights a relationship between an uncomfortable pillow and poor sleep. One study looking at pillow performance found that everyone "who reported poor sleep quality also reported poor pillow comfort.".

Sheets, meanwhile, might be something of an afterthought, but synthetic fabrics can trap heat and cause sweaty wake-ups — even though the often low price-point can seem attractive.

Recent findings suggest that dr. Prather notes that along with the right mattress, "the quality of the sheets," and their "breathability" as well as "the quality of the pillow, can all contribute to how comfortable people are, and certainly comfort is something that we want to foster when we're trying to get people to sleep well.".

Our best pillows of 2026 can help you determine what's right for you and our guide to the best bed sheets sets of the year has options for different sleep preferences, seasons, and budgets.

While a basic alarm clock can be a better option that relying on your phone, if it's visible from your bed it's potentially making nighttime wakeups worse.

"I prefer people to use actual alarm clocks and to try and find non-alarming alarm clocks," claims Darwall-Smith. However, she adds that "I prefer people not to look at their clock.".

According to research, clock-watching or 'time monitoring behaviour' (TMB) is common in people who experience insomnia, and something that perpetuates the symptoms of the condition.

In a recent development, looking at the clock when you wake during the night is "only bad news" states Dr. Prather. "I deal with people with insomnia, but most people are looking at the clock hoping that it's later in the night than it is. And they're almost always wrong.".

Being aware that it's not as late as you hoped then leads to "an immediate anxiety or frustration or discouragement, which pushes against falling back asleep," he explains.

Obviously, we're not suggesting getting rid of the main light in your bedroom altogether, and living each evening in a state of complete darkness.

But if you find yourself awake during the night? "You should not turn on big lights," says Dr. Prather. "If you can keep it low light, that's certainly better.".

According to recent reports, speaking of light at night, Darwall-Smith explains that "if you're shining light into your brain at 4 a.m., that's not [good]. Because sleep is reset by the light-dark cycle. As we push towards wakefulness, our eyes register light and it's part of what pushes us up into [being] awake.".

However, Dr. Prather cautions against "[sitting] in the dark with your thoughts, usually that isn't a good solution." He recommends activities that are sleep supportive, relaxing and distracting, like reading with a book light, or using a Kindle on low intensity.

Being wide awake in the middle of the night is rarely pleasant, but you don't always have to be concerned by a brief awakening.

Industry observers note that "Waking up during the night is normal... it's part of sleep structure. Especially as people get older, it would be very uncommon for people to not wake up during the middle of the night," states Dr. Prather.

Perfectionism is insomnia's best friend.

Darwall-Smith agrees, adding that, "What we're looking at is the quality of what that waking is. If you get up, wander around, go and have a pee, go back to bed, happy days. You get up and your eyes are peeled to the ceiling and you're freaking out, not so happy days.".

And though we've covered ways you can help your sleep by adjusting your bedroom environment, the experts we spoke to emphasized focusing on what works for you, and not adding stress by focusing on creating a 'perfect' environment. "We're not looking for perfection. We're looking for good enough to sleep better," states Dr. Prather.

Darwall-Smith agrees: "Perfectionism is insomnia's best friend. And if we're rushing around trying to perfect our sleeping conditions, Well, do we really need to? Good enough is good enough.".

We've talked about what to remove, but there are useful products which can help tackle complications with noise, light and comfort that may be impacting your night's rest. You don't need to strive for absolute perfection, consider these as tools for a calmer, more relaxing night. Even better, these three items are all reduced in the Black Friday mattress deals.

50 Years Ago Today: The Beach Boys Play Pivotal ‘Brian’s Back’ Concert in Cincinnati

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • “Brian is the Beach Boys, and we’re his messengers,” Dennis Wilson told People magazine in its August 1976 cover story about the band.
  • Just a few years earlier, the idea of a 1960s has-been group appearing on the cover of a mainstream magazine like People would have seemed absurd, about as likely as Herman’s Hermits or the Dave Clark Five having a major resurgence.
  • The Beach Boys weren’t able to generate much interest in their upcoming work, but their 1960s compilation Endless Summer hit Number One in October 1974.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

“Brian is the Beach Boys, and we’re his messengers,” Dennis Wilson told People magazine in its August 1976 cover story about the band. “We’re thrilled to have him back.”.

Just a few years earlier, the idea of a 1960s has-been group appearing on the cover of a mainstream magazine like People would have seemed absurd, about as likely as Herman’s Hermits or the Dave Clark Five having a major resurgence. But the Beach Boys were the beneficiaries of an enormous nostalgia wave that swept America in the mid-1970s, giving us American Graffiti, Happy Days, Sha Na Na, and Grease.

The Beach Boys weren’t able to generate much interest in their upcoming work, but their 1960s compilation Endless Summer hit Number One in October 1974. As a result, they dumped most of the recent material from their live repertoire and began playing arenas and even stadiums. “We knocked them dead every time we went out just playing the hits,” Al Jardine told Rolling Stone in 2025. “It allowed us to grow musically at home while we could continue to entertain. It was a nice balance.”.

Recent findings suggest that but by 1976, as Endless Summer mania began petering out, the group needed a new gambit to keep drawing the big crowds. That’s why band manager Steve Love decided to rouse Brian Wilson from his bed and get him back on the road for the first time since 1964, generating a groundswell of interest in the band.

They promoted the “Brian’s Back” campaign with an NBC television special put together by Lorne Michaels and the original Saturday Night Live team, which included a legendary sketch where Dan Aykroyd and John Belushi storm into Brian’s bedroom as the “Surf Police” and force him to surf for the first time. Annie Leibovitz shot a classic photo of Wilson standing on the sand that day in his blue robe, which appeared on the Nov. 4, 1976, cover of Rolling Stone.

Much of the press outside of Rolling Stone presented Wilson as a goofy eccentric rather than a genuine genius. “Brian is like an amiable child (violence was never one of his symptoms) trying to relearn the simple social graces,” People wrote. “As Brian told Mike [Love] lately, ‘I’m tired of being a failure.'” Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century.

That’s why he decided not only to join the tour but also to produce a new Beach Boys record for the first time since Pet Sounds. The result was the underwhelming 15 Big Ones, which is thin on new originals and heavy on classic covers like Chuck Berry’s “Rock and Roll Music,” the Dixie Cups’ “Chapel of Love,” and Fats Domino’s “Blueberry Hill.”.

In a recent development, brian Wilson was an infrequent presence throughout their shows in the summer of 1976, but fully committed to a winter tour in November and December that followed a two-month hiatus from the road, giving him time to record The Beach Boys Love You. The run of dates began Nov. 22 at the Riverfront Coliseum in Cincinnati, Ohio. Tickets ($7.50 in advance and $8.50 on show day) were unreserved throughout the entire venue, which encouraged fans to line up all day to secure choice spots.

It has been revealed that (Three years later, 11 Who fans were trampled to death when doors opened at this same venue. As a result, Cincinnati outlawed “festival seating” at concerts. The ban wouldn’t be lifted until 2002, when Bruce Springsteen and the E Street Band played an arena show at the U.S. Bank Arena on the Rising tour.).

The Beach Boys show opens with “Wouldn’t It Be Nice” and “Palisades Park,” before Mike Love welcomes “my cousin, the one and only, the magnificent, Brian Wilson!” The crowd roars as he briefly stands up from his perch behind the piano, and then they kick into “Little Deuce Coupe,” “Darlin’,” “In My Room,” and “God Only Knows” while the crowd squeals with delight. Related Content Al Jardine Writes Open Letter to Fellow Beach Boy Mike Love: 'Praying For Your Recovery' Watch John Stamos and the California Sound Substitute for an Ailing Mike Love at Epcot Center The Beach Boys Cancel Final 2026 Concert The Beach Boys Canceled Another Show. A John Stamos Spinoff Group Is Taking Their Spot.

It has been revealed that “Brian was introduced early on in the first set, and most of the crowd stood to acknowledge one of the giants in the history of rock,” noted a review by Dennis Freeman of the News Record. “He didn’t do much, sat impassively behind his piano, but it was key to the group that he was with them again.”.

It has been revealed that after warming the crowd up with oldies, they shifted the show to the present with Al Jardine’s “Back Home” from 15 Substantial Ones. It goes over particularly well with this crowd since it’s all about going back to Jardine’s birthplace of Ohio. “Well, I’m going back this summer to Ohio,” he sings. “I’m going to seek out all my friends I’ve always known/I’m going back to that farm that I remember.” (The song fell out of the band’s rotation in 1978 and wasn’t brought back until a Jardine and the Pet Sounds Band concert in Warren, Ohio, earlier this year.).

“How would you like to hear a couple of new ones we haven’t even done for the public yet?” Mike Love asks the crowd after “Back Home.” “These aren’t even released yet. They will be out in January on our new album. Keep it quiet and don’t go singing to too many groups since they might rip it off. The first one we’re going to do is called ‘Love Is a Woman.’ It sends chills up and down where I won’t tell you. The other one is a song about being on an airplane, so we call it ‘Airplane.’ So listen real good. We hope you like it.”.

According to recent reports, nobody in the arena had any idea they were witnessing a historic moment. This was the first time anyone outside the tight Beach Boys circle had heard even a note of music from The Beach Boys Love You. And even though many fans likely used this as an opportunity to run to the bathroom or grab a beer, the group did a magnificent job on both. “Airplane” is especially transcendent. (Sadly, they’d only play Love You songs a handful more times, and they wouldn’t go near any of it after 1979. It wasn’t until Al Jardine’s inaugural tour with the Pet Sounds Band in 2025 that Love You finally got the treatment it deserved in front of live audiences.).

They win the audience back with a trio of 1960s songs (“Catch a Wave,” “Heroes and Villains,” and “Surfin’ USA”) before introducing the crowd to a local woman named Joellyn Lambert, a former taxi driver who drove Jardine through town in 1970 and inspired his song “Susie Cincinnati.” They recorded it for 15 Big Ones and placed an ad in the local paper prior to the show seeking her out. “Attention!!!” reads the notice. “The Beach Boys are looking for the lady cab driver named Suzi who picked them up six years from the airport. Group wants the person to be guest at their November 22 concert at Riverfront Coliseum.”.

Sources indicate that lambert was stunned when the Cincinnati Post tracked her down and arranged the visit. “I still can’t believe this is really happening,” she told the paper. “I’m now stopped on the street and asked if I’m really ‘Susie Cincinnati.'”.

The deep cuts continued with “It’s Okay,” “A Casual Look,” “Feel Flows,” and “Everyone’s in Love With You” before they closed out the night with a long run of surf-era hits that finished with “Fun, Fun, Fun.”.

“We danced, clapped and sang our way through classic after classic, each song bringing back memories of summers past,” wrote Freeman in the News Record. “‘Surfer Girl’ led into ‘California Girls’ and climaxed with ‘Good Vibrations.’ The audience was pretty young, mainly 18-year-olds, and it was fascinating to note the songs which were greeted with the most applause were the group’s early pre-Beatles hits.”.

Recent findings suggest that “It highlights the timelessness of the Beach Boys’ music,” he continued. “It also indicates that rock critics are wrong that time is up for the group. Even if the apparent re-emergence of the group as a creative force is short-lived, be assured the people will want to hear and see the Beach Boys for a long time to come.”.

In a recent development, they would indeed. But what they didn’t want to hear or see was basically any song they recorded after “Do It Again.” Those fans were in luck since the Beach Boys essentially abandoned any pretense that they were anything but a perpetual-motion 1960s jukebox not long after the 1976 Brian’s Back tour. The idea of seven songs from a upcoming album and another two from an album that wasn’t even released yet, as they did in Cincinnati, soon became unthinkable. Trending Stories Patrick Stewart Cause of Death Revealed Miley Cyrus and Maxx Morando Marry at Palm Springs Wedding Princess of Wales Reflects on Cancer Battle in 'Heal' Documentary Special Boy George on His Israel Trip: 'I Wasn't Able to Not Say Something'.

The Beach Boys returned to Cincinnati on Oct. 10 of this year for a show at the PNC Pavilion at Riverbend. Love is now the final legit member in the touring lineup, and this was a deeply upsetting concert for many fans since it was the first one where he was unable to stand or even sing. He’s been battling a severe health ailment for at least the past year and hasn’t been seen since a show the following night in Nashville.

In a recent development, whatever happens going forward, the News Record was prophetic back in 1976 when it said “people will want to hear and see the Beach Boys for a long time to come.” Does that mean they’ll become a zombie group like Foreigner or the Four Tops that continues to tour without any original members? Could Jardine finally be given the chance to front his own version of the Beach Boys? Are their children going to take over? There’s simply no way to know at this point. But it’s very hard to imagine a summer passing without some version of the Beach Boys on the road.

According to recent reports, amazon’s Black Friday and Cyber Monday sale has officially started—but keeping track of the best discounts yet to land and figuring out which deals are worthwhile can be a challenge. As an alternative, you can have Alexa give you a heads-up about deals on products you already know you want to purchase, so you don’t have to spend time sorting through the noise.

According to recent reports, then head to the Alexa mobile app and go to More in the top left (the three horizontal lines) > Settings > Notifications > Amazon Shopping and toggle on Deal Recommendations under the Shopping Recommendations options. This ensures you’ll receive notifications for items that appear in your shopping activity.

If Alexa finds an upcoming deal on something in your Saved for Later, your Wish List, or in your Shopping Cart, you’ll receive a pop-up alert on your Echo Show display or see a yellow light ring on your Echo speaker. You can also ask, “Alexa, what are my notifications?” to hear a list of deals it has compiled thus far. You can also say "Alexa, let me know when [product name] goes on sale.".

Alexa can detect deals up to 24 hours in advance, so you can either ask it to remind you again when a deal starts or request that it buy the item when the deal goes live. Simply say, “Alexa, buy it for me,” and it’ll charge the default payment and send the item to the default delivery address on your account.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After releasing developer beta 2 of macOS 27.3 earlier this week, the company is now rolling out the public beta for customers looking to try the latest features ahead of next month’s official release. Here’s what’s coming.

Last Monday, Apple released macOS 27.3 beta 2, with new privacy controls for Full Disk Access and automation tools, and the availability of Apple Intelligence in China.

Those came alongside several upcoming features and tools on macOS 27.3 beta 1, including vertical tabs and adaptive dark mode in Safari, native Live Activities support, Markdown rendering in Quick Look, additional checks for potentially harmful content shared through iCloud links, and Siri AI support for Traditional Chinese, Norwegian, Turkish, and Vietnamese.

Sources indicate that and speaking of Siri AI, macOS 27.3 also expands the assistant’s capabilities across Apple’s own apps, allowing people to perform more complex actions in Messages, Music, Calendar, Photos, and Reminders, as well as manage files and folders. Apple is also introducing new tools for third-party developers to build more advanced Siri AI integrations using Markdown-based instructions.

While macOS 27.2 was a rather uneventful upgrade, macOS 27.3 is shaping up to be the biggest update since the release of macOS 27, and consumers on the public beta can now try out these upcoming features ahead of their official release.

The release build for macOS 27.3 public beta 2 is 26C5047e, which matches the developer build.

If you’d like to join Apple’s free public beta program, visit beta.apple.com.

Did you spot anything upcoming in today’s beta? Let us know in the comments.

Expectations that a latest Avengers: Doomsday teaser or trailer is imminent have hit fever pitch over the weekend following cast member Hayley Atwell’s omission while signing autographs in New York that it is dropping on Monday (November 23).

“There’s a new trailer dropping on Monday… am I allowed to have said that?” Atwell, who returns to the franchise as Peggy Carter, told fans on Friday night.

In a recent development, A few hours prior to Atwell’s omission, some 7,000 miles away in Qatar, co-director Joe Russo had also hinted at fresh drops before the picture’s opening by Disney on December 18, telling fans to keep checking their feeds. Watch on Deadline.

Talking in a fireside chat at the Qatar Film Committee’s second Doha Industry Days, Russo explained that the four teasers, preceding an official trailer this summer, had played an integral role in the final version of the film.

He said it had been a way to connect with the fans, which was essential because the audience landscape had changed so much since Avengers: Infinity War and Avengers: Endgame in 2018 and 2019 respectively.

“I have to work extra hard to subvert your expectations and be aware of who you are as a viewer and how you’re changing,” said Russo.

According to recent reports, “The last time I did this, in 2018, 2019, is very different than now because we’ve been through a pandemic; lots of people spent a lot of time on social media. Movies saw a tremendous downturn, streaming saw a tremendous upturn, and now that all seems to be reversing. So, it shifts constantly,” he mentioned. “You have to be a futurist to try to predict where the market is going.”.

It has been revealed that “I have to interact with the fans in order to understand what is moving them, what is working for them,” he remarked. “What we’ve been doing with Doomsday is very different than the last time we did this because the speed of conversation on the internet is even faster than it was in 2018, 2019.”.

It has been revealed that “I had this idea, why don’t we start the story a year early? Why don’t we start dropping clues in the year leading up to the movie… we did four trailers that were sprinkled out,” he continued.

Kicking off on December 23, 2025, the first trailer showing Steve Rogers (Chris Evans) returning home, unpacking his Captain America suit, and holding a baby. A teaser on November 30 highlighted Thor (Chris Hemsworth) praying to Odin for strength. This was followed onJanuary 6 2026 drop featuring the X-Men and a January 13 teaser, featuring the Wakandans and Fantastic Four.

“We’ve done a series of tags around the characters because the story actually started in January of last year, and you’ve been watching it slowly unfold and these are all pieces of something that are going to equal two and a half hours of your time on December 18,” he said.

Recent findings suggest that “It’s slowly investing them [fans] emotionally. But I’m also getting feedback as that’s happening and we can make adjustments as we go, based on what people are tracking or not tracking,” he continued.

Industry observers note that “It’s a very complicated story also, so I have to make sure that they’re following each little crumb we give them. If they get the wrong thing from it, then I have to make adjustments, knowing that they might have the wrong idea about it.”.

Talking about his return to the Avengers franchise alongside brother Anthony Russo, Joe Russo said he had been reluctant at first because of the immense challenge of pulling off a Marvel movie at that scale.

He credited Robert Downey Jr., who played Tony Stark/Iron Man in Avengers: Endgame, with planting the seed for a return to the franchise, with his revelation that he was down to play Victor von Doom/Doctor Doom.

“He’s a very dear friend of mine, but I also think he’s the greatest actor of his generation. This is a supremely talented, charismatic human being. And he translates incredibly well on a global scale. There’s something about the nature of his performance that translates,” said Russo.

“There’s a style that belongs to these films that allows them to work in every market around the world. He just embodies that,” he remarked.

Russo noted Robert had gently enquired whether he was up for coming back to the Avengers franchise over dinner a couple of years ago.

“I was still recovering from Infinity War and Endgame. And I was hesitant… he’s smart, he doesn’t push too much, he just kind of dropped the idea on the table and let it sit there, and then after dinner, he brought it up again, and I was like, ‘I don’t think I could do it, I’m still too tired.’ And then this festered for a little bit. And he didn’t even really tell me what he was going to do going back,” recall Russo.

According to recent reports, “And then another conversation happened where he remarked, ‘You know, I’m going to play Doom’. And I said, ‘That’s a really clever idea”. I can see a corollary there. There are thematics, greatest hero, greatest villain. There’s a multiverse. There’s a reason for being. There’s a compelling idea there. And I went, ‘Well, of course, who else could play the greatest villain other than you.”.

According to recent reports, “It started to simmer in my brain a little bit. But we didn’t have a story. You can’t just show up with an empty canvas, so I still said no.”.

Russo credited longtime collaborator, screenwriter Steve McFeely, with coming up with the premise that gave a way in to writing Doomsday, after they had been pitching ideas back and forth.

Industry observers note that “Steve McFeely called me and said, ‘I have a crazy idea about how this works… what would happen if you left the cameras rolling at the end of Endgame? What’s the very next scene that happens,” recounted Russo.

Industry observers note that “I remarked, “That’s really risky for a movie that had the level of success it did. You’re going to impact people’s emotional investment in it… this could blow up in your face,’ and then I went, ‘I love it’,” he continued.

Industry observers note that “The concept was like that’s a very happy ending for one character. And what if happiness is finite, and what if you have to take happiness from someone else to create your own happiness… What happens in that story? That’s where I went, ‘Right, I know what to do with this.” The idea that like there was a cost to a happy ending.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that “I’ve always joked that I’m a little bit Jew-ish-ish with a substantial hyphen,” indicates Culture Club frontman Boy George. He had recently returned from an eight-day trip to Israel, where he performed two sold-out shows at Tel Aviv’s Menora Mivtachim Arena on Nov. 4 and 7. George’s arrival is a rare one, as most Western artists have steered clear of the country, which has been plagued by political infighting, wars in Gaza and Iran, and global criticism for its handling of the conflicts.

But the 65-year-old is defying convention with characteristic flair. George burst on the pop scene in 1982, one of the first MTV stars with the New Wave hit “Do You Really Want to Hurt Me?” Challenging gender and cultural norms in an oversize hat, Rasta dreads, drag makeup, and a T-shirt that spelled Culture Club in Hebrew (Havurat Aguda), Boy George was an instant sensation and ruled the pop charts for years to come.

It has been revealed that four decades later, Boy George is still advocating for multiculturalism and LGBTQ+ rights, but his hometown of London feels less tolerant. On his way to the doctor in April, he arrived at the Jewish neighborhood of Golder’s Green moments in the wake of an antisemitic stabbing spree, the culmination of a disturbing 82 percent uptick in physical assaults in the U.K. in the first half of 2026, per the Community Security Trust. He then visited the Nova exhibit in London and released the reggae-infused single “We Will Dance Again” (Od Nirkod in Hebrew) in late July on Instagram and X. He made his position clear through the lyrics: “You say genocide/I say war…. You condemn the Jews with selective memory/Musicians holding flags, mouthing like sheep…. You never mention Oct. 7/Young girls raped against trees, murdered brutally/For the crime of dancing.”.

The song prompted a swift and harsh backlash. He remarked he “parted ways” with longtime manager of his BGP label, Tony Pontius, was removed from Bandcamp for using AI on the track, lost old friends like Human League and Heaven 17 founder Martyn Ware, was disinvited from a memorial honoring stylist friend Pam Hogg, and was pulled from a West End revival of “Jesus Christ Superstar.” Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century.

Never one to back down, George spoke out, released his single with live instrumentation on Warner Music/ADA in October (it charted in the U.K., France, Greece, and Latvia), and announced he would perform in Israel, boycotts be damned. While there, he met with Oct. 7 survivors, victims’ families and held a press conference at the site of the Nova Festival in Re’im, where Hamas killed 378 concertgoers and staff, took 44 hostages, and sexually assaulted concertgoers, according to an independent U.N. investigation.

Upon his return to London, George reflected on his trip, the blowback he received, and the alarming rise in antisemitism in an interview with Rolling Stone.

Rolling Stone: Is it true that “We Will Dance Again” was inspired by your visit to the Nova Exhibition in London?

Sources indicate that boy George: Well, it started before that. A lot of musicians were putting flags onstage and using words that I didn’t necessarily support. I had posted a few positive comments online [supporting Nova survivors], and a couple of artists did the usual “shame on you, shame on you.” And I started to see it was getting a lot of rage online. I [thought], I’ll write about what’s going on, because there’s only so many love songs you can write. I’ve known Jewish people since I was a teenager in London. Being in the fashion world and obviously rock ‘n’ roll, it would be very amazing if you didn’t know someone Jewish.

Sources indicate that given that, were you surprised by the lack of compassion for Oct. 7 victims?

I think people were very quick to celebrate what happened on October the 7th and change the narrative, twist it around, make it about something else. And it felt that some of the reaction was already planned. As soon as I saw a Palestinian umbrella, I was like, they got products. This isn’t just people with cardboard and some words scratched on it. A lot of musicians I respected were saying ‘Free Palestine.’ And there was no voice for the Jewish community in London. I went to New York and was given an award by [ewish publication] Tablet magazine for my support of the Jewish people, and I felt a little bit like a fraud. But at that point, nobody was saying anything. So I was kind of like a lone wolf in that sense. Industry observers note that the song really came out of me going to Newly introduced York, getting this award, and thinking, “I really want to do something measured and powerful.” I almost didn’t go to [to Nova]. I thought it was going to be really traumatic. I grew up not that long after the Second World War. We knew about the Holocaust, and anyone that claims it’s not true makes me really angry. So when this [Oct. 7 denial] started to happen, I thought to myself, “I never thought I would live in a world where this would happen again, where this language was being used again.” I wasn’t able to not say something. My Jewish friends remarked to me, “You’re saying things that we can’t say.”.

Being an ally can be fraught these days….

In a recent development, sometimes you need allies from outside, like straight guys supporting gay people and trans people. You need allies that are not part of that group. In the Seventies, when we started Culture Club, our whole ethos was about anti-racism and anti-prejudice. All that stuff was really the backbone of what we were singing about, which is why we called ourselves Culture Club, and why we wore the Jewish star and presented Rastafarian images. We probably naively were mixing up a lot of religious ideas, but it was more about that feeling of why can’t people just live in harmony? … My tastes are very eclectic, not only musically but also culturally. As a kid, if I saw a religious Jewish guy, I’d be like, “That look!” I am interested in other people and human beings.

So, was your iconic hat a nod to the Hasidic look?

That hat was an original Hasidic hat, and in fact, when John [Moss, Culture Club drummer and George’s former boyfriend] went to buy it, because my initials are G.O.D., for George O’Dowd, they wouldn’t put that in the hat. It would have been great!

What’s it like performing your old hits now?

I feel like it’s an ending of something for me. I’m not saying I’ll never sing those songs again. Of course I will, but my feeling is that next year I might start a very different type of band, a punk band or a reggae band. I just need to do something different, because I feel like that old boy George doesn’t really exist anymore.

Do you mean the insecure 20-something George who dated his bandmate, got into drugs, and went to prison, as depicted in the Culture Club documentary?

Industry observers note that I was dealing with a very complicated relationship. I’d grown up in a very dysfunctional family, where there was a lot of fighting, and you grow up thinking that that’s normal. I went from one dysfunctional relationship to another, which is why I joke now that creativity is my lover. One thing I’ve learned in the last 10, 15 years is that songwriting is not hard. Finding what you want to say is the biggest challenge. A song like “We Will Dance Again” kind of wrote itself. When I was at Nova, I saw “we will dance again” written everywhere, and I was like, well, there’s the hook! And then the rest of it was simply looking at what was being noted and using those words in a very blatant way, literally reading stuff out of the newspaper and challenging that as a writer, which I think is the job of an artist to say, “Is there another way of looking at this?” I’ve never said anything negative about Palestine, or anywhere else. It’s about me saying, “I know my Jewish friends are good people. I know this to be a fact.” They fed me more than any other race. You want to be my friend? Feed me.

Having that personal connection, was it hard going from the NOVA exhibit in London to the NOVA massacre site in Israel?

So touring Israel was less of a political stance than a humanitarian one for you?

Industry observers note that I don’t really have a stance. I don’t even know what that means. I’ve been called everything you can think of: Goy George, Genocide George, all of that stuff. I felt like I had to go, and now that I’m back in London, it was the right thing to do. I will go back and do a recording of the songs that I did at Menorah [Mivtachim Arena], because it would be great to put it out as a Boy George in Israel tribute.

Recent findings suggest that bringing former hostage Omer Shemtov onstage with you was so moving. Are you thinking of recording a song with him?

Industry observers note that hopefully, yeah. In a recent development, I’ll deal with it as necessary. Once you’ve got your makeup and your hat on, you become quite formidable.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The iPhone 18 Pro Max isn't the only 18 Pro Max to be released this year, now that Xiaomi has just revealed the Xiaomi 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max flagships. The two phones share more than just a name, though, and it seems Xiaomi has adopted a very Apple-looking camera bump on the back of its phones. But considering the camera specs are totally different, I started wondering what the actual quality differences were.

Industry observers note that the iPhone 18 Pro Max is one of the best camera phones, sporting a trio of 48MP camera lenses: one main, with variable aperture, an ultrawide angle, and a telephoto lens with 4x optical zoom. The zooming camera offers up to 16x "optical quality" and has a maximum magnification of 40x. The Xiaomi 18 Pro Max, on the other hand, has a 200MP main lens, a 50MP ultrawide and a 200MP telephoto with 3.2x optical zoom.

Recent findings suggest that you'd think that the higher resolution camera would produce the best photos, right? Well we've seen time and again that resolution doesn't always equal quality, especially now that camera phones rely on software just as much as they do hardware. That's why phones like the iPhone 18 Pro Max perform so well in our photo shootouts.

Sources indicate that but obviously the only way to find out for sure is to actually take some photos and compare the results from each phone. So, out of iPhone 18 Pro Max and Xiaomi 18 Pro Max, which 18 Pro Max actually has the best cameras?

The latest and best iPhone, the iPhone 18 Pro Max comes with a fresh variable aperture camera, a larger battery, incredible performance from the A20 Pro chipset and all those other things that make the iPhone worth owning.

While not officially available in the U.S., the Xiaomi 18 Pro Max has a lot of great features. They include a rear-mounted display, 200MP main and telephoto camera lenses, a 6.98-inch display with Privacy Display and an enormous 7,050 mAh battery.

The main camera shot is quite different on both phones. The Xiaomi certainly excels in taking a brighter photo, but the result means that the lighter areas look considerably more washed out compared to the iPhone. The overall quality isn't as good either, since the iPhone can pick up more detail in the surroundings, such as my dogs' fur and the gravel on the path. In contrast, the Xiaomi tends to blur those finer details together, especially in the background.

It has been revealed that shooting indoors, things are a little more balanced, but it's clear that the Xiaomi's camera isn't quite as focused as the iPhone's, and most of the Lego set is blurry in comparison to Apple's camera. However the coloring and detail seem to be much closer than they were with the outdoor shot.

The Xiaomi camera's habit of brightening up the image seems to work in its favor on the ultrawide angle lens, with the iPhone adopting a more washed out and drab-looking color temperature. There are reasons for that, and it all comes down to Apple's automatic white balance being somewhat anti-Fall.

However, coloring aside, the detail on the iPhone-captured shot just isn't there. You can even see it in the grass if you look closely, with all the stalks looking pixelated and blurred, compared to the much sharper detail captured by the Xiaomi.

When it comes to color, the Xiaomi does edge the top spot with slightly more vivid coloring of these berries, in part thanks to the slightly brighter images. The iPhone hasn't washed out the coloring in this instance, and manages to offer a nice bright image with solid contrast between the different colors.

The Xiaomi 18 Pro Max's front camera sports a 50MP sensor, compared to the 18MP one on the iPhone 18 Pro Max, but how much of a difference does it make? As was the case with the rear cameras, the photo is a lot brighter, which really highlights the fact that the sun is shining directly onto my face. Meanwhile the iPhone's shot is a little darker, but the tones seem more true to life and don't make it look like this is my first time outside in several months.

The quality is good on both, even going so far as to pick up the reflection of my other dog in my sunglasses. However, zooming in shows how much of a difference high resolution can make. Xiaomi's rendition of my reflected dog is clear and almost perfect, while the iPhone's is pixelated and grainy. Then again, the rest of the photo is fine, and zooming right in isn't something a lot of folks will be doing.

In a recent development, xiaomi's Portrait mode is, honestly, incredibly disappointing. The bokeh effect is barely noticeable, and it doesn't really emphasize myself in the same way that the iPhone does. The IPhone 18 Pro Max ramped up that effect to the point where the background isn't that visible, and it makes me pop out a little more. The quality of the photo isn't quite as good, but with the extra bokeh and the return more accurate coloring, it's the clear winner.

According to recent reports, zooming into 4x magnification and things are fairly even. The iPhone's coloring is a little more drab than Xiaomi's, but the overall quality of the zoomed-in shot is basically the same, to the point where it's more about personal preference than anything else.

Jumping up to 8x magnification and you can see how Apple's "optical quality" feature really shines. The shot of my dog at this magnification is much more clear than that of the Xiaomi 18 Pro Max, which noticeably merges the finer details of my dog's fur. The contrasting colors on the Xiaomi's telephoto is more noticeable than the iPhone's, but the loss of quality really lets the team down.

If you increase the magnification to 40x, there's absolutely no question about which camera is better. It's Xiaomi's, simply because the phone produced a clear and crisp shot that the iPhone just can't compete with. I assume some AI upscaling was involved, as is the case with so many other phones, and it's something that Apple consistently fails at. Maybe that's something Apple can include on the iPhone 20.

Going right in with the Macro mode, and the iPhone takes the crown once again. As with before, the picture isn't as bright as Xiaomi's shot, but that doesn't actually matter in this case. The iPhone managed to produce a much crisper photo, with bright colors and details that Xiaomi's camera didn't quite match.

Low light performance can make or break a camera phone, and I'm honestly a little torn over which camera is better in this situation. The iPhone 18 Pro Max produced a shot that is brighter and captured more detail, but it also appears somewhat overexposed in the process.

Sources indicate that the Xiaomi 18 Pro Max managed to capture less detail on the church and its surroundings, despite the higher resolution camera, but produced a shot that looks slightly nicer — so long as you don't zoom in too much. And, honestly, I can't tell you which one I like better.

Industry observers note that overall, the iPhone 18 Pro Max managed to beat out the Xiaomi in more categories, though, the two phones drew in several rounds. That indicates that Xiaomi 18 Pro Max's camera is no slouch, but not enough to beat the iPhone's camera in those core categories. The quality of the 8x zoom in particular was especially disappointing, since a 200MP lens should have the resolution to be able to cut down a high-quality image to simulate extra magnification — just like Apple does.

According to recent reports, given the choice, and purely based on camera performance, I'd pick the iPhone 18 Pro Max over the Xiaomi. Still the iPhone 18 Pro Max didn't dominate, and the Xiaomi camera certainly manages to produce some great shots. The fact they tied in four different categories just goes to show that these two phones are both very capable camera phones.

But Xiaomi obviously needs to work on fixing its shortcomings, including capturing more detail in low light, improving the bokeh effect and all those other things that could make the camera even better.

Following a week of controversy, Russell Brand’s wife promised to no longer share her husband’s statements from prison.

In the latest episode in the couple’s Sunday Service series — now hosted solely by Laura Brand, with some prerecorded footage of her now-imprisoned husband — Laura told viewers, “Last week’s episode drew a considerable amount of attention and, now that I understand the parameters set by the brilliant staff at HMP Littlehey [prison], I will absolutely honor that.”.

In the video posted last Sunday following Russell’s conviction and sentencing, Laura read a message to listeners from Russell where he reiterated, “I am not guilty for the offenses I have been jailed for, so something strange is happening.”.

That communique sparked a firestorm in the U.K., where “prisoners are strictly banned from making statements that cause distress to victims, and speaking to the media is only permitted in exceptional circumstances,” a spokesperson for the prime minister said.

The Prison Service of England and Wales requested that the Google-owned YouTube take down the video, saying Brand’s message was “distressing for victims.” However, Google denied the request, stating that — while hurtful for the victims — Brand’s video didn’t violate any of the platform’s rules. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that tom Jackson, a former Denver Broncos player and an NFL analyst for ESPN, has died.
  • Jackson’s family told ESPN that he passed on Friday, in what his longtime co-host Chris Berman called an “unexpected” death, having previously spoken “at length” with Jackson on Tuesday.
  • “He was a vital 75,” said Berman on ESPN‘s Sunday NFL Countdown.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that tom Jackson, a former Denver Broncos player and an NFL analyst for ESPN, has died. He was 75.

Jackson’s family told ESPN that he passed on Friday, in what his longtime co-host Chris Berman called an “unexpected” death, having previously spoken “at length” with Jackson on Tuesday.

“He was a vital 75,” said Berman on ESPN‘s Sunday NFL Countdown. “Tom was poignant. He was active. This is a shock.”.

“I was fortunate to work side by side with Tom for 30 years, primarily on NFL Primetime and Sunday NFL Countdown,” he added. “It was a labor of love for our whole team, both in front of the camera and behind it. We always hoped our viewers enjoyed the shows as much as we did bringing it to them every week.”.

In honor of the Broncos “Orange Crush Defense” linebacker, the entire Countdown crew wore orange ties during Sunday’s show.

Born April 4, 1951 in Cleveland, Ohio, Thomas Louie Jackson was recruited by University of Louisville head coach Lee Corso, playing college football for three seasons from 1970 to 1972, during which he was a two-time Missouri Valley Conference player of the year.

During the 1973 NFL Draft, Jackson was selected 88th overall by the Broncos, where he played a 14-year career as linebacker, helping lead the team to play Super Bowl XII and Super Bowl XXI.

Jackson went on to work for ESPN Studios in 1987, paired with Berman on Sunday NFL Countdown and NFL Primetime. His years of broadcasting experience as an NFL analyst earned him the 2015 Pete Rozelle Radio-Television Award from the Pro Football Hall of Fame.
