For example, the Amazon Prime for Young Adults program allows young adults between the ages of 18 and 24 to get all of the Prime perks for half the cost—$7.49 per month or $69 annually.

I'll be the first to admit I didn't know all of the benefits that Amazon Prime offers to its members. There are a lot more perks than people think. Here are the most impressive ones (and check out the full list):.

Fast free shipping on millions of items: Depending on where you live, shipping can take one or two days, and some even come on the same day for orders of $25 or more in most areas—and it’s always free (if being shipped by the Amazon store).

Select pre-ordered items can be delivered on their release date for free (for most areas).

The option to have items delivered inside your garage with a smart garage device (depending on where you live) for $1.99 per order, or for free if you combine it with Amazon Day delivery.

Earn rewards for future purchases when you select free no-rush shipping.

The option to have all your weekly orders delivered on a specific day, to reduce waste from boxes.

Amazon Prime Visa card: Cardholders get 5% back on Amazon, Whole Foods, Chase Travel, and other purchases. Prime members who use this card extensively can earn rewards that offset the cost of membership.

In a recent development, A Grubhub+ and Uber Eats membership, normally $9.99 per month, which gets you free delivery on eligible orders, lower service fees, exclusive deals, and other perks as long as you remain a Prime Member (it used to be only for a year). The Uber Eats membership gets you free delivery on eligible restaurants of $25 or more.

It has been revealed that sharing with family or friends: Amazon Family is the existing program for sharing Prime benefits, and it allows you to add separate profiles for one other adult who lives in the same household as the primary account holder, up to four teens, and up to four child accounts. This grants access to all the standard benefits, such as free delivery, Prime Video with ads, Prime Reading, third-party benefits like Grubhub, and access to audiobooks, e-books, certain games, and Amazon Music.

Industry observers note that amazon Health: Prime consumers get One Medical access for an additional $9 per month or $99 per year. Through your devices, you’ll have 24/7 access to on-demand virtual care, plus real-life access to primary care offices in a number of U.S. cities. It accepts most major health insurance intends, too.

Amazon Pharmacy: Access to free two-day delivery and other savings on medications.

Prime Video: Prime includes unlimited streaming of movies, TV highlights, and Amazon Originals with ads, which normally costs $9 per month.

Amazon Music Prime: Access to Amazon's Spotify-esque music streaming service (not to be confused with Amazon's other music streaming subscriptions).

Amazon Luna: A cloud gaming platform that offers new free games every month, free downloadable PC games, content, a monthly Twitch channel subscription, and a free channel subscription on Twitch each month for Prime Members.

Amazon Photos: Unlimited photo storage plus 5 GBs for videos and other files (which extends to members of your Family Vault).

Prime Reading: Free access to a rotating selection of e-books and magazines for Kindle or Fire tablets and Kindle apps.

Amazon's First Reads: You get up to two free e-books every month from a curated list of books handpicked by editors.

It has been revealed that whatsApp is gradually rolling out an increase to its group chat limit, allowing up to 1,500 participants to join in, instead of the previous 1,024 cap. Here are the details.

While there are exceptions, there are generally two kinds of WhatsApp users: those who hate group chats, and those who can’t seem to be in enough of them.

If you’re in the second category, you’re likely aware that WhatsApp has steadily increased the number of participants allowed in group chats over the years, jumping from 100 to 256 in 2016, then to 512 and, soon after, to 1,024 in 2022.

Now, as spotted by WABetaInfo, WhatsApp is once again expanding that limit, raising the maximum number of participants in a group chat to 1,500.

According to the website, the new limit is rolling out to consumers on iOS and Android, though the rollout is gradual, meaning “not every account will see the higher limit immediately.”.

Recent findings suggest that whatsApp is automatically updating existing groups to support the new limit. This means that admins do not need to take any action to unlock the higher capacity. As soon as the enhancement becomes available to their accounts, their groups will support up to 1500 members. As a result, the update lets admins add up to 476 new members to their existing groups.

This rollout comes as WhatsApp has been working to make group chats easier to manage. Just last month, the organization unveiled four upcoming features, including the ability to pin messages indefinitely, share status updates within groups, filter conversations by mentions and replies, and share recent message history with new members after they join.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that with top streaming services raising prices seemingly every year — hell, sometimes twice a year — an ad-supported, totally free streaming service like Tubi feels like a Christmas miracle, with over 20,000 reveals and movies available to watch without paying a cent. And that sprawling library isn't just about quantity, but quality, too, with content from major film studios including Paramount, MGM and Lionsgate, and television networks including A&E, Lifetime, and Starz.

But to keep that platform feeling fresh and interesting, every once in a while Tubi has to say goodbye to some fan-favorite flicks and series to make room for a newly introduced wave of film and TV titles. And with another month rapidly coming to a close (where exactly did November go?), that means you'll have to act promptly if you want to catch these three great movies for $0 before they're gone.

Whether you're in the mood for a weepy autumnal favorite, a beloved Ben Stiller comedy, or a little dystopian trip back to Panem, here are three movies to stream before they leave Tubi soon.

Ben Stiller, Robert De Niro, Blythe Danner, and Teri Polo are all back for a fourth "Meet the Parents" movie, "Focker in Law" — with the added fun of Ariana Grande playing a Focker daughter-in-law — which hits theaters nationwide on November 25. If you want to go back to the beginnings of the comedy franchise, though, the original "Meet the Parents" movie is available to watch on Tubi, but not for long.

If you missed the 2000 comedy all those years ago, "Meet the Parents" stars Stiller as the unfortunately-named Greg Focker, who is desperate to impress the parents of his girlfriend (Polo) during her sister's wedding, a goal made significantly more complicated by the fact that her dad is a formidable and overprotective CIA agent (De Niro).

Stream "Meet the Parents" on Tubi now.

Recent findings suggest that grab the Kleenex: It's "Stepmom" season. The foliage-filled 1998 weeper stars a Golden Globe-nominated Susan Sarandon as Jackie Harrison, a divorced mother of two who's been diagnosed with terminal cancer. As she battles her illness, she must contend with her ex-husband's new partner, the much younger and career-driven Isabel Kelly (Julia Roberts), who will soon become the stepmother of Jackie's beloved children, Anna (Jena Malone) and Ben (Liam Aiken).

Though critics at the time dinged the tearjerker for its melodrama ("Solid work from Julia Roberts and Susan Sarandon isn't enough to save 'Stepmom' from a story whose manipulations dilute the effectiveness of a potentially affecting drama," reads the critical consensus on Rotten Tomatoes), "Stepmom" has become an enduring fall favorite thanks to its cozy, family-focused vibes and those iconic leading ladies.

In case you somehow haven't heard, there's a massive new "Hunger Games" movie in theaters today: "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping," which centers on the 50th Hunger Games, about a quarter-century before Katniss Everdeen's participation.

Sources indicate that but before you rush out to your nearest cinema, you can revisit the first installment in the Panem prequels, "The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes," which is available to watch for free right now on Tubi. "Ballad" follows an 18-year-old Coriolanus Snow (Tom Blyth), who tries to restore his disgraced family's status in the post-war Capitol by mentoring Lucy Gray Baird (Rachel Zegler), a tribute from the impoverished District 12. But will his ruthless ambition get in the way?

Along with Blyth and Zegler, the star-studded cast also includes Peter Dinklage, Hunter Schafer, Josh Andrés Rivera, Jason Schwartzman, and Viola Davis.

Stream "The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes" on Tubi now.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nearly 20 years later, Danny Ocean is trying to get the gang back together for Ocean’s 14, which was expected to begin filming in 2026.

David Leitch, who is attached to direct the fourth installment in the heist film franchise, recently noted that George Clooney and his Smokehouse producing partner Grant Heslov have delivered a “great script,” but scheduling issues stand in the way.

“Oh, I mean, there’s a great script and I think everybody’s excited about moving it forward,” he told People. “I think it’s always been about getting all those people together, and their schedules are always the concern.”.

Industry observers note that leitch added, “Look, there’s a lot of excitement around it and … George and Grant did incredible work on the script. So, yeah, a lot of motivation to make it happen.” Watch on Deadline.

Clooney starred as Danny Ocean in the 2001 Steven Soderbergh-helmed remake of the 1960 Rat Pack film, reprising the role in Ocean’s Twelve (2004) and Ocean’s Thirteen (2007).

In January 2025, Leitch was in early talks to direct the next installment. Last October, the 2x Oscar winner Warner Bros. approved the budget for Ocean’s 14, which he expected to begin filming this year.

Ocean’s 14 will mark the first installment in the main franchise not directed by Soderbergh, after Gary Ross helmed the 2018 female-led spin-off Ocean’s 8, starring Sandra Bullock as Danny’s sister Debbie Ocean.

Meanwhile, Bradley Cooper is attached write and direct an Ocean’s 11 prequel, which will star Ryan Gosling and Margot Robbie as Danny Ocean’s parents.

These 14 New Features Are Coming to iOS 27.3

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1487 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that apple has been beta testing iOS 27.3 since Nov.
  • In a recent development, technically, anyone with a compatible iPhone can try out iOS 27.3 right now—assuming you enroll your Apple Account in the developer program.
  • Recent findings suggest that the iPhone Duo is Apple's first foldable smartphone, but also the organization's first phone since the iPhone SE 3 to ship with Touch ID.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that apple has been beta testing iOS 27.3 since Nov. 3. While this update isn't as large as iOS 27 proper, it's surprisingly feature-filled for a 0.3 update. This is only a beta, so anything could (and likely will) change before Apple officially releases the update. But, as it stands, iOS 27.3 tests 10 new features—including one feature the firm trialed in the previous beta.

In a recent development, technically, anyone with a compatible iPhone can try out iOS 27.3 right now—assuming you enroll your Apple Account in the developer program. But a word of warning: Betas can be temperamental, and could be risky. As such, I'd recommend avoiding the beta until Apple releases the public beta, which comes after a bit more testing to iron out larger issues. Either way, make sure to make a full backup of your iPhone to a Mac or PC first, as issues with the beta could result in permanent data loss.

Recent findings suggest that the iPhone Duo is Apple's first foldable smartphone, but also the organization's first phone since the iPhone SE 3 to ship with Touch ID. While it works well enough for unlocking your iPhone, it's still an adjustment for those of us used to Face ID. With iOS 27.3, Apple is now testing face unlock for the Duo—not Face ID, mind you. The Duo's front camera doesn't have the tech required to power Face ID or its secure protocols. Instead, this feature simply unlocks your iPhone Duo with a face scan. In addition, your Duo will still require Touch ID for Apple Pay and passwords, or after 45 minutes of inactivity. You can read more about this upcoming feature here.

According to recent reports, iOS 27.3 also comes with a upcoming setting that lets you lock your iPhone Duo by closing it—as you would expect from, say, a laptop—or, dare I say, a flip phone? Right now, closing the Duo seamlessly transitions what's on the significant screen to the smaller display, and you have to press the side button to lock the phone.

Recent findings suggest that with watchOS 27, Apple released "Audio Intelligence," a newly introduced set of features for Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4. Audio Intelligence uses the watches' new S11 chip, along with on-device AI and cloud-based AI, to run new features, like Sound Recognition and Shazam (music recognition).

With iOS 27.3, however, the firm is now officially testing the other two Audio Intelligence features it originally unveiled with watchOS 27. First, there's Live Rewind: By double-clicking the watch crown, you can pull up a transcript of the last 15 seconds of a conversation. Siri Recap, on the other hand, displays summaries of conversations you had that day, in case you need a refresher on any chats you might have otherwise forgotten about,.

The company generated some controversy when it first announced these two Audio Intelligence features, since, on the surface, it sounds like these new Apple Watches are essentially spying on people all day long. According to Apple, however, that isn't really the case. The company says Audio Intelligence is private, and never records or stores any audio. No speakers are ever identified, and text results (both transcripts and summaries) are deleted automatically after a set period of time unless the user saves them to the Siri app. You can read more about how Audio Intelligence works here.

Despite their claims, I'm sure there will still be strong feelings surrounding these Audio Intelligence features. We'll have to see whether Apple can prove Live Rewind and Siri Recap aren't all that creepy throughout the iOS 27.3 beta process.

iOS 27.3 also introduces app actions for Siri AI. Apple is testing latest abilities for Siri AI, including organizing files, planning events, or adding photos to albums. You could ask Siri to organize your Downloads folder, or delete files that haven't been opened in more than a year. You could ask Siri to find a coffee shop you went to last week, or to save an article to your Reading List in Safari. You could ask Siri to check your calendar and set up a time for an event based on when you're free. You can even ask the assistant to schedule, edit, or unsend messages.

For example, you could ask Siri AI to help you plan a trip with your friends. You could ask the AI to put together a themed playlist in Apple Music, schedule a message to a group about an upcoming trip, organize the websites you've been visiting in Safari into a tab group, and, after the trip, ask Siri to move your best photos to your favorites album. These new actions work in the following apps: Calendar, Files, Finder, Journal, Mail, Maps, Messages, Music, Notes, Photos, Preview, Reminders, Safari, Shortcuts, and Weather. Developers can also add Siri AI app actions support to their own apps.

It has been revealed that apple started testing its latest Health app with the iOS 27.2 beta, but pulled the redesign before the official release. Now, with iOS 27.3, the new app is back. The new Health app has a health dashboard for the first time, as well as new features like Health Age and movement assessments. It seems to be pulling from some popular competitor services, hopefully, for the better. For more on the new Health app, check out Lifehacker health editor Beth Skwarecki's explainer.

In a recent development, continuing on the Health track, iOS 27.3 also introduces "Gym Strength." This is a new Fitness+ feature that offers a personalized four-week strength-training initiative. You can customize these plans to meet your goals, experience level, and schedule, and they adapt as you progress. You'll get recommendations based on your experience with exercises, reps, and sets, including video demos for exercises. You can access Gym Strength on both iPhone and iPad, and Apple Watches are optional—though you can log your progress with the wearable if you have it.

Apple is also testing a new Siri AI feature in Safari, that gives the bot access to entire webpages, including the parts of the site that aren't on-screen. Say you want to know all the gluten-free options on a menu on a restaurant's website, but only a portion of the site is actually in view. You could ask Siri to read you the gluten-free options, and it would pull from the whole page, even though you can only see part of it.

In a recent development, vertical tabs have been a favorite among browser aficionados, as they give you more screen real estate in your browser while keeping your tabs off the side. Apple hasn't made the jump—until now. This feature works with iPads running iPadOS 27.3 as well as Macs running macOS 27.3.

Industry observers note that another new Safari feature in testing is "Adaptive Dark Mode." This feature forces websites into a dark theme, if they don't have a native theme of their own. There are third-party apps that can do this, but this is the first time Apple has offered this feature built into Safari.

According to recent reports, apple is also testing fresh StandBy experiences with iOS 27.3, which were previously only available on the iPhone Duo. When you turn your iPhone sideways while plugged in, you'll find new Analog and Digital Clock faces with new customization options. There's also a new Photos face, with the option to pull images from Shared Albums.

"Reachability" pulls your iPhone's display down towards the bottom of the screen, so you can access items towards the top of the display with one hand. It's a useful feature for those of us with major iPhones, and now, there's no iPhone bigger than the Duo. With iOS 27.3, Apple is testing Reachability for its first foldable phone. It's a bit like the inverse of how Reachability right now works: You can swipe on the left or right side of your Duo's display to shift the other side of the screen towards your current position. If you're holding your Duo in your left hand, a swipe of the left side will pull the right side over to the left, and vice versa.

Apple is also rolling out new languages for Siri AI in iOS 27.3. Now, Apple's smart assistant supports Traditional Chinese, Vietnamese, Turkish, and Norwegian.

In a recent development, if you have an Apple Intelligence-compatible iPad running iPadOS 27.3, you now have access to Siri Mode in Camera. As with iOS, you can open the Camera app on iPadOS to access Siri Mode, and ask Siri about your surroundings.

In a recent development, if you watch videos in Apple Podcasts, you can find them in more sources than the Podcasts app. With the new updates, you'll find these videos on Apple TV 4K, select smart TVs, your iPhone, iPad, Mac, and even in CarPlay. (Please don't watch video podcasts while driving.).

According to recent reports, ice storms cause long outages because several exposures act together. Ice adds weight to conductors, hardware and structures. Wind pushes on the larger iced surface. Trees and limbs bend into the line and add impact and uneven load. Conductors may also gallop and lose clearance. This paper explains how these loads combine and why the complete line must be assessed, not a single component. It reviews a monitored winter test of three conductor systems. History Reveals: Wayne Gretzky and Warren Buffett Can Teach Us About Investing

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (937 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • 10 stocks we like better than Vanguard S&P 500 ETF ›.
  • Industry observers note that wayne Gretzky is one of the most iconic figures in hockey.
  • Gretzky was so good at putting points on the board because of his uncanny ability to be in the right place at the right time.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Gran – Nov 22, 2026 at 7:30AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Vanguard S&P 500 ETF ›.

Industry observers note that wayne Gretzky is one of the most iconic figures in hockey. During his 20-year career in the NHL, Gretzky played in 1,487 games, scored 894 goals, and delivered 1,963 assists for a total of 2,857 points -- about 1.92 points per game.

Gretzky was so good at putting points on the board because of his uncanny ability to be in the right place at the right time. He seemed to anticipate where the puck was going to bounce next and put himself in position to capitalize on opportunities.

What can Gretzky's hockey career teach us about investing? More than you might think. Legendary investor Warren Buffett found inspiration from Wayne Gretzky. In a 2008 op-ed for The Fresh York Times, Buffett quoted Gretzky, who famously said, "I skate to where the puck is going to be, not to where it has been.".

There's a great lesson here about investing. Let's look at what Buffett meant by investing based on Wayne Gretzky's hockey skills -- and why stock market history reveals that this "Gretzky-style" investing approach is a winning strategy.

Industry observers note that warren Buffett. Image source: The Motley Fool.

In a recent development, it's understandable to get caught up in negative daily news headlines. On any given day, it might seem like the stock market is going to crash, that the world is ending. But remember: Stock markets are about the future, not today.

Just as Wayne Gretzky was great at anticipating the next move of the puck on the ice, investors try to anticipate the future. They allocate capital to stocks or sectors based on expected future earnings growth.

Stock investors are constantly evaluating what's likely to happen next -- which companies are poised to keep growing, which industries are about to benefit from positive economic changes, and which countries around the world are due for a stock market surge. They want to put their money into the places where "the puck is going to be" -- not where the action is happening right now.

What does this mean for you? Take a long-term approach to investing. If you're putting money into the stock market today, hopefully you're ready and able to leave that money alone for the next five years, 10 years, 20 years, or more. You're sending that money on a long journey into the future. Even if the stock market crashes tomorrow, you're making a long-term bet that your investment will grow in the long run.

It has been revealed that most of the time, that's a good bet. The S&P 500 (^GSPC -3.70%) has delivered 9.98% annualized returns over the past 98 years, even with terrible crises and crashes along the way such as the Great Depression, World War II, and the 2020 pandemic.

Industry observers note that no matter how risky and dangerous the world seems on any given day, the future of the stock market might be brighter than you imagine. It pays to be optimistic about stocks.

Gretzky's famous quote is also a reminder to avoid trying to "time the market." In his Times op-ed in 2008, Warren Buffett wrote:.

Sources indicate that just like a hockey puck bouncing around an NHL ice rink, markets move fast. The S&P 500 can crash, but it can also bounce back even faster. If you're waiting on the sidelines, trying to time the market and choose the "right time" to invest, share prices might shoot back up faster than you can buy in.

Sources indicate that if you miss out on the "best days" of the S&P 500, you might miss out on a significant chunk of future wealth. Fidelity research found that, based on historical S&P 500 returns from the end of 1987 to the end of 2025, an investor who missed the five best days of returns over those 38 years would have seen 38% lower overall returns.

Instead of trying to choose exactly the right day to buy stocks, it's better to put your money to work as soon as you can. "Time in the market" beats "timing the market.".

How should you invest based on this lesson from Buffett and Gretzky? Buying a low-cost S&P 500 index fund is often a good long-term bet.

The Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (VOO -3.42%) has delivered annualized gains of about 14.8% in the past 16 years since the fund's inception in September 2010. Even if the next few decades are not so fruitful and the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF only delivers the long-term stock market average return of 9.98%, that's still enough to get richer in the long run.

NYSEMKT · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

In a recent development, when you buy a low-cost index fund like VOO, you are not picking stocks or choosing individual sectors. You're making a long-term bet that the stock market itself will put your money to work in great companies that will profit from the economy of the future. In this way, investing in an S&P 500 ETF can put your money "where the puck is going to be.".

When our analyst team has a stock tip, it can pay to listen. After all, Stock Advisor's total average return is 719%* — a market-crushing outperformance compared to 192% for the S&P 500.

  • As my colleague Ryan explained, Apple will likely release iOS 27.3 to all iPhone users sometime in December.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that iOS 27.3 is right now in beta testing with developers and public beta people. The upgrade includes multiple upcoming features for iPhone users, including the redesigned Health app, iPhone Duo updates, and much more. Here’s everything you need to know about what’s new in iOS 27.3 ….

9to5Mac is supported by Sony: Score Sony’s ULT Field 1 Bluetooth speaker for 51% off. Powerful bass, room-filling sound, up to 12 hours of battery life, IP67 durability, stereo pairing support, and much more.

As my colleague Ryan explained, Apple will likely release iOS 27.3 to all iPhone users sometime in December. Typically, Apple would release its x.2 software updates in December, but this year is different because iOS 27.1 was exclusive to iPhone Duo. That means that, in terms of the timeline, iOS 27.3 is essentially the equivalent of iOS 27.2.

Here’s when Apple has released its December updates in recent years:.

So with that in mind, we expect iOS 27.3 to be released sometime during the first half of December.

Sources indicate that the redesigned Health app is back in iOS 27.3. This was first available during testing of iOS 27.2, but did not ship as part of that final patch.

In a recent development, the redesigned Health app is split into three tabs: Insights, Longevity, and Browse. The app features an all-new design that dynamically adapts based on your data, including Apple Intelligence. The Longevity tab includes a new Health age feature that uses Apple Watch data to show how your metrics track relative to your actual age.

For Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 users, it also offers easy access to view your Readiness score every morning.

For Apple Fitness+, iOS 27.3 adds a new Gym Strength feature. This creates progressive, four-week aims based on your strength goals, experience, schedule, and available equipment.

As you complete each week of workouts, the following week adapts based on the reps and weights you logged.

For iPhone Duo owners, iOS 27.3 adds Reachability support. This setting shifts the interface on the outer display to the right or left, making it easier to reach the far corners. It’s designed to make iPhone Duo easier to use with one hand, despite the wider outer display. You activate it by swiping right on the right edge of the screen or left on the left edge.

Reachability for iPhone Duo is on by default. You can turn it off in Settings > Accessibility > Touch > Reachability.

iOS 27.3 also brings a new face unlock feature to iPhone Duo. This is not full-fledged Face ID. Instead, Apple is using the front-facing camera on the iPhone Duo’s outer display to recognize you, then unlock the device. It doesn’t work for things like Apple Pay and passwords.

iOS 27.3 also tweaks the iPhone Duo’s software keyboard by making the keys slightly narrower and the font slightly smaller.

In a recent development, finally, iOS 27.3 includes a new option in the Settings app to have your iPhone Duo lock when closed. Once enabled, your iPhone Duo will lock when you fold it, rather than transition content from the inner display to the outer display.

When it debuted, the iPhone Duo included a more robust version of StandBy with new clock faces and expanded customization options. iOS 27.3 brings the iPhone Duo’s StandBy experience to all iPhone models.

This includes the redesigned Analog and Digital Clock faces, as well as additional customization options for colors and complications. The update also adds support for Shared Albums to the Photos face.

Sources indicate that iOS 27.3 brings several key Siri AI updates. First, the update expands Siri AI with many fresh capabilities across Apple apps. Apple explains:.

We started rolling out these upcoming capabilities across many Apple apps, including Calendar, Files, Finder, Journal, Mail, Maps, Messages, Music, Notes, Photos, Preview, Reminders, Safari, Shortcuts, and Weather, so users can do things like find a coffee shop they visited last week or archive files that haven’t been opened in over a year.

There are many more actions available now as examples for you to reference. To see what you can do in each app, just ask Siri AI.

With iOS 27.3, Apple is also starting to test upcoming ways for developers to create Siri AI integrations for the first time. This is described as an “early Developer Preview.” Apple explains:.

Today’s preview allows any app to bring its content and actions directly into Siri AI by using App Intents, making it easier for all apps to tap into Siri AI’s newest capabilities, including personal context understanding, onscreen awareness, natural language, and more. So people can just ask for help in their own words, and Siri AI carries out any custom action you’ve built, from checking a delivery to booking a reservation to placing an order.

While this is being tested as part of iOS 27.3, Apple says it will start shipping to customers in a few months.

iOS 27.3 also expands Siri AI to newly introduced languages, including French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish.

Sources indicate that iOS 27.3 also introduces usage limits on select Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features. The limits apply to things like:.

You can unlock higher usage limits with an eligible iCloud+ plan, starting at $2.99 per month. If you hit your usage limit, basic Siri requests will still work. That includes things like setting timers and alarms.

Recent findings suggest that iOS 27.3 brings the original set of Apple Intelligence features to China for the first time. This does not include Siri AI or other iOS 27 updates, but it does include the following features:.

Industry observers note that iOS 27.3 is a major patch to Safari. First, the update adds support for a newly introduced vertical tabs design layout on iPhone Duo’s inner display. If you choose this option, your Safari tabs will be arranged vertically along the left-hand side of Safari, rather than along the top. Vertical tabs are also available on Mac and iPad with macOS 27.3 and iPadOS 27.3.

It has been revealed that iOS 27.3 also adds a new Adaptive Dark Mode feature. This feature can automatically apply Dark Mode to websites that don’t natively support it. You can choose to have Adaptive Dark Mode automatically kick in or use it on a site-by-site basis.

Industry observers note that for Apple Music users, iOS 27.3 adds a new “Selfie Sing” feature that lets users record a video of themselves while singing karaoke. To use this feature, start playing a song and go to the lyrics view. Then tap the new camera button that appears on the right-hand side of the lyrics.

The update also refines the design of viewing lyrics while your iPhone is in landscape mode.

There are two key changes to the Apple TV app in iOS 27.3. First, the upgrade introduces video podcasts in the TV app. You can now watch your favorite video podcasts in the TV app, and sync your playback progress between the TV app and the Podcasts app.

Second, iOS 27.3 adds vertical video to the TV app. The app now includes a newly introduced “Explore Clip Collections” section where you can browse clips from Apple TV content in a TikTok-style design.

Here are a few other changes in iOS 27.3:.

What are your favorite newly introduced features in iOS 27.3? Have you spotted any other changes in the update? Let us know down in the comments.

Breaking: Disney Just Hit a 52-Week High. 3 Reasons It Still Has Room to Run.

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1105 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, walt Disney (DIS -1.89%) closed at a 52-week high on Nov.
  • Here's why Disney is breaking out despite a sell-off in the major stock market indexes, and whether the consumer discretionary stock has room to run from here.
  • Recent findings suggest that fiscal 2026 was arguably Disney's best year since before the COVID-19 pandemic.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Daniel Foelber – Nov 22, 2026 at 7:45AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Walt Disney ›.

In a recent development, walt Disney (DIS -1.89%) closed at a 52-week high on Nov. 18 -- the day after it reported its fourth-quarter and full-year fiscal 2026 results. Disney is now up 7.6% year to date and just a hair below its highest level in over four years.

Here's why Disney is breaking out despite a sell-off in the major stock market indexes, and whether the consumer discretionary stock has room to run from here.

Recent findings suggest that fiscal 2026 was arguably Disney's best year since before the COVID-19 pandemic. Overall revenue grew 8% year over year, and margins improved, driven by a 12% increase in operating income.

In a recent development, A major reason for Disney's increase in profitability is that Disney+ is now a key contributor to entertainment earnings, whereas just a few years ago it was losing money. In fiscal 2026, the entertainment subscription video-on-demand (SVOD) segment, which mainly comprises Disney+ and Hulu, generated $2.57 billion in operating income, up from $1.3 billion in fiscal 2025. That's a significant 47.2% of total entertainment operating income for the fiscal year -- proving that streaming is helping to offset the declines in linear cable networks.

It has been revealed that disney's sports segment grew revenue 5% year over year and operating income by 7%, which may seem weak at first glance. But sports holding its own is impressive, considering margins remain under pressure due to media rights costs, the challenges of integrating ESPN with Hulu and Disney+, and the risk of sports streaming cannibalizing traditional cable customers.

Experiences had another excellent year, including notching over $10 billion in revenue in a single quarter (the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026). Overall, the experiences segment generated a whopping 28.3% operating margin for fiscal 2026 and contributed 56.7% of Disney's total operating income.

For fiscal 2027, Disney is forecasting another year of double-digit adjusted earnings-per-share growth, including 8% adjusted operating income growth.

NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

Disney is benefiting from an in-person experiences boom. In an era of rising screen time, folks are yearning for in-person connections with their families and others. And Disney's experiences drill into the core of that desire.

While the parks continue to be Disney's ultimate cash cow, its latest results were a reminder of just how vital Disney's other experiences have become -- namely its cruise business.

Sources indicate that the cruise industry is on fire. On its third-quarter fiscal 2026 earnings call, Carnival mentioned it is already half-booked for full-year 2027, even with occupancy and pricing at record levels. Royal Caribbean Cruises (RCL -2.20%) is coming off an exceptional summer sailing season.

Recent findings suggest that disney's multiyear ramp-up in its cruise fleet is paying off big-time. It launched two ships in the late 1990s and two more in the early 2010s before a decade-long pause. But since 2022, it has launched four ships -- doubling its fleet. The company plans to launch five more ships over the next five years -- bringing its total fleet to 13 ships. And on the Nov. 17 earnings call, CEO Josh D'Amaro said that Disney would add even more ships if it could get ones that met the company’s standards, given cruise ships are much more flexible than building land-based resorts.

In a recent development, disney has shifted more from a motion picture manufacturer to an experiences powerhouse -- realizing that experiences present a more attractive risk/reward profile than trying to smash a home run with a box-office hit (although it still relies on new content to drive fresh storytelling). Management is guiding for $9 billion in fiscal 2027 capital expenditures (capex) -- which is significant relative to its operating expenses. A lot of that is going to experiences, including building out the cruise fleet and some major park renovations.

It has been revealed that avengers Campus at Disney California Adventure Park is set to double in size in 2028. Tropical Americas is expected to come to Animal Kingdom as soon as next year, alongside a Monsters Inc.-themed land in Hollywood Studios. Construction is underway at a latest Cars-themed land and Disney Villains Land in Magic Kingdom. There's also a Spider-Man-themed land in the works at Shanghai Disneyland. And the grand prize is a new Disneyland in Abu Dhabi, which is expected to open between 2030 and 2033.

In sum, Disney's latest fiscal year and guidance validate that it is putting capex to good use on projects that will be embraced by guests and benefit its bottom line.

Since Josh D'Amaro took over as CEO earlier this year, a major theme has been returning capital to shareholders.

In Disney's third-quarter fiscal 2026 earnings report in August, the company noted it believes its shares are undervalued, which is why it accelerated stock buybacks. The move has proven correct so far, given Disney's recovering stock price. And despite Disney's massive fiscal 2027 capex forecast, it still expects to generate $11 billion in free cash flow and target $9 billion in stock buybacks.

The same day as its earnings release on Nov. 17, Disney declared a 33% dividend increase -- boosting the semiannual dividend from $0.75 per share to $1 per share for an annualized yield of 1.7%. It's worth noting that buybacks are still a much larger share of Disney's capital return program -- which leaves plenty of room for future dividend hikes.

Recent findings suggest that disney has a reasonable valuation -- even after its recent run-up. The stock trades at just 17.4 times adjusted fiscal 2026 earnings -- which is more than reasonable for an industry-leading entertainment giant growing earnings by double digits.

Disney has an unmatched intellectual property portfolio, vastly improved streaming profitability, ongoing cash flows from legacy linear networks, a resilient sports segment, and a high-margin experiences segment.

It has been revealed that add it all up, and Disney remains a balanced buy for value investors who believe consumers will continue to pay a premium for high-quality in-person experiences. The larger dividend provides an added incentive to hold the entertainment stock over the long term.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Samsung Electronics’ Digital City campus in Suwon, South Korea.
  • Samsung Electronics has named newly introduced heads for its memory chip and smartphone businesses.
  • In a recent development, sang Joon Hwang will run the memory business, and Won-Joon Choi takes over Mobile eXperience, the unit behind Galaxy phones, Samsung mentioned in a newsroom statement.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Samsung Electronics’ Digital City campus in Suwon, South Korea.

Samsung Electronics has named newly introduced heads for its memory chip and smartphone businesses. The changes came in a week when it reportedly paused some chip shipments to China under new US export rules. The tech giant unveiled the changes on Friday in Korea.

In a recent development, sang Joon Hwang will run the memory business, and Won-Joon Choi takes over Mobile eXperience, the unit behind Galaxy phones, Samsung mentioned in a newsroom statement. Co-chief executives Young Hyun Jun and TM Roh keep their roles.

It has been revealed that samsung promoted Hwang to president. He previously led memory development, including DRAM and the high-bandwidth memory (HBM) used in AI chips. Samsung said it expects him to strengthen its memory products for the AI era. It reportedly plans to make HBM parts for AMD and Nvidia at a second Texas fab.

Recent findings suggest that sangyeun Cho, who ran Samsung’s chip business in the Americas, becomes president of System LSI, its chip design unit. Jong Myeong Lee, the former head of process development, becomes chief technology officer of the Device Solutions division, which makes Samsung’s chips.

Sources indicate that choi has been chief operating officer of the mobile unit since March 2025 and led the releases of the Galaxy S26 and Galaxy Z Fold8. Roh had run the mobile business for most of the last seven years, 9to5Google noted. He stays in charge of the Device eXperience division, which includes phones and TVs.

It has been revealed that earlier this week, the Financial Times reported that Samsung and TSMC had suspended some shipments to Chinese customers. Both are applying for licences from the US Commerce Department under upcoming rules, the FT reported.

According to recent reports, the rules close a route that let Chinese designers order advanced chips through third-party packaging and testing firms. They also remove an exemption for chips not meant for AI, according to the FT. They arrived in the same week as US limits on Chinese remote access to AI chips in overseas data centres.

Samsung’s Chinese customers include ByteDance and Baidu’s chip unit Kunlun, while TSMC makes phone chips for Xiaomi, the FT reported. It is unclear which customers have been told to wait. An industry insider told the FT that Washington will likely approve licences for consumer smartphone chips. The process could still cause delays. TNW has not independently verified the report.

Chinese firms have already warned about the curbs. Tencent and Alibaba remarked this week the rules will slow growth in AI.

Some data centre operators that serve China have also been hit. Shares in Japan’s Datasection have fallen 47% since Monday, and it warned annual revenue could be up to 89% below its forecast, The Telegraph reported.

Industry observers note that samsung did not link its leadership changes to the export rules. Its statement says it wants the new team to strengthen its future competitiveness in semiconductors.

Breaking: Shopping for a massive-screen TV on Black Friday? Check these 5 things first

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that TV deals are one of the best parts of Black Friday, and if you’re vigilant, you’ve probably already noticed discounts starting to trickle in.
  • Sources indicate that but making a big purchase like a TV is also where a bad deal can cost you the most.
  • It has been revealed that so, let’s not spoil your Thanksgiving dinner, and make sure you get the best TV deal you can this Black Friday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that TV deals are one of the best parts of Black Friday, and if you’re vigilant, you’ve probably already noticed discounts starting to trickle in. If you’ve been eyeing a major-screen TV and waiting for your moment to strike, this is probably the best time of year to buy one.

Sources indicate that but making a big purchase like a TV is also where a bad deal can cost you the most. A huge discount can look great on paper, and it’s easy to miss the fine print when the low price tag grabs all your attention. You’ll save money now, but if you buy the wrong TV for you, you may find yourself annoyed months later when you realize you picked up a model with the wrong panel, weak gaming specs, or another personal deal-breaker.

It has been revealed that so, let’s not spoil your Thanksgiving dinner, and make sure you get the best TV deal you can this Black Friday. Before you add anything to your cart, here are five things I’d check first.

If you're looking for a TV that delivers fast action and flawless detail, the UR8 RGB MiniLED TV from Hisense creates natural color that's closer to real life. Its AI processor will adjust the picture in real time, balancing it without any manual setup, so sunsets look warm and skin tones look natural. The 180Hz motion processing reduces blur so you can clearly see what's going on, whether it's in a fast-moving action movie or the latest AAA video game.

When you start TV shopping, try not to get bogged down by the “was” price you’ll see in big, bold letters on the product page. Instead, treat it as context. The “was” price is usually just the TV’s launch MSRP, and plenty of TVs sell for well below it for most of their shelf lives. What matters most is the current price compared to what the TV cost in September and October of 2026, so pull up a price tracker before you pull the trigger. If the deal doesn’t beat its most recent price, it isn’t really a deal.

Industry observers note that older models are also where a lot of the deepest discounts hide. Retailers still have last year’s stock to clear, and we’ve even noted that 2025 TVs may be the safer buy this year considering recent tech price hikes. Double-check what you’d give up by going with an older version. Sometimes it’s something inconsequential like a tiny bit of brightness. Or, sometimes it’s something you really care about, like a faster refresh rate for gaming.

Industry observers note that consider where you’ll actually put the TV before you buy it, because the room will determine the panel you need. OLED is always my pick for a dark room. But if your living room gets a lot of natural light, brightness and glare resistance will matter more, and that’s where Mini-LED shines. It gets brighter, usually costs less per inch, and some models have screens built to fight reflections. The anti-glare screen on the Hisense U6SF Pro I reviewed stood out.

It has been revealed that there’s a middle lane, too. QLED TVs are usually the budget-friendly option, with bright, punchy color for less money. The tradeoff is that they typically have fewer dimming zones than a Mini-LED, so blacks can look a bit grayer when you turn the lights down.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

As an avid gamer, this is the part of the spec sheet I read first. Look for native 120Hz or 144Hz panels, variable refresh rate (VRR), and the number of HDMI 2.1 ports. A TV can say “4K at 144Hz” and still offer only two HDMI 2.1 ports. That’s totally fine if you have just one or two gaming consoles. But toss in another device and a soundbar, and you’ll run out of room fast. So, take stock of all your gear first to figure out the configuration you need. If you can get a TV with four HDMI 2.1 ports, that’s pretty much the best-case scenario.

It has been revealed that while you’re at it, check the TV’s OS, too, since you’ll be using it to navigate your content every day. There’s no wrong choice between Roku, Fire TV (Vega OS), and Google TV, but if you’d rather not relearn a remote, it’s worth knowing which one comes in the box. Personally, I like Roku TVs for their streamlined simplicity, but your mileage may vary.

According to recent reports, when it comes to TVs, the price tag is just the beginning. TV speakers are usually not great, and the bigger the screen is, the more you’ll notice. I’d plan on snagging one of the best soundbars with pretty much any set. Make sure there’s room for it, though, because some TVs sit pretty low, and a soundbar can end up blocking the bottom of the picture or the sensor. Also, please don’t forget to measure your space. Make sure to check the TV stand width against your media console (lots of big TVs have feet way out at the edges), the doorway, and the wall if you’re mounting it.

I’d also think twice about any extended warranty pitches at checkout. They aren’t always a bad idea, but check what the manufacturer’s warranty already includes first. While you’re at it, I’d also check the return window. Some retailers stretch theirs for the holidays, but some don’t, and January is a bad time to find that out.

Industry observers note that conventional wisdom states that TV prices bottom out around Black Friday and Cyber Monday, but this year comes with an asterisk. Chips and panels have both gotten pricier, and there aren’t many signs that will change anytime soon. That doesn’t mean prices won’t drop later this month, but it does mean the price floor might be a bit higher than you remember. So if a TV passes the first four checks and the price makes you happy, I’d buy it now. Holding out for another $100 off is how people end up missing out on the TV they really want.

My rule of thumb is to set a maximum price before I start scrolling, and set a price alert for the model(s) I want. It’ll keep the countdown timers and “only 3 left!” banners from making the final decision for you. Also, ask about the store’s price adjustment policy—some will refund the difference if the price drops within a set window.

In a recent development, if you end up missing the best deal, don’t panic. Cyber Monday is right after Black Friday, and TVs often go on sale well into December. The catch is that popular sizes of the best models tend to sell out first. Ultimately, the best Black Friday TV deal is the one that best fits your room and budget.

The sophomore season of “Presumed Innocent” is based on “Dissection of a Murder,” the debut legal thriller novel by Jo Murray, who also serves as a co-executive producer. Up-and-coming defense attorney Lelia Reynolds (Brosnahan) faces off against her district attorney husband (Rhys) in a murder case that threatens to destroy both their careers and their marriage.

Apple has started making a habit of renewing indicates that were originally intended as limited series.

Etsy will revise its AI training terms after sellers close their shops

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that the newly introduced terms take effect on 16 December.
  • Etsy and its “third party partners and vendors” may use sellers’ content to “develop, train, test and improve artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies.”.
  • Several sellers who had run shops for years stated they were leaving.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the newly introduced terms take effect on 16 December. They let Etsy and its partners use sellers’ content to build and train AI. The previous version had no clause about AI, the Times reported. The key line reads:.

Etsy and its “third party partners and vendors” may use sellers’ content to “develop, train, test and improve artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies.”.

Several sellers who had run shops for years stated they were leaving. Illustrator Aaron Millard said on Instagram he was deleting the shop he had run for nearly a decade. He wrote that sellers had no way to opt out.

It has been revealed that kristen and Geoff Zephyrus deleted their shop too. They have sold home goods and stationery on Etsy for 13 years as Cognitive Surplus.

“For Etsy to be helping to train algorithms with our human content is just unimaginably awful,” Kristen Zephyrus told the Times.

James Ossman, Etsy’s vice president for customer operations, answered sellers in a post on Etsy’s website this week.

Etsy will not “use your content to train A.I. models designed to copy your original work or replace your creativity,” Ossman wrote.

In a recent development, he noted third parties get access to sellers’ content for uses such as fraud detection and advertising. In a statement to the Times, he said Etsy would send sellers the revised terms soon. Sellers’ creative work belongs to them, he added.

It has been revealed that some critics doubt the reassurance. Tyler Wilde, PC Gamer’s US editor-in-chief, wrote an opinion piece on the clause. To him, it reads like blanket permission to train AI on user content for any purpose. He argued that Etsy should leave every seller out of AI training by default.

Etsy has faced seller protests before. In 2022, more than 20,000 sellers went on strike over a fee rise. Etsy had raised its basic sales fee from 5% to 6.5%. In October, it tightened its rules on low-quality AI content after users complained, the Times reported.

In a recent development, the firm cut 12% of its staff in August. The dispute also lands amid wider pushback against AI. Donald Trump Jr told Axios this week that investors had underestimated the AI backlash. Elton John urged Australia to protect artists from AI at the Aria awards.

Apple’s ‘just works’ approach is great, but goes a little too far

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (954 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • “It just works” is one of the phrases most commonly associated with Apple.
  • Of course, it’s now commonly used ironically when Apple products don’t do what they are supposed to (Apple Home, I’m looking at you), but I do think that it’s absolutely the right philosophy and goal – most of the time ….
  • Recent findings suggest that macworld referenced an Apple brochure from 1996 entitled “Why do people prefer Macintosh?” This is a collection of testimonials from customers, a number of whom use the “it just works” phrasing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

“It just works” is one of the phrases most commonly associated with Apple. Interestingly, it appears to have been coined by the manufacturer’s customers and then used by reviewers before it was later picked up by Steve Jobs.

Of course, it’s now commonly used ironically when Apple products don’t do what they are supposed to (Apple Home, I’m looking at you), but I do think that it’s absolutely the right philosophy and goal – most of the time ….

Recent findings suggest that macworld referenced an Apple brochure from 1996 entitled “Why do people prefer Macintosh?” This is a collection of testimonials from customers, a number of whom use the “it just works” phrasing. It was subsequently used by a number of reviewers. The earliest example I can find of Steve Jobs adopting it was in 1999, when discussing the rollout of FireWire to the Mac in the PowerMac G3.

Industry observers note that it’s hot-pluggable. You don’t have to turn your computer off to connect and disconnect peripherals, you can just plug them right in. Again, the drivers are dynamically loaded. There are no terminators and there are no switches. It just works.

(If you have a link to any earlier example, please do let me know in the comments.).

I’m a big fan of the philosophy. Most of the time, users should just be able to get on with the tasks they want to execute without having to worry about the technology. The tech that makes it all possible should sit there quietly in the background.

However, there are cases where I think Apple takes this approach a little too far, and where tech-savvy owners at least would like a little more transparency and control.

It has been revealed that airPods firmware updates are a good example. Back in September, there was quite a significant update in the form of custom EQ. It’s a rather basic version, but still a feature many had wanted for a long time. Instead of being able to manually trigger the update, owners had to wait until it “just worked.”.

Apple’s support document has a how-to guide that is essentially an outline of the conditions required to permit an patch, and an instruction to simply wait until it happens. Which you will only know by repeatedly checking.

Make sure your AirPods are connected via Bluetooth to your iPhone, iPad or Mac. Connect your charging case to a power source. Put your AirPods in their charging case and close the lid. Keep the lid of the charging case closed, and keep your AirPods in Bluetooth range of your iPhone, iPad or Mac. Wait at least 30 minutes for the firmware to be updated. Check the firmware version again.

In a recent development, another example, and one I’ve complained about before, is that there is no way to manually trigger an iCloud document sync, nor any progress indicator when it does finally happen. In the best of cases, it takes seconds; in the worst, many hours. And again, the only way to find out is to repeatedly check.

It has been revealed that it’s the same story when shooting a video on your iPhone. Will it still be there an hour later, available to instantly edit and view? Maybe, or maybe it will have been offloaded to the cloud, requiring it to be downloaded before you can do anything with it – while a video you shot months earlier is still stored locally on the device! You can, of course, switch off optimization altogether, but if you choose to use it, you get no control over it. I want a setting that allows me to do things like specify local retention of all photos and videos taken within the past fortnight.

According to recent reports, will that video be available in the Mac Photos app when you check half an hour later? Maybe, maybe not. You can click the Sync Now button as many times as you like, and it will apparently have no effect, claiming it’s up to date despite the video being entirely absent. It will be there when it’s there.

In a recent development, once it is in the Photos app on your Mac, it’s a similar story when exporting it to a folder. You can drag and drop the video into the folder, and this time you are manually triggering the transfer (yay!), but there will be absolutely no visual indication that it is in progress. No grayed-out icon, no progress bar, nothing. So far as the user interface is concerned, it appears that your drag and drop had no effect – until the video file finally appears.

According to recent reports, I think with all of these things and more, Apple needs to offer options. Yes, most non-tech users may be perfectly happy to just wait until things happen, but there ought to be a standard way to trigger things that currently happen in their own sweet time, as well as progress indicators and confirmation that a process is complete.

Sources indicate that is this an ecosystem-wide improvement you’d like to see? Please share your thoughts in the comments and add any frustrating examples of your own.

SK Hynix will become Kioxia’s largest shareholder through a bond swap

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (461 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Thenextweb

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • SK hynix’s exhibition booth at the Supercomputing 2026 (SC26) conference.
  • SK Hynix will become the largest shareholder in Kioxia, its Japanese rival in flash memory, by converting bonds it has held since 2018 into shares.
  • Recent findings suggest that bloomberg’s Yoolim Lee first reported the filing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

SK hynix’s exhibition booth at the Supercomputing 2026 (SC26) conference.

SK Hynix will become the largest shareholder in Kioxia, its Japanese rival in flash memory, by converting bonds it has held since 2018 into shares. It will hold an indirect stake of about 14.1%, it stated in a filing on Friday.

Recent findings suggest that bloomberg’s Yoolim Lee first reported the filing. The move puts SK Hynix ahead of Toshiba, Kioxia’s former parent, which held 10.46% in early November, according to Korea JoongAng Daily.

SPC2 is a special-purpose company set up for the 2018 deal. SK Hynix will convert 129bn yen ($810m) of its bonds into 129,000 shares. It will also buy Bain Capital’s remaining 1,001 SPC2 shares for 100m yen. The steps close in December, leaving SK Hynix as SPC2’s sole owner.

According to recent reports, apart from the payment to Bain, the deal adds no new money, MoneyToday reported, citing the firm. SK Hynix called it a follow-up step after it sold out of a separate Kioxia fund in June. Gains from that sale funded about 7tn won ($5.2bn) of special dividends in the third quarter.

Recent findings suggest that SK Hynix joined the Bain-led group that bought Kioxia, then Toshiba Memory, in 2018. It put in 395bn yen at the time.

It has been revealed that both companies make NAND, the chips used for storage in phones and AI servers. SK Hynix held 19% of the global NAND market in the second quarter and Kioxia 14%, according to Counterpoint figures cited by Bloomberg. Together that tops market leader Samsung’s 28%.

The 2018 deal caps SK Hynix at 15% of Kioxia’s voting shares until 2028, unless Kioxia agrees otherwise. Kioxia lists the stake as a risk factor in its annual report, citing a possible conflict of interest, Bloomberg reported.

Both sides say nothing changes in how Kioxia is run. A Kioxia spokesperson said its management will stay independent.

“We right now have no prepares to further buy or sell shares in Kioxia. We will continue to respect Kioxia’s independent management going forward,” an SK Hynix official stated.

Masahiro Wakasugi of Bloomberg Intelligence sees little change in the short run.

The move is “unlikely to materially change near-term NAND competition,” Wakasugi wrote.

The stake still gives SK Hynix some say over massive decisions, he added. That includes the power to oppose a possible deal between Kioxia and Sandisk.

Separately, SoftBank’s Masayoshi Son reportedly explored a buyout of SK Hynix itself. The Korean manufacturer reported a 632% profit jump in October, even as memory stocks slid.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that if you're building a portfolio from scratch with $10,000, there are some must-haves.
  • Industry observers note that you'd certainly want some more aggressive growth stocks or ETFs to provide long-term alpha.
  • One value stock that would serve that role is McDonald's (MCD +0.33%).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Dave Kovaleski – Nov 22, 2026 at 8:00AM EST.

10 stocks we like better than McDonald's ›.

Industry observers note that if you're building a portfolio from scratch with $10,000, there are some must-haves. You'd probably want broad market and large-cap exchange-traded funds (ETFs) as core holdings.

Industry observers note that you'd certainly want some more aggressive growth stocks or ETFs to provide long-term alpha. And you would definitely want stocks or an ETF to provide some ballast when the broader markets or growth stocks are down.

One value stock that would serve that role is McDonald's (MCD +0.33%).

In a recent development, mcDonald's is one of the largest fast food restaurant chains in the world and has been for a long time. It has also been one of the best defensive stocks on the market, buoyed by its consistent earnings in most markets and its excellent dividend.

Sources indicate that the proof is in the performance. If you go back 25 years, encompassing the dot-com bear market, the global financial crisis, and everything since, McDonald's stock, on a total return basis, has an average annualized return of 12.4%. As the chart demonstrates, that beats the S&P 500 and other top consumer stocks, like Walmart (WMT +1.51%), Coca-Cola (KO +0.94%), Target (TGT -0.97%), Proctor & Gamble (PG +0.91%), and PepsiCo (PEP +1.11%).

WMT Total Return Level data by YCharts.

But when you drill down a bit further, you see that during most bear markets and downturns since then, McDonald's stock has not only beaten the benchmarks but had positive returns in some of the worst downturns.

NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

Recent findings suggest that for example, in 2008, when the S&P 500 was down 37%, McDonald's stock was up 9% for the year. In 2018, when the S&P 500 dropped 4%, McDonald's stock rose 6%. And in 2022, when the S&P 500 dropped 18%, McDonald's stock rose 1%.

So, it has the long-term performance that beats the benchmark, but more importantly, it performs well when the market doesn't. That is an notable quality to have in your portfolio, as it helps smooth out overall returns during bouts of volatility or negative market sentiment.

McDonald's consistency is why it has been able to raise its dividend for the past 50 years in a row, making it a Dividend King, which is any company that has raised its annual dividend for at least 50 consecutive years. McDonald's at the moment pays out a high yield of 2.80% with a very manageable 49% payout ratio, so it is in a good financial position to keep boosting its dividend.

McDonald's is also in the beginning stages of a multi-year turnaround initiative called NEXT, which management hopes will set the brand on a course for growth over the next decade. The NEXT plan aims to gain 1.5% market share in both the chicken and beverage categories, increase sales, raise the operating margin to the low- to mid-50% range, make restaurants more efficient, and have free-cash-flow conversion in the mid-to-high 80% range, among other goals, all by 2030.

It seeks to do this by improving the menu options and prices, capitalizing on the brand, modernizing restaurants and operations to make them more productive, and invest in people to improve the customer experience.

Industry observers note that there are myriad challenges facing McDonald's including diet changes, competition, and the economy, but it has been able to anticipate changes in the past to maintain its market share. The newly introduced plan should allow McDonald's to maintain its leadership as a low-cost option for consumers.

That is why investors looking for a good value stock to balance out their portfolio should consider McDonald's.

Sources indicate that I’ve used Apple’s Calendar app for years, and there’s an elegant simplicity to it. But one key area the app has long lagged behind competitors is event creation.

When you need to create a newly introduced event, the Calendar app historically has required manually filling in various fields for the title, date, time, invitees, etc. By contrast, the excellent third-party app Fantastical lets you type in natural language and it automatically fills in relevant parameters based on what you type.

Recent findings suggest that in iOS 27, Apple finally introduces its own natural language input for Calendar events. You can type out your event details and certain recognized parameters will be used to automatically fill in the detail fields.

While the feature still isn’t on par with what Fantastical offers, since it doesn’t support as many data points as the third-party alternative, it’s very much a step in the right direction.

Apple has always pitched Siri as being like a personal assistant. As such, calendar-related tasks should have been Siri’s strong suit. But until iOS 27, you couldn’t actually manage your calendar very well using Siri.

Industry observers note that one of my favorite personal examples is from this summer when the NFL schedule was released. I asked Siri to find the Dallas Cowboys schedule and add every game to my calendar, and it pulled this off with ease.

Siri is so much better than before at assisting with your calendar, and iOS 27.3 will bring even more capabilities soon.

Tech Report: OpenAI indicates its agents now finish nearly half of 2 to 4-hour research tasks

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (705 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thenextweb

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that openAI says its coding agents now complete 46% of research tasks that would take a person two to four hours, with no human help.
  • Sources indicate that the figures come from Research acceleration: The jagged frontier, a report OpenAI published on Wednesday.
  • At API list prices, the median OpenAI researcher used about $2,400 of agent time a day in October.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that openAI says its coding agents now complete 46% of research tasks that would take a person two to four hours, with no human help. In March the figure was 23%. For tasks of four to eight hours, success rose from 13% to 35%.

Sources indicate that the figures come from Research acceleration: The jagged frontier, a report OpenAI published on Wednesday. It is the firm’s second on how AI speeds up its own research, after its first such report in September. OpenAI states labs should be required to track and publicly report signs of recursive self-improvement, where AI speeds up the building of future AI. It adds that the reporting does not mean it intends to pursue full self-improvement.

At API list prices, the median OpenAI researcher used about $2,400 of agent time a day in October. That is up 62% from $1,500 in September. At the 90th percentile, daily use reached about $23,000, more than double September’s $11,000.

Measured in time, agent use per researcher rose elevenfold, from 0.5 to 5.7 “agent workdays” a day. OpenAI counts every eight hours of agent running time as one workday. By mid-October, more than two-thirds of researchers ran at least four agents at once at their daily peak. More than 10% ran at least 16.

In September, the value of agent use in OpenAI’s research organisation was about twice its pay bill for researchers. That excludes equity, which OpenAI says makes up 70 to 80% of their target pay. Internal use still took only 2% of research compute.

Results for OpenAI research agents vary widely by task, which is why the tech giant calls the gains jagged. Agents succeeded alone 79% of the time when monitoring training runs, and 72% when answering technical questions. They managed 25% when writing code for inference and serving systems, and 29% when building evaluation and training environments.

It has been revealed that openAI flags a caveat in its own numbers. As agents improved, researchers may have changed which tasks they handed over, so the success rates track those choices as well as the models.

It has been revealed that in a survey of 101 research staff, OpenAI asked what each would give up to keep frontier coding agents for three months. The median answer was 40% of team headcount, or 30% of team compute. The tech giant warns that self-reports may be inaccurate and that it sampled staff in an ad hoc way.

OpenAI also asked key researchers where the main ideas behind GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.2 Astra came from. Post-training and safety researchers credited people with all of them, with models helping to build them. For GPT-6.2 Astra, pretraining researchers said they developed ideas in conversation with Codex, and one credited it with key insights.

In interviews, researchers said agents still have poor taste in research ideas, code, data and writing, and need close oversight. One pretraining researcher doubted the human edge would last.

Industry observers note that “I do think I have more taste in terms of the ideas. But I have no confidence that will continue to be true for any significant period of time,” the researcher told OpenAI.

Safety and Alignment saw the largest rise in researcher time of any area, OpenAI says, with documented workweeks up 77% from January to September. Growth picked up after the Hugging Face breakout in July, when its own research agents hacked the AI platform.

In a recent development, openAI is not alone in publishing such data. It cites three reports from Anthropic, which says it has met its own threshold for AI-accelerated research. The same day, OpenAI said its models had found gains in AMD’s GPU design.

In a recent development, to see whether AI is speeding up progress itself, OpenAI tracks an internal version of Epoch AI’s capabilities index. Its frontier has risen 16.4 points a year since August 2025, against the 14 a year Epoch found since late 2024. OpenAI notes that its models score higher on its own index than on Epoch’s.

In this post we will take a first look at RPython because it is the kind of VM implementor’s programming language that I keep thinking about. More on that later.

Before we continue, please heed this warning: RPython is an implementation detail of PyPy. It has not had the years of polish that the rest of the system has had. Please do not badger maintainers.

We’re going to build a little program in RPython. I am mostly following along with the docs, specifically Getting Started with RPython.

This is the RPython compilation process. In it, RPython is analyzing types, removing memory allocations, monomorphizing functions, and generating C code. Then it hands this C code off to a C compiler to compile.

In a recent development, you should have in your current directory an executable named double-c, which you can run like ./double-c. It should also print 6.

Recent findings suggest that so far, this is not so different from Python. But let’s try something Pythonic. Let’s see what happens when we also use + to mean string concatenation.

In a recent development, under normal Python 2, this will work just fine, printing aa and then 6. Under RPython, though, you get this inscrutable error (again, rough edges):.

and are unceremoniously dropped into the debugger, Pdb (hit Ctrl-D or type exit).

From this message you are meant to intuit that RPython did not enjoy that two different types flowed into the double function. It helpfully tells you that there was a UnionError when trying to reconcile the SomeChar and SomeInteger types that flowed into the function’s first parameter. It then gives you a pointer to the offending line and an IR dump.

This happens because RPython requires function parameters to be monomorphic. Though the variables are syntactically untyped, RPython computes a type analysis to discover what type each variable should be. When "a" and 3 both flow into x, boom, complaint.2.

Industry observers note that to get around this, we do what all good C++ programmers do and we templatize the function. The RPython spelling of this is, as with many other features, a function annotation:.

You will find now that RPython happily compiles the program. This works because it makes a upcoming copy of double for every input type of the first (0) argument.

“Hey wait a minute,”, you might ask, “doesn’t this mean it stops being a valid Python 2 program?”.

In a recent development, this runs ~instantly, which is a major relief. Developing an interpreter project with a 30 second or more turnaround time for each compile would be really frustrating.

This has been a taste of RPython, both great and somewhat frustrating. I intentionally made it about RPython as a programming language rather than being so focused on RPython as a programming language implementation tool because I want some of its features to exist in a general purpose programming language… that then also might be used to implement other programming languages.

10 stocks we like better than Johnson & Johnson ›.
